studies.title: Anhedonia modulates the effects of positive mood induction on reward-related brain activation.
studies.abstract: Blunted activation in the reward circuitry has been associated with anhedonia, the inability to experience pleasure in previously rewarding activities. In healthy individuals, reward-related activation has been found to be modulated by acute contextual factors such as induced positive mood. Accordingly, blunted reward response in anhedonia might involve a failure to appropriately modulate reward-related activation as a function of context. To test this hypothesis, 29 participants (19 females, mean age of 24.14 ± 4.61, age range 18-34), with a wide range of anhedonic symptoms, underwent functional MRI while anticipating and receiving monetary rewards, before and after a positive mood induction. Change in neural activation from before to after mood induction was quantified, and effects of anhedonia were investigated through whole-brain, ROI, and functional connectivity analyses. Contrary to hypotheses, results indicated that during reward anticipation (but not receipt), nucleus accumbens activation decreased while its connectivity with the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex increased, following positive mood induction. Critically, anhedonia modulated both effects. The unexpected finding of decreased activation to reward cues following positive mood induction is compelling as it aligns with a prominent behavioral model of the effect of positive mood on exploration of rewarding and neutral stimuli. Furthermore, the modulation of this effect by anhedonia suggests that it may be a key process altered in anhedonia.

studies.title: Brain responses and approach bias to social alcohol cues and their association with drinking in a social setting in young adult males.
studies.abstract: Alcohol is mainly consumed in social settings, in which people often adapt their drinking behaviour to that of others, also called imitation of drinking. Yet, it remains unclear what drives this drinking in a social setting. In this study, we expected to see stronger brain and behavioural responses to social compared to non-social alcohol cues, and these responses to be associated with drinking in a social setting. The sample consisted of 153 beer-drinking males, aged 18-25 years. Brain responses to social alcohol cues were measured during an alcohol cue-exposure task performed in an fMRI scanner. Behavioural responses to social alcohol cues were measured using a stimulus-response compatibility task, providing an index of approach bias towards these cues. Drinking in a social setting was measured in a laboratory mimicking a bar environment. Specific brain responses to social alcohol cues were observed in the bilateral superior temporal sulcus and the left inferior parietal lobe. There was no approach bias towards social alcohol cues specifically; however, we did find an approach bias towards alcohol (versus soda) cues in general. Brain responses and approach bias towards social alcohol cues were unrelated and not associated with actual drinking. Thus, we found no support for a relation between drinking in a social setting on the one hand, and brain cue-reactivity or behavioural approach biases to social alcohol cues on the other hand. This suggests that, in contrast to our hypothesis, drinking in a social setting may not be driven by brain or behavioural responses to social alcohol cues.

studies.title: Neurocognitive and Hormonal Correlates of Voluntary Weight Loss in Humans.
studies.abstract: Insufficient responses to hypocaloric diets have been attributed to hormonal adaptations that override self-control of food intake. We tested this hypothesis by measuring circulating energy-balance hormones and brain functional magnetic resonance imaging reactivity to food cues in 24 overweight/obese participants before, and 1 and 3 months after starting a calorie restriction diet. Increased activity and functional connectivity in prefrontal regions at month 1 correlated with weight loss at months 1 and 3. Weight loss was also correlated with increased plasma ghrelin and decreased leptin, and these changes were associated with food cue reactivity in reward-related brain regions. However, the reduction in leptin did not counteract weight loss; indeed, it was correlated with further weight loss at month 3. Activation in prefrontal regions associated with self-control could contribute to successful weight loss and maintenance. This work supports the role of higher-level cognitive brain function in body-weight regulation in humans.

studies.title: Genetic risk for obesity predicts nucleus accumbens size and responsivity to real-world food cues.
studies.abstract: Obesity is a major public health concern that involves an interaction between genetic susceptibility and exposure to environmental cues (e.g., food marketing); however, the mechanisms that link these factors and contribute to unhealthy eating are unclear. Using a well-known obesity risk polymorphism (FTO rs9939609) in a sample of 78 children (ages 9-12 y), we observed that children at risk for obesity exhibited stronger responses to food commercials in the nucleus accumbens (NAcc) than children not at risk. Similarly, children at a higher genetic risk for obesity demonstrated larger NAcc volumes. Although a recessive model of this polymorphism best predicted body mass and adiposity, a dominant model was most predictive of NAcc size and responsivity to food cues. These findings suggest that children genetically at risk for obesity are predisposed to represent reward signals more strongly, which, in turn, may contribute to unhealthy eating behaviors later in life.

studies.title: Real-time imaging of cortical areas involved in the generation of increases in skin sympathetic nerve activity when viewing emotionally charged images.
studies.abstract: The sympathetic innervation of the skin not only primarily subserves thermoregulation, but has also been commandeered as a means of emotional expression. While the majority of brain imaging studies of emotion have utilised the galvanic skin response as a means of inferring changes in skin sympathetic nerve activity (SSNA), spontaneous fluctuations in the galvanic skin response bear little relation to spontaneous fluctuations in SSNA. To improve our understanding of the central neural processes involved in the generation of autonomic emotional markers, we recorded SSNA concurrently with brain functional magnetic resonance imaging in 13 subjects. Emotional changes were evoked by presentation of positively-charged (erotica) or negatively-charged (mutilation) images from the International Affective Picture System. Positive and negative emotionally-charged images evoked significant increases in total SSNA and signal intensity in the orbital, dorsolateral and ventromedial prefrontal cortices, amygdala, nucleus accumbens and anterior insula. Increases in signal intensity during increases in SSNA occurred in a number of brain regions, including the central and lateral amygdala, dorsolateral pons, thalamus, nucleus accumbens, and cerebellar cortex. Signal intensity decreases during SSNA increases occurred in the left orbitofrontal, frontal and right precuneus cortices. These data reveal for the first time, cortical and subcortical sites involved in generating SSNA changes during emotions.

studies.title: Valence, Not Utility, Underlies Reward-Driven Prioritization in Human Vision.
studies.abstract: Objects associated with reward draw attention and evoke enhanced activity in visual cortex. What is the underlying mechanism? One possibility is that reward's impact on vision is mediated by unique circuitry that modulates sensory processing, selectively increasing the salience of reward-associated stimuli. Alternatively, effects of reward may be part of a more general mechanism that prioritizes the processing of any beneficial object, importantly including stimuli that are associated with the evasion of loss. Here, we test these competing hypotheses by having male and female humans detect naturalistic objects associated with monetary reward, the evasion of equivalent loss, or neither of these. If vision is economically normative, processing of objects associated with reward and evasion of loss should be prioritized relative to neutral stimuli. Results from fMRI and behavioral experiments show that this is not the case: whereas objects associated with reward were better detected and represented in ventral visual cortex, detection and representation of stimuli associated with the evasion of loss were degraded. Representations in parietal cortex reveal a notable exception to this pattern, showing enhanced encoding of both reward- and loss-associated stimuli. Experience-driven visual prioritization can thus be economically irrational, driven by valence rather than objective utility.

fulltext_screening_results.reason: This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: (I3) the fMRI task is a multimodal alcohol taste cue paradigm that includes clear visual cues (the words “Alcohol” vs “Water” preceding taste delivery); (I4) analyses include a within-participant contrast Alcohol > Water; (I5) the manuscript reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain activation clusters referenced for ACC and thalamus for the Alcohol > Water contrast, with image acquisition and preprocessing details indicated in Supplementary Materials); (I6) voxelwise results are available/indicated in the main text and supplementary materials; (I7) participant demographics, cue type, preprocessing and software (e.g., FSL FLIRT, MATLAB/Psychtoolbox) and acquisition parameters are reported or referenced in Supplementary Materials. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary material referenced).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cocaine vs neutral pictures (visual cues) in 23 cocaine-dependent participants. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of cocaine>neutral at the first level and group-level voxelwise second-level analyses with whole-brain, familywise-error-corrected results (tables/figures of coordinates and clusters provided). Methods include scanner field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM8), and participant demographics. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

Although this fMRI study uses visual alcohol cues (alcohol and food images) and reports task-evoked voxelwise results (e.g., regulation contrasts and parametric covariation of brain activity with craving, with small-volume correction for VS/vmPFC), the paper does not report a within-participant voxelwise contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., alcohol > neutral/food) at the group level. Inclusion criterion I4 (explicit within-participant drug-cue > control contrast) is not met based on the full text provided. Therefore the study cannot be included for a meta-analysis specifically targeting cue-reactivity contrasts, despite meeting other criteria (I3, I5, I6, I7).

This is an fMRI study using visual cannabis cues in adolescent cannabis users with a within-participant cannabis > non-cannabis contrast. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected results (z thresholds and corrected p-values reported) and presents activation clusters (tables/figures/supplementary figures). Participant demographics, cue type (active/passive), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT, FLAME) are reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening.

This empirical fMRI study used visual cocaine cue pictures and a within-subject contrast of cocaine > neutral cues. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported: whole-brain one-sample t-test results and a small-volume-corrected PAG result (SVC) are presented. Methods report participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (visual cocaine pictures), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Results are reported in the main text and supplementary material. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (palatable food pictures vs. scrambled controls). It includes a within-participant contrast of food>control and reports group-level voxelwise GLM results with small-volume FWE-corrected ROI analyses (right amygdala effect reported, p_FWE=.006). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), stimuli, preprocessing, and SPM5 analysis are described. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrast, and qualifying voxelwise (small-volume-corrected) results. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (palatable food photographs) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food>non-food. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, P<.05 using FLAME1), and participant age/sex, cue type, field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are described. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food and non-food pictures). It includes within-participant contrasts comparing food>non-food (parametric and categorical analyses) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with family-wise-error (FWE) correction and small-volume corrections in a priori ROIs (NAc, VTA). Core methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM12) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This article reports an empirical human fMRI study using a visual alcohol cue reactivity task and reports within-subject contrasts (Alcohol > Control) at the first level and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster FWE-corrected results with MNI coordinates). Methods include MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), and participant demographics. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual drug-cue fMRI), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results reported), I6 (results reported in main text/figures/tables), and I7 (key methodological/participant details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of tobacco cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (craving and aversive smoking-related images) in smokers and non-smokers. It includes within-participant contrasts of craving>control and aversion>control (Cr vs mosaic, Av vs mosaic). Group-level voxelwise random-effects GLM results are reported (FDR-corrected maps and region coordinates/BA descriptions), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Methods report participant sex/age group (male), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (Brain Voyager, GLM/RFX), meeting reporting preferences. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject cue>control, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies.

This task-based fMRI study used visually presented word cues (alcohol- and cannabis-related words) in an addiction-Stroop task, including within-participant contrasts of alcohol>neutral (color) and cannabis>neutral. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed with SPM8 and cluster-level correction (3dClustSim) and report significant clusters and correlations, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, first- and second-level analyses), results, and discussion; key details (participant demographics, cue type, 3T field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and whole-brain corrected voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or lack of within-participant contrasts) apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related and neutral images (visual cue component) in heroin-dependent patients and controls. It includes within-participant contrasts (BOLD_drugcues > BOLD_neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results: whole-brain analyses and OFC small-volume-corrected results (FWE-corrected cluster thresholds) with tables/figures of significant clusters. Methods and results (including preprocessing, scanner, statistical software SPM8, MRI field strength implied by 3T scanner) are fully reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes the required within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a visual cue-based monetary reward anticipation task (arrow cues) and reports within-participant contrasts (anticipation of monetary reward > anticipation of verbal feedback). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain analyses with coordinates and ROI-corrected VS results), and necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets the review objective of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-subject Smoking>Neutral contrasts and conducts group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FLAME) with cluster-level correction (z=3.1, Pcorrected<.05), and presents results in tables/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (visual smoking and matched neutral images), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is original human fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI task study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie vs low-calorie images). It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie) at the group level, reports voxelwise results including small-volume-corrected coordinates for the basolateral amygdala, and provides sufficient methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI, SPM12/MATLAB preprocessing). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the review objectives and inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI task study of natural (monetary) reward-related cue-reactivity using explicit visual cues (shapes on the MID and visual faces in the probabilistic reward task). It reports within-subject contrasts of reward-cue>neutral (Reward Cue–Neutral Cue) and loss-cue>neutral (Loss Cue–Neutral Cue). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction are reported, and small-volume/ROI analyses were also performed; results are presented in tables/figures. Participant demographics, MRI acquisition, and preprocessing/statistics are described. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This full-text reports an fMRI task exposing participants to visual marketing clips (alcohol, cannabis, neutral) and includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol marketing > neutral; cannabis marketing > neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (with significant clusters and cluster-level FWE correction) and ROI/SVC analyses in striatum are described. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM8 statistical software, and participant demographics. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results), I6 (results reported in main text/tables/figures), and I7 (reports age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistics). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity but the cue modality is gustatory (taste: alcohol vs juice) rather than visual. The review's inclusion criterion I3 requires a clear visual cue component (visual-only or multimodal that includes visual cues); this study does not include visual cues and therefore fails I3. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant alcohol>juice contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise/whole-brain voxel results presented as spatial component maps and Talairach labels), I6 (voxelwise results available in main text/figures/tables), I7 (reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text is complete. Exclusion is therefore based on failure to meet I3 (no visual cue component).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual picture cues (cocaine and food) with within-participant contrasts (cocaine>neutral; food>neutral). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain cluster-level FWE correction and small-volume correction for the hypothalamus; coordinates and cluster statistics are described in the text/figures. Participant demographics and analysis software (SPM) are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for visual cue reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and voxelwise whole-brain/small-volume-corrected results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This fMRI study uses visual smoking cues and reports a within-participant smoking>neutral contrast, and provides participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details. However, the task results are reported as extracted beta weights from a priori ROIs (insula and ACC) rather than as group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore it fails the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), I7 (reporting of participant sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task result), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (factorial 2×2 medication × time, with cluster-level inference and tables/figures of results and supplementary tables), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/SPM12), participant demographics (male, age range), and cue type, meeting reporting preferences. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli in adolescent smokers. It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral cues, presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (significant activations reported at p<.001 with cluster threshold) and a-priori ROI analyses, and provides participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

This fMRI study of opioid-dependent individuals used visual drug-cue videos (10-min heroin video) and computed within-participant drug-cue minus neutral-session contrasts, and reports participant demographics and MRI details. However, the reported analyses are ROI-based (sphere extractions and ROI ANOVAs) and no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results (e.g., SPM second-level voxelwise contrasts or corrected coordinate tables) are presented in the main text. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast), I7 (reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistics). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group result reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This article is an empirical fMRI study that directly assesses cocaine (drug) cue-reactivity using videotaped visual cues and provides within-participant task contrasts and group-level voxelwise results. The methods describe visual-only/multimodal videotape cues, within-subject contrasts (e.g., emotion0 vs baseline1, emotion1 vs emotion0, emotion2 vs baseline2), and group-level randomization/voxelwise statistical maps with reported p values and figures/tables of regional activations. Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM96) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, figures, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for task-evoked voxelwise analyses of drug-related visual cues and should be included.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study using visual cue videos (cocaine, gambling, sad) that elicited cue-specific cravings/urges. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing video epochs to baseline (V1>B1, V2>B2) and reports group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (3×2×3 ANOVAs) with whole-brain family-wise-error correction (Monte Carlo simulation). Neuroimaging results are presented in tables and figures (Table 2, Figures, Supplementary Figures), satisfying reporting requirements. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objectives and inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise corrected results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This article is a narrative/interpretive synthesis of a series of prior ERP and fMRI studies rather than an original empirical fMRI report. It does not present new group-level voxelwise task-evoked fMRI results, coordinate tables, or details of a within-participant drug-cue>control contrast as a primary empirical analysis. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper / review without original human fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (paper itself is not an original fMRI study reporting its own visual cue-reactivity dataset), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast results presented for an original fMRI experiment), I5/I6 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results or coordinates reported in this article). Full text appears complete for a review article (intro, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Exclusion E4 met: the study reports only seed-based/effective connectivity analyses (PPI and Granger causality) and does not report a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise activation contrast (drug cue > control) at the group level. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI cannabis cue-reactivity with a visual component — the task was multimodal including visual presentation of cues) and I4 (within-subject cannabis cue ON vs. neutral cue ON contrasts were used in PPI). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result for cue>control activation is reported; the reported voxelwise results are connectivity (PPI) maps rather than standard task-evoked activation contrasts). Therefore excluded under E4.

Primary reason for exclusion: the study does not include a visual cue component (I3 not met). It used personalized guided-imagery audiotaped scripts (auditory imagery) for stress, favorite-food, and neutral/relaxing cues rather than visual-only or multimodal designs that include visual stimuli. The study does meet I4 (within-participant contrasts of favorite-food vs neutral and stress vs neutral were performed) and I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and cluster thresholds) and I6 (results reported in main text and supplemental tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I3 (visual cue component).

Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only ROI-based analyses with no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is fMRI of drug cue-reactivity with clear visual smoking-related picture cues), I4 (within-participant smoke>rest contrasts and PSC (smoke–rest) analyses are reported), I7 (participant age range/sex stratification, cue type, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/TBV) are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported in the manuscript), I6 (not applicable because no qualifying voxelwise results are provided in text, tables, or figures). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded for the meta-analysis because it provides only ROI-based task results and lacks the required group-level voxelwise statistical maps or small-volume-corrected results (E3).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual film cues (cocaine, sex, nature) to evoke cue-induced craving in cocaine users. It includes within-participant contrasts (cocaine film vs nature film) and group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample and two-sample t tests, voxel-wise threshold p=0.0025 with cluster extent), with results reported as activation clusters/tables and figures. The manuscript reports participant demographics (age/sex), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) and provides whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine-addicted smokers using visual craving cues (pictures) and reports behavioral and BOLD changes associated with neurofeedback. However, the fMRI results are reported as ROI-based percent BOLD change and paired t-tests on extracted ROI time series from anatomically drawn insular ROIs in four participants. The paper does not present any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results, nor does it report a within-participant fMRI contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli at the voxelwise/group level. Therefore it fails the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked analysis and the within-participant cue>control fMRI contrast required for inclusion. Exclusion ID E3 (only ROI analyses, no qualifying voxelwise result) applies.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity that includes clear visual stimuli (grayscaled images) alongside haptic conditions. The study reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., VS–VC, HS–HC) and group-level, whole-brain RFX-GLM/ANOVA results with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction and coordinates/tables. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Full text (abstract-level content only) indicates an fMRI study using food images (natural rewards) and relationships between affect and regional activation. This satisfies I3 (visual natural reward cues). However, the provided content does not report or make clear: (a) any within-participant cue>control contrast (I4) — no explicit food>control or equivalent contrast is described; and (b) any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical results (I5) — methods/results details and coordinate/table/voxelwise reporting are absent. Because the manuscript content is incomplete for verifying essential inclusion criteria, I cannot confirm that qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results are present. Therefore the study is excluded from the review at this stage (fulltext_incomplete flag set) pending a complete full text.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage pictures). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcoholic > non-alcoholic beverages) and second-level group voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with small-volume (mesocorticolimbic mask) and FWE/FDR-corrected results (tables and figures). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core voxelwise task-evoked results are provided. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity using visual cues with within-participant cocaine>neutral contrasts (cocaine minus neutral image contrasts). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded using SPM8 with cluster-level correction; results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps and in tables/figures with coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (stimuli, MRI acquisition, preprocessing in SPM8, statistical analyses), Results (one-sample t-test, between-group t-test, regressions) and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review’s requirements for visual cue-based fMRI, task-evoked within-subject contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise group-level results. Full text appears complete.

This study uses an fMRI MIDT with visual monetary reward cues (satisfies I3) and reports within-participant contrasts of reward anticipation (A2 win/A2 loss) relative to implicit baseline (satisfies I4). However, the main text reports ROI-based analyses (NAc, insula, MPFC) and does not present group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results with coordinates or SVC-corrected statistics. Although an exploratory whole-brain analysis is mentioned (see supplement), no qualifying voxelwise results are provided in the supplied full text and the supplement content is not available here. Therefore the study effectively reports only ROI results in the accessible text, triggering exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses, no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Inclusion criterion I5 (group-level voxelwise result) is not met. Excluded for E3; inclusion criteria met: I3, I4; inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (and smoking) cue-reactivity with visual cues and reports within-participant contrasts (drinking cues > neutral cues). However, all reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based (extracted VS and MPFC ROI effect sizes and statistics) with no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistical results presented. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast) are satisfied, but I5 (at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol-associated > abstract control stimuli. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM99, voxel-by-voxel GLM, group fixed-effects; thresholding reported) with reported activations in reward and attention networks. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. Although the fMRI pilot sample is small, the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-evoked group-level voxelwise results with visual cue-reactivity.

This fMRI study used audiovisual (visual+auditory) cocaine cues and calculated activation measures within ten predefined neuroanatomic regions (ROI approach), reporting percent change and fraction of activated pixels per region. It does include a within-subject contrast of cocaine cues > neutral (percent change between segments) and reports participant age/sex and scanner field strength. However, the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (no whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected analyses or coordinate tables of such voxelwise results). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (no qualifying voxelwise, whole-brain or SVC result). Exclusion ID met: E3. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (visual cue component present), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, field strength reported). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (favorite-food) cue-reactivity but uses individually tailored auditory guided-imagery scripts (audiotaped personalized scripts) rather than visual cues; no visual stimulus component or multimodal design including visual cues is reported. Thus inclusion criterion I3 (clear visual cue component) is NOT met. The study does meet I4 (within-participant contrast: favorite-food vs neutral), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses with FWE correction), I6 (results presented in tables/figures), and I7 (reports age/sex, cue type, 3T field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failing I3.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cues (video clips) of drug (cocaine) and natural reward (food) and reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain flexible-factorial and small-volume-corrected ROI analyses). The study includes within-participant contrasts comparing DRUG versus FOOD cue reactivity (DRUG>FOOD bias), which provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise contrasts relevant to drug and natural reward cue-reactivity. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T Siemens TrioTim), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an empirical perfusion fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue reactivity using audiovisual (visual) stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cues vs nonsmoking control cues at the group level with voxelwise statistical maps (t values, cluster-level results), including tables of coordinates and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI cue-reactivity analyses and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-evoked human fMRI study of tobacco (drug) cue-reactivity using visual videotaped cues. The study reports within-subject contrasts of cigarette cues > neutral cues (e.g., cigarette cue crave minus neutral; cigarette cue resist minus neutral) at the group level using voxelwise mixed-effects analyses (FSL/FEAT/FLAME) with voxelwise thresholds (Z>2.3, cluster p=0.01), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Core article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is present and participant/sample details (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual anticipatory cues for monetary reward/loss (natural reward), includes within-participant contrasts of reward-cue > non-incentive cue and loss-cue > non-incentive cue, and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (AFNI; cluster-corrected maps and voxelwise ANOVA) with coordinates and VOI results. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software are reported. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cues (videos of cocaine and food) and includes within-participant contrasts of cocaine>food. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (whole-brain contrasts with cluster correction, thresholding and reported activations), satisfying requirements for voxelwise results. Reporting includes participant demographics (matched age/sex/education), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity with audiovisual (visual included) cues and a within-participant cocaine>neutral contrast, but the paper reports ROI-based analyses (vermian ROIs and group ROI ANOVAs) and does not provide a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical result (figures include a single-subject activation map but no group voxelwise coordinates/SVC). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes a within-participant contrast of food>nonfood, and reports group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain analyses with cluster-level FWE correction) with coordinates and tables/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12/CAT12). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an empirical fMRI paper of alcohol cue-reactivity using a multimodal (gustatory + visual label) cue paradigm, includes within-subject Alcohol>Water contrasts, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-corrected Z-statistics) with coordinates in tables. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI task-based study of cannabis cue reactivity using clearly defined visual stimuli (images of cannabis, cigarettes, neutral, and animal cues) (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts examining cannabis cues > neutral (Can > Neutral) and a stricter Can > Neutral + Cigarette contrast (I4). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were conducted using FEAT with cluster-wise multiple comparison correction (Z>2.3, cluster p<.05), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result (I5); ROI results are also reported but whole-brain results are present. Results and maps/tables/figures are described in the main text (I6). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (fMRIPrep) and analysis software (FSL/FEAT) are reported (I7). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI cue-exposure study with a visual component (multimodal tactile+visual) and reports within-participant cannabis cue > appetitive cue contrasts; participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. However, all group-level neuroimaging results are reported as ROI-based mean z-statistics extracted from predefined masks; the paper does not present whole-brain voxelwise or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked results or coordinate tables/figures that would qualify. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: there is no clear visual cue component. The task used individualized audiotaped guided imagery (auditory imagery) rather than visual-only or multimodal designs that include visual cues. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts of cue conditions, e.g., favorite-food vs neutral-relaxing), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain connectivity results with FWE correction), I6 (results reported in main text/figures/supplement), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (visual cue component). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to visual cue-reactivity studies.

Full text reports an fMRI study using visual alcohol-related pictures and neutral control images (visual cue component). The primary analyses include within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral stimuli and anticipation of monetary gain/loss > no outcome. Group-level voxelwise results are reported, including small-volume-corrected (S.V.C.) analyses in the ventral striatum (p < 0.05 FWE for VOI) with stereotactic coordinates. Results and methods (subjects, MRI field strength 1.5T, preprocessing, SPM2) are fully described. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise results), I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures), and I7 (participant and acquisition details reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food images (natural reward cues) with within-participant contrasts comparing cue types (e.g., ADMIT_TASTY>ADMIT_NOT_TASTY and ADMIT_TASTY>REGULATE_TASTY). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical analyses are reported (voxelwise P<0.001, cluster FWE P<0.05) and results are presented in tables/figures. Relevant methodological details (participant sex/age range, cue type, 3T MRI, SPM8 preprocessing/statistics) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that tests visual alcohol-paired cues (novel geometric shapes) and reports a within-subject contrast [CS+ > CS−]. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (cluster-forming p=0.001, cluster-level FWE-corrected pFWE<0.05), with coordinates/tables and figures presenting the voxelwise results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/FSL) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for task-evoked, voxelwise cue>control contrasts with visual stimuli and is includable in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine dependence using visual smoking-related cues and control images. The manuscript reports within-participant contrasts ("smoke > control") and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (RFX ANOVA and RFX ANCOVAs) with cluster-size multiple-comparisons correction; results are presented in tables and figures with coordinates. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing, and analysis software (BrainVoyager) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study examines visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports a within-subject food>neutral contrast, and provides participant demographics and methodological details. However, the neuroimaging analyses are ROI-based (AAL-derived ROI mean estimates and paired t-tests) and do not present a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical result necessary for coordinate-based meta-analysis inclusion. Although Talairach coordinates were mentioned as ‘‘calculated,’’ the main reported results are ROI mean comparisons rather than qualifying voxelwise SVC or whole-brain peak coordinates. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I6 (results/coordinates acceptable if present — reporting suggests coordinates were considered), and I7 (participant/method details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC task-evoked statistical result reported). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used personalized auditory guided-imagery (audiotapes) to elicit favorite-food cues rather than presenting visual stimuli. The meta-analysis specifically requires studies with a clear visual cue component (I3), which is not met here. The study does meet other requirements: it reports within-participant contrasts of favorite-food cues versus control (I4), provides whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (I5) with results presented in supplemental/tables (I6), and reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and analysis software (I7). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing inclusion criterion I3 (lack of visual cue component).

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related and neutral images (visual cue component) with within-participant contrasts (heroin-related > neutral). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses, p < .0001, cluster-level corrected) with coordinates in tables/figures. Methods report participant demographics (14 males, mean age), 3-T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), satisfying reporting preferences. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and include within-subject cue>control contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cocaine-related pictures vs natural scene pictures (I3). It includes within-participant contrasts of cocaine cues > control stimuli and reports task-evoked activation contrasts (I4). Voxelwise whole-brain analyses and group-level random-effects models are described with multiple-comparison correction and cluster thresholds, providing qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results (I5). Results and coordinates/MNI seeds are reported in the text (and implied figures/tables), satisfying acceptability of reported voxelwise results (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported (I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject cue contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This fMRI study used a visual cue-reactivity task (full-colour cannabis images vs matched neutral images) with an explicit within-participant cannabis>neutral contrast. Group-level voxelwise analysis was performed using FLAME (mixed-effects) for exploratory ROI analyses, yielding a reported significant cluster in the left putamen with MNI coordinates (x=−24, y=4, z=6), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software—FSL/FEAT/FLAME) are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Although sample size is modest, no exclusion criteria are triggered (coordinate-level voxelwise results were provided, not ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses).

This study uses an fMRI cannabis cue–reactivity task with visual stimuli and reports participant demographics and MRI details (meets I3 and I7). However, the authors explicitly state that "A voxelwise approach was not completed for this analysis" and report hypothesis-driven ROI average percent signal analyses only; thus no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results are provided (meets exclusion E3). Additionally, the manuscript does not present a within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus contrast (it reports activations during cannabis and neutral pictures separately and between-group effects), so there is no accompanying within-subject cue>control contrast (meets exclusion E5). Therefore the study does not satisfy the voxelwise/within-subject analytic requirements and must be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) in heavy-drinking participants. It includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > rest/control, reports group-level voxelwise results (one-sample and ANOVA) with whole-brain FWE-corrected findings (right inferior frontal gyrus) and a small-volume (ROI) FWE-corrected result in the ventral striatum; peak coordinates and cluster sizes are provided. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant demographics. Therefore all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity voxelwise task-evoked results are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol stimuli with an explicit within-subject contrast (alcohol > neutral). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain second-level analyses with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster-extent correction) presented in tables/figures, and provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/12). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task activation, and includes the required within-participant contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (high-caloric food images) with within-participant contrasts (e.g., WATCH Food > WATCH Neutral). Group-level, voxelwise random-effects t-contrasts were performed using SPM8 on 3T data and statistical maps were thresholded with FWE-correction; coordinates and ROI results (MNI coordinates reported for insula correlations) are provided. The manuscript reports necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/software). Thus it satisfies: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with corrected thresholds), I6 (coordinates/results reported), and I7 (required reporting details). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and include within-subject contrasts (so E3–E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues vs neutral images with within-participant contrasts (heroin-related > neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses reported using SPM5. Results are reported at p≤0.05 FWE-corrected with cluster threshold and regional activations are described. Participant demographics (male, age range), MRI field strength (1.5 T), cue type (visual heroin-related images), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol vs non-alcohol photographs as distractors. It reports within-participant AD> (vs) NAD contrasts (AD-NAD) and voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (rmANOVA) with multiple-comparison correction (FWE) as well as voxelwise correlational analyses; an a priori amygdala ROI analysis is also reported. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, SPM5) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a within-participant task-evoked contrast of a natural reward cue (monetary) versus control (50¢>0¢). The monetary cue was presented visually (money reminder cue and word stimuli), satisfying the visual-cue requirement. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses with voxel-wise thresholds, cluster extent correction, and coordinates for significant clusters, and provides sufficient methodological details (participants’ age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Although drug-word versus neutral-word contrasts were collapsed and not emphasized, the monetary 50¢>0¢ within-subject contrast qualifies as a natural reward-related cue>control contrast. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards.

This paper is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol vs control images presented during a combined stop-signal task. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol and control picture trials (e.g., CRAlcohol - CRControl and GOAlcohol - GOControl) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected, tables of MNI coordinates are reported). Participants’ age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is an empirical fMRI study using monetary cues in a visual MID task (visual cue component) and assesses reward-related cue-reactivity (monetary gain/loss cues). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., gain cue > neutral cue; loss cue > neutral cue) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses using whole-brain BPM with small-volume correction (SVC) in predefined VOIs, with SVC-adjusted FWE-corrected results. Participant/sample details, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual smoking pictures and neutral control images in abstinent smokers. It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking > neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (cluster-corrected thresholding; tables/Supplementary materials cited). Voxelwise results are available in the main text/tables and supplementary material. The paper includes methods (preprocessing/statistical software: FSL) and detailed imaging analysis. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and includes a qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast). Some reporting details (e.g., MRI field strength, explicit mean age) are not evident in the provided excerpt, but missing preferred details do not preclude inclusion per criteria.

This fMRI study directly investigates alcohol cue-reactivity using visual cues (cue symbols for alcohol, food, neutral) and an established cue paradigm. It includes within-participant task contrasts of alcohol cues versus control stimuli (e.g., high-threat alcohol cues contrasted against high-threat food and high-threat neutral cues) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain results with multiple-comparison correction (AFNI 3dClustSim), satisfying the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical results. Details on participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Prisma), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, CONN) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met. No exclusion criteria apply (none of E3–E6 are met). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used visual drug cues (opioid words) in an opioid-word Stroop task (I3). A within-participant OW>NW contrast (opioid words vs neutral words) was computed at first level and entered into group-level SPM voxelwise analyses (I4). The paper reports voxelwise second-level task-evoked statistical results (one-sample and two-sample SPM analyses) with cluster-level FWE-corrected findings for the between-group contrast (thus satisfying group-level voxelwise reporting; I5). Results and contrasts are reported in the main text and figures/tables (I6). Participant/sample, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, AFNI) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task-evoked voxelwise results, includes within-participant contrasts). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and neutral controls, reporting within-participant drug-cue>neutral contrasts and group-level voxelwise results (AlphaSim-corrected whole-brain analyses). Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing and SPM8, and participant demographics. The paper provides coordinates/cluster results and correlation analyses. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI task (Monetary Incentive Delay) using visual cues signaling monetary reward (natural reward-related cues). It includes a within-participant contrast of anticipation of reward > neutral anticipation and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (mixed-effects, cluster-thresholded) as well as ROI results. Participant/sample and MRI details (age, sex, 3T field strength, preprocessing software) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material availability is noted.

This is an empirical task-fMRI study using visual alcohol cues as distractors during a response-inhibition task (meets I3). It includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol > neutral/scramble (meets I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported using voxel-wise p<0.001 with cluster-extent correction to achieve pFWE<0.05 and identified clusters/ROIs (meets I5 and I6). Methods report participant demographics (all-male sample, N and ages in tables), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), satisfying I7. The study does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore this study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol images (visual stimuli) and a within-participant alcohol>neutral beverage contrast. The paper reports group-level voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses within a striatum mask (masked voxelwise thresholding with cluster-level correction and MNI coordinates reported), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise result (small-volume-corrected). Relevant details (participant sex, cue type, 3T scanner, SPM5 preprocessing) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue reactivity using pictorial alcohol stimuli in adolescents. The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts of alcoholic versus nonalcoholic pictures and voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical results (cluster-corrected), with coordinates/tables and figures (Tables 2–3, Figure 2). Participant demographics, cue type, scanning parameters, preprocessing, and software (AFNI) are described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual word cues (alcohol-related words vs neutral words). The study reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses (independent-samples t test and single-sample t tests) across the whole brain with clusterwise correction; results are described by anatomical regions and statistical thresholds. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI acquisition parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual cocaine cue videotapes (meets I3). The analyses include within-participant contrasts comparing cocaine cue viewing to a neutral baseline (first 30 s and full 3 min), satisfying I4. Group-level voxelwise results are reported: whole-brain voxelwise correlation analyses and between-group voxelwise contrasts with clusters and Talairach coordinates displayed in tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected task-evoked voxelwise results (I5, I6). Participant demographics (age/sex distribution), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical methods are reported, meeting I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), and include within-participant cue>control contrasts (E5 not met). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol images (alcohol vs neutral) in recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients, meeting the meta-analysis scope. It includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim cluster-wise FWE) and cluster coordinates/tables/figures. They also report an ROI (ventral striatum) small-volume analysis, but whole-brain voxelwise results are present and qualifying. Key methodological details (3T MRI, SPM preprocessing, participant age/sex, cue type) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes the required within-participant contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study used a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with visual cues signaling reward magnitude (natural reward-related cues). It reports within-participant contrasts of REWARD>NEUTRAL (anticipation) and LOSS>NEUTRAL, and includes group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses corrected for multiple comparisons (Monte-Carlo corrected p<.05) as well as ROI results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts and group-level voxelwise results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related images and matched neutral images. It reports a within-subject contrast of smoking > neutral and conducts group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANCOVA) with cluster-level correction; results are reported as whole-brain coordinates/tables and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex: women), cue type, MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (Brain Voyager QX) are reported. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations).

This is an empirical fMRI study using clear visual cues (abstract geometric shapes) predicting beer versus water (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of beer>water for anticipation, outcome notification, and delivery phases (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs, cluster-level FWE correction) with activation coordinates and NeuroVault links (satisfies I5 and I6). The manuscript provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only (whole-brain results are reported), not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The full text describes an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking videos (clear visual cue component) with a within-subject design comparing smoking versus neutral videos. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain cluster-corrected P < 0.05) with MNI coordinates and tables/figures, and describes methods (subjects, fMRI, analysis with FSL 4.1). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (heroin-related images and IAPS pleasant/neutral images) in abstinent opioid-dependent males and controls. The paper includes within-participant contrasts (heroin vs. baseline; heroin vs. neutral; pleasant vs. baseline), reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates and corrected thresholds (FDR) and regression analyses (voxelwise), and provides scanner field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistics (SPM2). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criterion applies.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (120 food vs 120 control pictures) with within-subject contrasts (food–control) at the first level and group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper reports whole-brain and small-volume-corrected results (coordinates and PFWE values), details preprocessing/statistics (SPM5) and MRI field strength (3T), and provides participant age/sex. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical task-evoked voxelwise results present). Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of cue-reactivity using visual drug-related words presented via MRI-compatible goggles (visual cue component). It reports within-subject drug>neutral contrasts and performs voxelwise group-level SPM analyses with cluster-level multiple-comparisons correction and small-volume correction in the mesencephalon; coordinates and tables are provided. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. These findings satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (visual cues, within-participant contrast, and qualifying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This full-text reports an empirical human fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity using visual (audio-visual) smoking cues and matched nonsmoking control cues. Design includes within-subject contrasts (smoking cue > nonsmoking cue) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses using SPM2. Results are reported as voxelwise statistical maps and coordinates (tables/figures) and small-volume correction (SVC) was applied for a priori ROIs; cluster-level whole-brain results are also described. MRI field strength (3.0 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. The article contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

Full text content provided is incomplete (only references and metadata). I cannot verify core methods, results, or analyses. Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3-E6 violations identified from the limited content). Inclusion criteria met: none can be confirmed from the provided text. Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be assessed: I3 (visual cue component – title suggests virtual environments but methods not available to confirm visual-only or multimodal design including visual cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast not verifiable), I5 (presence of qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results not verifiable), I6 (reporting of voxelwise results in tables/figures/supplementary cannot be confirmed). Action: request full article (introduction, methods, results) to determine eligibility.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (120 high- and 120 low-calorie food images) and within-subject contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie; high-calorie > objects). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 with small-volume correction (FWE-corrected results reported for a priori ROIs), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked voxelwise results. The manuscript provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (audiovisual heroin and matched neutral images).
