This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual food cues (HC vs LC pictures) in obese participants pre- and post-laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. It includes within-participant HC>LC contrasts, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE-corrected, P_FWE<0.05) with results described in the main text and supplementary materials, and provides MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective (natural reward visual cue-reactivity) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used resting-state fMRI (ICA and ACC-seed rsFC) to examine neural correlates of nicotine withdrawal and withdrawal-induced craving; there was no task presenting visual drug or natural reward cues and no within-participant cue>control (visual) contrast. Thus it does not address cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity results. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only seed-based connectivity/resting-state analyses without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an fMRI cue-reactivity task with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level task-evoked voxelwise results), I6 (not applicable — no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of a natural reward (chocolate) that includes a clear visual cue condition (picture of chocolate) and multimodal conditions. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of visual cue > control (chocpic vs grey control) and related contrasts, and presents group-level voxelwise SPM results with small-volume corrections and peak coordinates. Methods report participant demographics (female, age 20–30), cue types, 3.0 T scanner, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual monetary reward cues ($ vs #) during an antisaccade task, meeting the review focus on drug or natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity. The study reports within-participant contrasts (Reward vs Neutral) and analyzes reward>neutral effects. Group-level mixed-effects fMRI analyses were run and z-statistic images within a priori ROIs were corrected for multiple comparisons using FDR (i.e., small-volume correction within ROIs), satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise, small-volume-corrected task-evoked result. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, FSL). Whole-brain analyses found no clusters beyond ROIs, but that does not negate the reported small-volume voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

This study used an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay Task to examine reward/loss processing with monetary cues, not drug cues or prototypical natural reward cues (e.g., food, erotic stimuli). Inclusion: I5 is satisfied (group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction and reported coordinates), I6 is satisfied (coordinates and ROI results reported in main text/tables), and I7 is satisfied (participant demographics and methodological details reported). Exclusion: none of E3–E6 apply. Not satisfied: I3 (study does not assess drug- or clearly defined natural reward-related cue-reactivity; stimuli are monetary task cues rather than drug or natural-reward cue images) and I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control as required by the review scope). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s scope for drug or natural reward cue-reactivity and is excluded.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs. neutral images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral), group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with explicit thresholding and cluster correction (AlphaSim/FWE) and reports regional activations (peaks/ROIs). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM5/SPM8) and task details are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol and non-alcohol beverage images (meets I3). It includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral beverage cues (ALC-BEV) (meets I4). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with FWE cluster-correction and peak coordinates (meets I5 and I6). The manuscript provides participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) details (meets I7). The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are applicable. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking videos as cues (I3). It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking>control videos (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported with multiple-comparisons correction (whole-brain corrected and a priori small-volume correction for DLPFC) and coordinate tables/figures (I5, I6). Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (fmristat), and cue type are reported (I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based task analyses and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of drug cue reactivity using visual smoking cues), I4 (within-participant comparisons of smoking cues vs control cues), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level task result reported). Full text appears complete and contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related pictorial cues and neutral control images, with within-participant contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) reported. The paper provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster-corrected statistics (Z>2.3, cluster p<.05) for SR vs N contrasts in smokers, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. ROI analyses of the ventral striatum are also reported. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is an original human fMRI study). Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual picture cues (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug, and IAPS emotional pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral (e.g., alcohol>neutral, polydrug>neutral, marijuana>neutral). Analyses were performed as group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistics using FSL/FEAT (mixed-effects OLS) with results presented in tables and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual alcohol, polydrug and marijuana picture cues and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise BOLD contrasts (meeting I3, I5, I6, and I7), the reported analyses contrast non-studied versus studied items within the same drug cue categories rather than a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast (e.g., drug > neutral or non-drug). Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli as required (I4 not met). This fMRI study uses visual food stimuli (meets I3) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results analyzed with SPM5 at the second level (meets I5 and I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported (meets I7). However, the reported contrasts are pleasant versus unpleasant food pictures (food>food), not food cues versus neutral/non-food control stimuli or baseline, so there is no qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet inclusion criterion I4.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food pictures. It includes a within-participant contrast (food > control) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain voxelwise results thresholded at P<0.001 with cluster extent and additional small-volume FWE-corrected tests in a priori ROIs). Results are presented in tables and figures with coordinates. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, reporting within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are presented (stereotactic MNI coordinates for local maxima, voxel-wise subtraction figures), satisfying the requirement for a voxelwise group-level result reported as coordinates/figures. The manuscript documents participant age/sex, cue type (visual food images), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, PsychoPy), so preferred reporting items are present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of smoking cue-reactivity using visual smoking vs. neutral images, with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FLAME, cluster-corrected p<0.05, Z>2.3) for the smoking>neutral contrast and extracts DMN ROI betas; voxelwise results are described in the main text. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), participant age/sex, and cue type are reported. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for visual cue type, within-participant cue>control contrast, and qualifying group-level voxelwise results.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol-related images (IAPS) with a within-participant contrast (alcohol>neutral). Group-level voxelwise results are reported: whole-brain analyses (peak-level p<.001, cluster-level FWE p<.05) and anatomically defined small-volume-corrected ROI analyses in the bilateral amygdala (FWE-corrected p<.05). Participant characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5/SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking-related images in 30 chronic smokers. It includes within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral (aversive smoking-related vs. neutral; appetitive smoking-related vs. neutral) and reports group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster correction (Monte Carlo/3dClustSim) and coordinate results (main text/supplementary tables). Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3.0T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Full text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (and food/items as control visual stimuli) in alcohol-dependent and control women. Within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol cues to control stimuli are explicitly reported (e.g., (2×ALC) – (FOOD + ITEM), high-risk vs low-risk contrasts), and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed using mixed-effects FLAME with cluster correction (z>2.3, p<0.05). Methods report participant demographics (female, ages 18–28), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL v4.1.9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). More importantly, the study used script-guided imagery (auditory/imaginal cues), not visual cues, so it fails inclusion criterion I3 (requires a clear visual cue component). The study does report a within-participant contrast of drug cues > stress (I4) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results across the brain (voxelwise, uncorrected whole-brain results) satisfying I5; reporting of results in the abstract/figures is consistent with I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Because I3 is not satisfied and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) with within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs. neutral/abstract) at first-level and group-level voxelwise analyses reported (whole-brain linear correlations with coordinates and cluster sizes). The methods report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and SPM5 analysis, and participant demographics (age/sex). Voxelwise group results (p-values, coordinates, clusters) are presented in the main text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for within-participant cue>control contrasts, task-evoked voxelwise group results, and reporting details required for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug (methamphetamine) and natural reward (sexual) images with within-subject contrasts (methamphetamine>neutral; sexual>neutral) and group comparisons. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (cluster in left superior frontal cortex with peak coordinates, cluster size, and p-value using cluster-level FWE correction), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results. Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity, but the experimental cue modality is gustatory (taste delivery of preferred alcoholic beverage vs litchi juice) rather than visual. Inclusion criterion I3 requires a clear visual cue component (visual-only or multimodal that include visual cues), which is not met. The study does meet I4 (within-participant contrast alcohol cue > control cue), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with cluster correction), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded solely because it lacks the required visual cue component (I3 not met).

This is an fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay task with visually presented cues (word cues indicating potential monetary reward/loss). It includes within-participant contrasts of reward-related cues (A1 prospect and A2 anticipation of $5) versus implicit baseline, and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume FWE-corrected findings (ventral striatum/NAcc and other ROIs). Key methodological details (participant age/sex info, 3T field strength, SPM2 preprocessing) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol > non-alcoholic beverage) at the individual level and group-level voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates and tables; some results were tested with family-wise error correction and voxelwise analyses are reported (voxel-wise threshold and cluster extent provided). Methods report MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI), participant demographics (age- and gender-matched groups), and cue types. Full article includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI included alcohol beverage pictures—visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant contrast of alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage pictures was modeled). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result for the drug-cue>control contrast is reported—the manuscript states 'no effect... (data not shown)' for alcohol stimuli), I6 (qualifying voxelwise results for the alcohol cue contrast are not presented in main text, tables, figures, or supplements as provided). Full text appears complete. Because the review requires a reported group-level voxelwise drug-cue>control result (whole-brain or SVC) and this is not available in the article, the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion decision because the study does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast of natural reward cues versus a control stimulus (e.g., appetizing food > unappetizing food or food images > neutral) required by I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual food images), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain results with cluster correction reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/tables), I7 (participant age/sex and MRI details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no qualifying within-participant natural reward-related cues>control-stimuli contrast presented; the reported contrasts compare reappraisal instructions while viewing appetizing foods rather than food cues versus non-food/neutral control). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restrictions). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

Full text appears incomplete / paywalled (only abstract and references available). From the abstract: (a) visual alcohol-related video cues were used, satisfying I3; (b) a within-subject alcohol versus neutral contrast was performed (reported as not significantly different), satisfying I4. However, the reported main results focus on psychophysiological interaction (PPI) seed-based connectivity (effective connectivity) with the posterior cingulate cortex; no clear evidence is available in the accessible text that a group-level voxelwise task-evoked (alcohol cues>control) result was reported as a whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical map/coordinates. Therefore I5 cannot be confirmed and, based on available information, the study effectively reports only seed-based connectivity results, which meets exclusion criterion E4. Because the full article is not accessible, this decision has limited confidence.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol and smoking cues in the same participants. It includes a clear visual cue component (smoking videos) as part of a multimodal design, satisfying the visual-cue requirement. Within-participant contrasts are reported (smoking cue vs fixation baseline; alcohol taste vs baseline), and group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (voxel-wise one-sample t tests across subjects with cluster-wise inference and FSL tools). Results are presented in figures and described in the text (cluster-wise p-values and peak regions), meeting the requirement that qualifying voxelwise results be available. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-participant cue>control contrasts; empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity (food images). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing high-caloric > low-caloric food (Tea and Water conditions) and interaction contrasts. Group-level voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain and ROI small-volume-corrected tests) are reported with FWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates (e.g., DLPFC correlation p(FWE)=0.031), satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an fMRI task study using visual infant face stimuli (baby schema) as natural reward-related cues in opioid-dependent participants. It includes within-subject contrasts (Low, Unmanipulated, High baby schema; modeled vs crosshair and comparisons across levels) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (FEAT/FSL whole-brain analyses, cluster-corrected at z=3.1, p<0.005 FWE) with activation in the ventral striatum. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT), participant demographics, and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject cue (smoking) > neutral contrast. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (familywise error and cluster-corrected results) identifying cue-reactive clusters, with results described in the main text and supplementary materials. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and statistical software (FSL, FILM) are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes the required within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (anticipatory shapes and words) to probe nondrug (monetary) reward cue-reactivity in alcohol-dependent patients and controls. It includes within-subject contrasts of reward cues > no-incentive cues (pre-response $1/$10 vs $0) and WIN vs HIT contrasts, and reports group-level voxelwise statistical maps with FDR-corrected results (whole-brain), with tables and figures. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, AFNI preprocessing/statistics) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (photographs of appetizing vs bland foods) assessing natural reward cue-reactivity with a within-subject contrast (appetizing > bland). Group-level voxelwise second-level SPM analyses are reported (whole-brain and small-volume-corrected ROI results with coordinates and statistical thresholds). Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI investigation using visually presented monetary incentive cues (GAIN/LOSS/NEUTRAL) and contrasts anticipation of monetary gain/loss versus neutral within participants. It provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain cluster-corrected maps using FLAME/FEAT with reported thresholds and peak coordinates). Participant demographics, cue type (monetary visual cues), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT/FLAME) are reported. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related vs neutral images) with within-subject contrasts (smoking>neutral) reported. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-corrected, tables/figures with coordinates) analyzed at the group level using Brain Voyager QX on a 3T scanner. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol-modulated smoking cue reactivity using visual cigarette-related images in heavy-drinking nondaily smokers. It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking vs control cues (reported in post hoc tests and ANOVA interactions) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results using whole-brain analyses with FDR correction for ventral striatum as well as uncorrected whole-brain results; results are presented in figures/tables. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study reports an fMRI food-cue (natural reward) task using visual stimuli (food vs. non-food pictures) and includes within-participant food>non-food contrasts (percent signal change computed per subject). Importantly, the authors performed a group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis examining glucose vs. water differences in food cue reactivity (task-evoked contrast based on food vs. non-food), reporting significant clusters in OFC and VS, which satisfies the requirement for a voxelwise task-evoked result. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner and analysis software are reported. Although ROI analyses are also used, the presence of the whole-brain voxelwise analysis means the study is eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of visual reward-cue reactivity. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text (abstract and methods) describes a behavioral cue-reactivity study using personalized videotaped cues to elicit urge to drink; no functional MRI methods, data, or voxelwise group-level results are reported. Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for fMRI task-evoked voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (not an fMRI study with visual cue component for imaging), I4 (no within-participant fMRI cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results), I6 (not applicable — no voxelwise imaging results available to report), and I7 (imaging/method reporting not applicable). Inclusion criteria met: none. Exclusion criteria met: none of the specified exclusion IDs (E3–E6) precisely apply because the paper is an empirical behavioral study rather than an fMRI study; however it fails to meet required inclusion criteria for the review. Full text appears complete for the purposes of screening (behavioral methods, results, conclusions present).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues (picture blocks) with a within-participant contrast ('alcohol—neutral') and group-level voxelwise analyses reported with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster-extent FWE correction. Results are presented in tables/figures (including supplementary tables) and demographic/MRI/preprocessing details (3T scanner, SPM5/8, sex distribution, age range) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, nor non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies all meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study examines fMRI responses to visual natural reward cues (high-calorie food images) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistics for the main effect of cognitive strategy; participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and preprocessing/software are reported. However, it does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food cues > neutral/control stimuli) at the group-level voxelwise or small-volume-corrected level. The primary voxelwise analysis tested differences among cognitive control strategies (up-regulation, suppression, reappraisal) and explicitly excluded the passive viewing condition from that ANOVA; passive viewing consisted of food pictures without a neutral non-food control, so no qualifying cue>control contrast is available. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met, which precludes inclusion despite other criteria being satisfied.

This is an fMRI task-based study using visual food cues (IAPS images) with a within-participant contrast of appetitive (AC) > neutral (NC) blocks. Data were analyzed with a whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise GLM (Talairach space) and results are reported as voxelwise clusters/statistics (cluster size, voxelwise p-threshold), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Imaging parameters (3T scanner), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX), participant sex distribution, and cue type are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward-related cue-reactivity.

Full text provided is only a brief summary/abstract, not a complete article (methods, detailed results, and statistical reporting are missing). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI with alcohol-related visual cues is clearly described). Inclusion criteria not verifiably met: I4 (the summary implies cue-related activation but does not explicitly report a within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no confirmation that a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical result is reported), I6 (cannot verify that voxelwise results are available in tables/figures/supplement), I7 (reporting of participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details not provided). Exclusion criteria met: none can be confidently applied from the summary alone (E3–E6 cannot be assessed). Because the core article content is incomplete, I cannot confirm required voxelwise task-evoked results; therefore the study is excluded pending access to the full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-related pictures and neutral IAPS images (visual cue component). It includes within-subject contrasts (CUEalc > IAPSneutral) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume FWE-corrected and whole-brain FWE-corrected findings (coordinates, figures, and tables). Methods report participant demographics (age/sex matching), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, BPM). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual smoking-related images and a within-participant smoking>neutral contrast, with group-level voxelwise results (cluster-corrected Z=2.3, p<0.05) presented in tables and figures. Participant demographics, MRI acquisition parameters, preprocessing, and statistical methods are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual cues (alcohol-related pictures and IAPS positive/negative/neutral images) in detoxified alcoholic subjects and matched controls. It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral; positive>neutral; negative>neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses using SPM5 (whole-brain voxelwise results, tables/figures cited). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are provided. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and should be included.

This study investigates visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results, but it does NOT include a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food images). Instead, contrasts compare task states with the same food stimuli (inhibition vs passive viewing, imaginary eating vs passive viewing, and inhibition vs imaginary eating). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (natural reward, visual food cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported, FDR-corrected), I6 (coordinates/figures reported), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). Exclusion criterion triggered: E5 (only between-condition/task contrasts without a qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because no within-subject natural reward>control cue contrast (I4 not met).

Although this fMRI study used visual alcohol cues and reports participant demographics and acquisition/preprocessing details (I3 and I7 satisfied), it does not report a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast (I4 not met) nor a group-level voxelwise or small-volume-corrected cue-reactivity map for alcohol cues (I5 not met). The authors primarily report voxelwise results for reward (win>lose) and ROI-based analyses for stimulus-category effects, and explicitly state they found no specific alcohol-cue effects; no qualifying alcohol>control voxelwise task-evoked statistical result is provided. Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis’ necessary cue-reactivity criteria and is excluded. Exclusion criterion applied: E5 (no accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5.

This study is a PET (H2[15]O) neuroimaging study, not an fMRI study. The meta-analysis objective explicitly targets fMRI studies of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). Therefore the primary inclusion criterion requiring use of functional MRI is not met. Study strengths relevant to the review: it used within-participant contrasts of drug video > neutral video (I4), reported group-level voxelwise task-evoked SPM results with whole-brain and corrected findings (I5,I6), and provided participant demographics, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software details (I7). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete. Final decision: EXCLUDED due to modality mismatch (PET vs required fMRI).

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual food pictures (natural reward cues) and a within-subject contrast of food pictures > location pictures. Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM99) are reported with voxelwise cluster results shown in tables/figures (whole-brain voxelwise inference with reported thresholds and coordinates). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective (visual natural reward cue-reactivity) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-participant cue>control contrasts; the study is empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of interest (Look Craved > Look Not Craved and Look Craved > Look Neutral). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported using whole-brain cluster-correction (AlphaSim) and a targeted relaxed cluster threshold to interrogate the ventral striatum (reported as a 29-voxel cluster), satisfying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected reporting. Relevant methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) are provided. Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (all food > non-food; high-calorie > low-calorie) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain results survived FWE correction (cluster-extent threshold) and region-of-interest small-volume corrections were also applied, meeting the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. The paper provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking cues with a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast and reports participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and preprocessing software (satisfies I3, I4, I7). However, the paper’s primary analyses extract average beta values from a priori ROIs (4mm spheres) and use these ROI values in Cox/logistic regressions; the manuscript does not report a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical result (I5 not met). No qualifying voxelwise results are provided in the main text, tables, figures, or supplements to meet I6. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results) and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (fattening vs nonfattening) and reports participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details. However, the analyses are presented using an a priori ROI approach and averaged activation within those ROIs (and ICCs); the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume–corrected task-evoked statistical results (no coordinates or voxelwise SVC results are provided in the main text). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI cue-reactivity investigation of smoking using visual stimuli and a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast, and reports participant demographics and scanning details. However, group-level results are presented as ROI-based averaged parameter estimates from 5-mm spheres and subsequent ANOVAs rather than as voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level task-evoked statistical maps or coordinates. No qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results are reported in the main text or tables, so the study reports only ROI analyses and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual smoking cues), I4 (within-participant smoking>neutral contrast), I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, field strength, and software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently the study is excluded from the voxelwise meta-analysis.

Exclusion criteria met: E4 (study reports only resting-state functional connectivity analyses without any task-evoked cue-reactivity contrasts) and E5 (study reports only between-group RSFC contrasts between opioid users and non-users with no within-participant drug-cue > control-stimulus contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (study reports methodological details such as MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (CONN toolbox, SPM, AFNI), and participant information). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity task with a visual cue component — the study used resting-state fMRI, not cue presentation), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no task-evoked voxelwise group-level statistical results; reported results are RSFC group comparisons, not task-evoked contrasts), I6 (not applicable because no qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results to report). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of task-based visual cue-reactivity and must be excluded.

This is an empirical task fMRI study using visual smoking cues and within-subject contrasts (smoking images vs. neutral images) entered into analyses. Subject-level beta maps contrasting smoking vs. neutral images were derived and used in MVPA; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with cluster-wise family-wise error correction via wild bootstrapping) tested relationships between classification accuracy and behavioral attentional bias and group-by-bias interactions. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, AFNI, MVPA toolbox). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual romantic cues (natural reward) vs neutral controls, with within-subject contrasts (romantic>neutral) and group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses with cluster-based correction reported. Methods report visual-only stimuli (IAPS romantic images), scanning on a 3T scanner, preprocessing/analysis with SPM8, and results described as whole-brain cluster-corrected activations across regions. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and qualifying voxelwise group-level results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos). The study reports within-participant contrasts of food cues > control (Food vs Objects; Unhealthy Food vs Objects; Healthy Food vs Objects) at the group level, and reports voxelwise group-level results including whole-brain cluster-corrected activations and ROI analyses. Voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results are described and thresholding/correction methods reported. Participant demographics and cue types are reported; some methodological details (e.g., scanner field strength) are not explicit but this alone does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

The study examines alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in an fMRI within-subject design (I3 and I4 satisfied) and reports participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (I7). However, the paper does not present any group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Instead, all reported analyses are ROI-to-ROI task-modulated connectivity analyses (generalized PPI) and ROI-based correlation tests. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criteria E3/E4 (reports only ROI/connectivity analyses with no qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results). Accordingly, the study must be excluded from the voxelwise activation meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking-related images (visual cue component) and includes within-participant contrasts of smoking-related > neutral images. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results from whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction (cluster-corrected p ≤ .005) and details preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager) and MRI field strength (3T). Behavioral Stroop and ICA connectivity analyses are also present but do not replace the task-evoked voxelwise results. Participant sex (women-only) is reported; other descriptive details (age) are not emphasized in the provided excerpt but I7 is preferred not required. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not trigger any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (Food-pics images) that examines neural responses to natural reward-related stimuli. It includes within-subject task regressors for food trials (go and no-go trials modeled) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses (3dMVM exploratory whole-brain results with coordinates and cluster tables). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, ANTs, SPM not needed) are reported. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity, contains within-participant cue-related contrasts, and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates.

This study investigates fMRI visual food-cue reactivity (natural reward) using food vs. object images (satisfies I3) and includes within-participant contrasts comparing food vs. object responses (satisfies I4). However, all reported fMRI results are ROI-based: COPEs were extracted from 14 predefined ROIs and analyses were conducted on these ROI-wise mean values. The manuscript does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical results (no tables of coordinates or voxelwise clusters are reported). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected analysis). Accordingly, the study must be excluded from the voxelwise meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity with visual cigarette stimuli and visual natural-reward (romantic partner) stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., acquaintance+cigarette vs. acquaintance+pen; partner+pen vs. acquaintance+pen) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with cluster-wise multiple-comparison correction (Monte Carlo/AlphaSim) and coordinates/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, and AFNI preprocessing/statistical software. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity that used audio-visual stimuli (visual component present), acquired task-evoked perfusion fMRI at 3T, and reported within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking control cues. Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses were performed and significant clusters (e.g., medial orbitofrontal cortex) are reported with coordinates and cluster-correction thresholds. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion and reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity that reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., alcohol imagery > neutral imagery) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain results, but the cue modality is personalized audiotaped imagery (auditory/imaginal scripts), not visual stimuli. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts present), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results / whole-brain analyses reported), I6 (voxelwise results are reported in main text/tables/figures), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength [3T], preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion ID not met: I3 (requires a clear visual cue component — visual-only or multimodal including visual cues). No exclusion criteria were triggered (no E3–E6 met). Therefore the study is excluded because it lacks the required visual cue component (I3). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high- and low-calorie food images vs. objects). It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie foods>objects; low-calorie foods>objects). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed using SPM8 with small-volume correction (a priori ROIs) and FWE correction reported, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results. Results are reported in the text and quantified via percent signal change and ROI peak coordinates. Participant demographics (female, ages 19–28), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli and includes a within-participant smoking>neutral contrast (I3 and I4 satisfied). The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses; however, the smoking cue > neutral effect was reported only at P<0.005 uncorrected and explicitly did NOT survive correction for multiple comparisons. No whole-brain- or small-volume-corrected voxelwise cue>control result is presented for the cue-reactivity contrast, so inclusion criterion I5 is not met. I7 (reporting of participant/scan/preprocessing details) is satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Because the review requires at least one qualifying (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) voxelwise cue>control result, this study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of methamphetamine cue-reactivity using visual pictorial cues in a within-subject, placebo-controlled design. The primary contrast reported is Methamphetamine Cue>Control Cue (within-participant), and the paper reports whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise BOLD results (Z-statistic maps, cluster thresholds, and supplementary tables of coordinates). Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are provided. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (visual cues, within-participant cue>control contrast, group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported, acceptable reporting of results in main text/supplement, and participant/method details). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (highly palatable vs. moderately palatable, and moderate vs. neutral). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (explicitly states whole-brain analyses were conducted and reports cluster-corrected results and supporting information tables), and voxelwise results are available in Supporting Information. Participant demographics and cue types are reported; MRI acquisition and processing details are referenced in Supporting Information. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical BOLD fMRI investigation of smoking (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli and a validated visual cue task. It reports a within-participant CUE>neutral contrast (abstinence vs. satiety; CUE>neutral) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with multiple-comparison correction (results for ACC reported whole-brain corrected and cluster-corrected). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and statistical software (FSL), participant age/sex, and cue type. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical).

This study reports an fMRI experiment with clear visual cigarette cues and within-participant cue contrasts (meets I3 and I4). However, all reported statistical results appear to be ROI-based (a priori anatomically defined ROIs and beta-parameter comparisons); the paper does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results required for inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Exclusion criteria applied: E3.

Study uses visual drug cues in an fMRI MID task and reports whole-brain and ROI voxelwise group results (with coordinates), and provides participant and acquisition/preprocessing details, so it satisfies I3, I5, I6, and I7. However, the manuscript does not report a within‑participant contrast of drug cues > control (neutral) stimuli in the standard cue‑reactivity sense. The primary within‑subject contrasts are premature>correct within incentive contexts and group comparisons (including drug vs money interactions), but no qualifying within‑participant drug‑cue > control‑cue contrast is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (no accompanying qualifying within‑participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of visual smoking cues with within-subject smoking>control comparisons (meets I3 and I4) and reports participant demographics, cue type, field strength, and preprocessing details (meets I7). However, the analyses are ROI-based and the paper explicitly used an ROI approach rather than reporting any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. No voxelwise statistical maps or small-volume-corrected coordinates are provided, so it fails I5. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise results).

This fMRI study investigates appetitive (natural reward: liquid food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (pictures) and reports within-subject CS+ > CS− contrasts. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed in SPM12 with small-volume correction (amygdala, NAcc, vmPFC) and reported peak coordinates and corrected p-values, satisfying voxelwise result reporting. Participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective (natural reward visual cue reactivity) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food and sexual images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (food > baseline; sexual scenes > baseline) and uses group-level voxelwise whole-brain regression analyses (with reported coordinates and thresholds) in addition to ROI analyses. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening.

Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3—this is an fMRI study using clear visual cues (cigarette and food images); I5—group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (whole-brain analyses with correction/SVC); I6—voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables/supplement; I7—participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Inclusion criterion not met: I4—there is no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (neutral) stimuli or natural reward cues > control stimuli. The reported contrasts focus on regulation (LATER vs NOW) and on cigarette vs food comparisons, but the study did not include or report a drug>neutral cue contrast required by I4. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because I4 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (216 food and nonfood images). The authors report within-subject contrasts of food>nonfood across three sleep conditions and present group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results with small-volume correction (SVC) within a priori ROIs, including peak coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values. Voxelwise coordinates and statistical thresholds are reported in the main text/figures/tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines visual alcohol cues (alcoholic beverage images) vs non-alcohol beverage control images presented concurrently with emotional IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-subject voxelwise contrasts comparing alcohol versus non-alcohol cues (e.g., ‘alcoholic versus non-alcoholic beverage cues paired with positive images’ and vice versa) and reports group-level voxelwise statistical maps with family-wise error correction and cluster thresholds (whole-brain corrected results, tables/figures). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of e-cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (images of the e-cigarettes) and reports within-participant contrasts comparing conditioned (sweet-, nicotine-, sweet+nicotine-paired) cues to control/unexposed cues. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction (p SVC values for NAcc) and whole-brain corrected correlations, satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue types (sight and smell of e-cigarettes), MRI field strength (Siemens 3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), meeting reporting expectations. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task study of natural-reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of spicy vs non-spicy foods). The study reports within-participant contrasts (spicy food > non-spicy food) entered into group-level random-effects analyses and reports voxelwise whole-brain results corrected for multiple comparisons (p < 0.05, FWE; cluster threshold k>20) with peak coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing pipeline and SPM12 statistical software. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrast) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses fMRI to examine neural responses to visual reward-predictive cues (monetary reward) and includes within-participant contrasts of rewarded (A+, B+) versus nonrewarded (C–, D–) stimuli. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical analyses are reported (thresholded T values and cluster-size correction, p<.05 corrected), with activation maps and regional results described in the main text, satisfying voxelwise reporting. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast: A+/B+ vs C-/D-), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I6 (results available in main text). No exclusion criteria apply. Note: I7 (reporting of MRI field strength and some preprocessing details) is not fully documented in the provided excerpt (field strength not explicit), but this is a preferred, not mandatory, criterion.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual smoking-related and affective images and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking>neutral, positive>neutral, negative>neutral) entered into random-effects group analyses. Group-level voxelwise results are reported (interaction in left middle frontal gyrus with MNI coordinates and cluster-corrected significance), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked result. Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, 1.5T field strength, SPM8 preprocessing). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cue reactivity using a block-design visual task (food vs neutral). It reports within-participant contrasts (food>neutral) and group-level voxelwise results: an ROI small-volume-corrected analysis in the ventral striatum (FWE-corrected) and an exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected 1-sample t test. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing in SPM5) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli tailored to participants’ drug of dependence. Methods report within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral cues at the first level and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with whole-brain cluster correction (coordinates and clusters reported). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, AFNI’s 3dClustSim) and participant demographics are provided. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (visual photographs) and multimodal (visual + auditory) design. The study reports within-participant contrasts of high-energy-dense (high-ED) > low-ED food cues for visual and auditory modalities (e.g., fed visual high-ED > fed visual low-ED), satisfying the cue>control contrast requirement. Group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed and reported with whole-brain thresholding, cluster correction (Monte Carlo/3dClustSim) and reported supra-threshold clusters/coordinates, meeting the whole-brain voxelwise evidence requirement. Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be included.

This study used a gustatory (taste) cue-exposure paradigm (alcohol taste vs. litchi juice control) rather than visual cues. Although it includes a within-participant alcohol>control contrast (I4) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (I5) with results available in text/tables/figures (I6) and provides participant/cue/MRI/preprocessing details (I7), it fails inclusion criterion I3 (clear visual cue component). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to visual cue-reactivity studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues and reports within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral. Methods describe group-level voxelwise (random-effects second-level) analyses with whole-brain thresholding (p<0.001, cluster ≥10) and report regional activations in tables and figures (coordinates provided). MRI field strength (1.5 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. Participant characteristics (age eligibility, smoking history, n=20) and cue type (ISIS smoking vs neutral images) are provided. Although sex breakdown is not explicitly stated in the provided text, omission of a single demographic detail does not preclude inclusion per I7. All primary inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol and soft-drink images in alcohol-dependent patients. The paper includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol versus control stimuli (e.g., [alcohol pull > soft drink pull] and ([alcohol pull > alcohol push] > [soft drink pull > soft drink push])). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with small-volume correction (FWE SVC) in the mPFC and NAcc, with coordinates and statistical values given in the main text (and whole-brain results reported in supplementary material). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), cue type, and participant sex are reported. The full article text (methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies with qualifying voxelwise results.

This is an fMRI task-based study using visual backward-masked cues (cocaine and sexual images) in human participants. It reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine vs. neutral; sex vs. neutral) and group-level voxelwise SPM results with cluster- and peak-level statistics and MNI coordinates. Visual stimuli are the primary cue modality. Methods report participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and SPM2 analysis parameters. Voxelwise task-evoked results are presented in text/figures and described with thresholds and corrected p-values, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected evidence. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it uses individualized script-driven imagery (auditory/internal imagery) rather than a visual cue component required by the meta-analysis. It does meet I4 (within-participant alcohol cue > neutral contrasts were analyzed), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported with whole-brain correction), I6 (voxelwise results and coordinates/figures/tables available), and I7 (participant demographics and methodological details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cues with visual stimuli and reports seed-based PPI task-dependent connectivity results (VTA connectivity changes) but does not present a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise activation contrast (high-calorie cue > control) at the group level within this manuscript. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without also reporting a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cue paradigm) and I7 (participant and MRI details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control activation contrast reported in this full text) and I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation result/whole-brain or SVC reported here). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is not an fMRI study: the paper reports pupillometry (eye-tracking) cue-reactivity data and does not include any MRI data, task-evoked voxelwise group-level or small-volume-corrected results. Therefore it fails key fMRI-specific inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast: alcohol vs neutral cues) and I7 (reports participant age/sex and cue type). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (functional MRI study) and I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (HiCal>Control, LoCal>Control, Food>Control) and group-level voxelwise results using SPM8 with small-volume correction (ROI mask) and MNI coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual Pavlovian cues (colored lights on a vending machine) paired with natural rewards (snack foods), and includes within-participant contrasts of CS+ > CS− (general PIT) and specific PIT contrasts. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (FWE-corrected) with peak coordinates and provides results online (NeuroVault), and details MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise results. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food pictures (natural reward) vs scrambled control images in a within-subjects design. It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts of food>control and task-evoked group-level results, including a small-volume-corrected (hypothalamus, pFWE-corr) voxelwise analysis and whole-brain exploratory results. Participant details and MRI methods are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity (I3), within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), and availability of group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (I5), with results available in text/figures (I6) and sufficient reporting of sample and MRI details (I7). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related visual cues (food images) with within-participant contrasts (hedonic foods > utilitarian foods; utilitarian foods > neutral objects). Group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed (whole-brain analyses with FDR correction reported) and ROI analyses supplement these results. MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2), participant age/sex, and cue types are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity study comparing alcohol dependence (AD) and internet gaming disorder (IGD). It does not include any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm or presentation of visual drug/natural reward cues, nor does it report any within-participant cue>control contrasts or group-level task-evoked voxelwise results. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only seed-based/connectivity/resting-state analyses without task-evoked results) and E5 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (the paper reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result), I6 (not applicable — no task-evoked voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of a natural reward (chocolate) using visual cues (chocolate pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts (chocolate vs neutral pictures) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain regression analyses (cluster-level corrected, Monte Carlo simulation) with reported Talairach coordinates and cluster sizes. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager) are described. Thus all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity voxelwise results are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original task-based fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using visual stimuli (International Smoking Image Series). It reports within-subject contrasts (smoking cue > neutral cue) with group-level voxelwise results (FDR-corrected whole-brain analyses, reported in text/figures/tables). Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), satisfying reporting expectations. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core article content present). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes a within-participant cue>control contrast). Therefore the study meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.
