This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts of food>baseline (pre- and post-meal) as well as group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results across groups. The methods describe voxelwise GLM analyses, statistical thresholds, and group comparisons (e.g., DEL vs HWC, UPD vs HWC, DEL vs UPD) with reported brain regions, meeting the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of reward-related cue processing using visual MID task cues (satisfies I3) and includes within-participant contrasts of win>neutral (satisfies I4). Participant/sample and methodological details are reported (satisfies I7). However, the manuscript reports ROI-based analyses (extracting BOLD from predefined striatal ROIs) and hypothesis tests on those ROI values; although whole-brain contrast images were computed to extract ROI values, the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical maps or coordinate tables/cluster results that would qualify under I5. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no qualifying voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying voxelwise group-level results) and I6 (no indication that qualifying voxelwise results are available in tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete.  Exclusion met: E3. Inclusion met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion not met: I5, I6.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural (food) reward cue-reactivity using visual Pavlovian cues (black-and-white patterns). It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts of food-outcome cues versus a no-outcome control cue and compatible>incompatible cue-response contrasts. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction (e.g., vmPFC cluster surviving SVC FWE P<0.05) and peak coordinates, meeting the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This article is a symposium-style summary reporting human laboratory studies (IV alcohol self-administration, cortisol, taste tests, and a clinical latent-class analysis of childhood trauma). Although it briefly references an fMRI investigation, the full text does not present an original fMRI task methods or task-evoked voxelwise results (no within-participant visual cue>control contrasts, no whole-brain or SVC voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables related to visual cue-reactivity). Therefore it fails to meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 (and I6 — no qualifying voxelwise results in text/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) directly apply beyond failure to satisfy the required inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for the article type (not truncated).

The study uses a monetary incentive delay (MID) fMRI task with visual monetary cues (natural reward-related visual stimuli). It computes within-participant cue contrasts (e.g., gain versus no-gain anticipation GVNant and no-loss versus loss NVLout), and performs/ reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses for these contrasts (noting whole-brain results are presented in the Supplementary Results/Figures), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked group-level results. Required study details (participants, cue type, MRI parameters, preprocessing/software) are reported. ROI analyses are present but are complemented by whole-brain voxelwise analyses, so the study is not ROI-only. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images (meets I3) and includes within-participant food>control contrasts entered into second-level analyses (meets I4). Participant/sample and MRI details are reported (female dieters, 3T scanner, preprocessing with SPM8), satisfying I7. However, the manuscript reports results primarily as ROI- and system-averaged ROI analyses (VS, OFC, and aggregated network ROIs) and ANOVAs on extracted beta values. I find no reported group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical voxelwise results (no cluster coordinates or SVC results presented for task-evoked contrasts). Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and fails the required I5 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED due to E3; inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7; unmet: I5.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related pictures). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking vs. neutral pictures (cue>control) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (2×2 ANOVA and planned t-tests) with FWE-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables. Voxelwise results are provided in tables/figures and described in the text. Core content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text; supplementary details are noted but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical task-evoked fMRI data are reported). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of hedonic food images > nonfood objects, and group-level voxelwise whole-brain random-effects results with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds and coordinate tables. Relevant methodological details (participant ages/sex, cue type, 3.0T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

The study reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results contrasting substance-free activity images (natural reward) versus neutral control images (within-participant contrasts: [reward]-[non-reward] and [win]-[non-win]). Visual cues are the primary stimuli (AID task), and results are reported from whole-brain FLAME analyses with cluster thresholding and anatomical localization; supplementary materials are referenced. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (7T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise results and reported details.

This fMRI study examines natural (food) reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (Willingness to Pay task), with a within-participant contrast of high palatable food > plain food. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation results (one-sample t-tests across participants for the contrasts) used to define ROIs and nodes for connectivity analyses; such voxelwise results are described in the main text and likely detailed in supplementary materials. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it meets the review’s criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and qualifying voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual food images, with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs objects, low-calorie vs objects, high vs low). Although primary analyses include ROI averages, the paper also reports an exploratory whole-brain mixed-effects voxelwise analysis with cluster correction (FSL; Z=2.3, cluster P<0.05) identifying significant clusters associated with BMI z-score change. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), and I6 (voxelwise results presented in main text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of food cues > nonfood control cues (food vs. nonfood) in a randomized cross-over design. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results from a whole-brain analysis (drink x cue interaction showing significant visual cortex effects, thresholded and cluster-corrected) and also reports ROI analyses (left OFC, ventral striatum). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the paper reports only ROI-based analyses and uses extracted parameter estimates rather than presenting any group-level voxelwise, whole-brain, or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results (meets exclusion criterion E3). Included criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images), I4 (within-participant Food > Non-Food contrast was computed), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and software are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the manuscript does not report at least one qualifying group-level voxelwise result (whole-brain or SVC-corrected) or coordinate table/figure showing such task-evoked activations for Food>Control. Therefore it must be excluded per the review criteria.

This empirical fMRI study assesses natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie food pictures vs. brick walls) with within-subject contrasts. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures of results, and provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software details. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking-related video cues (meets review objective). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking videos > control videos and reports group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (FLAME, permutation-based TFCE correction, P<0.05) with reported activations and supplementary tables/figures. The methods report participant age/sex, 3T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/Matlab), satisfying reporting preferences. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; VBM/TBSS and connectivity analyses are present but do not replace the qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical BOLD-fMRI study of smokers using visual smoking cues (pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts comparing smoking versus neutral pictures (LCSP minus LCNP). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain results and coordinates, e.g., dACC coordinates and Z values) and whole-brain correlation analyses. MRI field strength (3 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5), participant age/sex, and cue type are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Inclusion justified for meta-analysis of visual drug-cue reactivity.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using clearly visual food-video stimuli. The study includes within-participant contrasts of food video (FV) > control video epochs and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results using SPM2 with family-wise error correction (voxel-level FWE P<0.05) and cluster reporting; coordinates are referenced (Table 2). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and tests within-subject contrasts of food stimuli (FS) versus nonfood control (FN), meeting the cue>control requirement. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (ROI-based inference with FDR small-volume correction in anatomically defined ROIs), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. The paper reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM2). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (International Smoking Image Series). It includes within-participant contrasts (smoking > neutral) at the first level and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses with voxelwise threshold p<0.005 and cluster extent correction, reported clusters/tables). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM12), satisfying reporting preferences. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related film cues in amphetamine-dependent patients. It reports a within-subject contrast Drug movies > Neutral movies with group-level voxelwise results (whole-brain FWE-corrected activations) and also reports ROI analyses; MRI field strength (3T), participant demographics (age, all male), cue type (films), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual reward cues (images of a $100 bill vs a blurry rectangle) and reports within-participant contrasts of reward > nonreward (main effect of reward). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (cluster-corrected threshold z>3.1, p<.05) with coordinates/figures and adequate methodological details (age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study that assesses natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using clearly visual stimuli (actual food items presented visually). It includes within-participant contrasts of food > non-food cues across three physiological states (Wtinitial, Wt–10%placebo, Wt–10%leptin). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (voxelwise thresholding, tables/figures of peak coordinates; hypothalamus ROI/small-volume confirmation is also performed). Core methodological details are provided (participant sex, BMI; MRI field strength 1.5T; preprocessing/statistics using SPM2), meeting reporting preferences. No exclusion criteria are triggered: the paper is not ROI-only (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported), not connectivity/resting-state-only, and contains qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-subject contrasts. The paper reports group-level voxelwise SPM99 analyses (high-calorie > control, low-calorie > control, conjunctions, and subtraction contrasts) with statistical thresholds and coordinate tables; some results survive whole-brain correction. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high- vs low-caloric food images). It reports within-participant contrasts (high-caloric > low-caloric) and group-level voxelwise results with whole-brain cluster-level FWE correction. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for visual cue-based task-evoked voxelwise analyses and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual smoking video cues and reports task-evoked voxelwise results for the smoking > neutral contrast. It includes a within-participant contrast (smoking > neutral), whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with reported peak coordinates/z-statistics) and ROI follow-up, and reports key methodological details (participant ages, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software: FSL). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual natural reward stimuli (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food cues versus control (nature scenes). The authors generated subject-level food>control contrast images and submitted them to a second-level (group) voxelwise analysis (group T-map), and also report small-volume ROI analyses of the IFG; therefore qualifying group-level voxelwise results are indicated. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes a within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI task including alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage pictures (visual cue component) and computed linear contrasts between regressors of interest (including alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages) at the individual level. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using AFNI (3dMVM) and whole-brain correction (3dClustSim) is described; alcohol-related whole-brain results are reported as variable and referenced in Supplementary Table T1, indicating availability of group-level voxelwise task-evoked results for alcohol cues. Participant demographics (female, age range), MRI field strengths (3T scanners), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual food cues (food vs nonfood images) and reports within-participant task contrasts (food>nonfood) across timepoints. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (flexible factorial and two-sample t tests, voxelwise thresholds, cluster statistics, tables/figures), and small-volume/ROI analyses for the hypothalamus are also provided. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (visual food images), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), satisfying reporting preferences. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes task-evoked voxelwise results; includes within-participant contrasts; is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI task study comparing within-participant responses to high-calorie taste cues versus water (natural reward-related cue>control contrast), reporting whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (cluster-corrected maps and peak locations). Although the primary sensory modality is gustatory, the design includes a visual component (on-screen instructions concurrent with cue delivery), making it a multimodal cue-reactivity study with a clear visual cue element. The paper provides necessary methodological details (3T scanner, preprocessing with FSL/FEAT, TR/TE, participant age range, cue types) and reports PPI connectivity as a secondary analysis but also includes task-evoked voxelwise contrasts required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (food pictures: high-calorie, low-calorie, non-food) addressing natural reward-related cue-reactivity (food). It includes within-subject, within-participant contrasts (food vs. non-food and high- vs. low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain FWE-corrected findings and ROI/SVC analyses (coordinates, tables, and figures referenced). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistics (SPM12, details provided), and participant demographics. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, presents task-evoked within-participant contrasts). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues and within-subject smoking cue>neutral contrasts (meets I3 and I4). Results include voxelwise group-level activations reported as coordinates in the main text (meets I6), and participant/MRI details and preprocessing software are reported (meets I7). However, all voxelwise analyses were conducted only within an ROI mask and statistical thresholds are reported as uncorrected (k=20, p<0.001) with no small-volume correction or whole-brain corrected results. Therefore the study does not provide a qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result (I5 not met) and falls under exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI-restricted results with no qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected evidence). Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I6, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual video cues (explicit sexual, erotic, non-sexual exciting, money, neutral). It includes within-subject contrasts of natural reward-related cues (explicit sexual) versus control (exciting) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain FWE-corrected activations and small-volume-corrected ROI results) with coordinates and p-values. Participant age/sex, cue types, task design, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported in the text; MRI acquisition parameters are referenced. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used visual erotic videos as natural reward cues (sexual stimuli), includes within-participant contrasts of sexual activation vs neutral (paired t-tests), and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (SPM8 voxelwise contrasts with activation maps and MNI coordinates, reporting clusters >20 voxels). Key methodological details are reported (participant ages/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software), satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, and is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion: E3 applies — the study reports only an ROI-based analysis (mean beta values from 5-mm spheres) and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results for the qualifying contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of a natural reward — food — with clear visual cue stimuli) and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues > control stimuli is reported in the paper’s results — contrasts reported are between portion-size/ED conditions rather than cue>control), and I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results are provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity that used visual cue exposure (participants held and viewed a cigarette via live video) and a control cue (roll of tape). The analysis includes within-participant contrasts (cigarette vs. control) entered into group-level voxelwise GLMs and a 2×2 ANOVA, with Monte Carlo cluster correction; results are reported as whole-brain coordinates in tables and figures. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (AFNI, FSL, etc.), participant age/sex, and cue type are provided. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with within-subject contrasts (high-energy vs. neutral; low-energy vs. neutral; high vs. low). Group-level voxelwise analyses were reported using whole-brain FDR correction (P<0.05) and cluster-level results; imaging acquisition (3T), preprocessing (DPARSF) and analysis software (SPM12) are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI visual cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise results.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cue-reactivity. It includes within-participant contrasts of hedonic food images > non-food control images (H>O) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FDR-corrected) as well as small-volume ROI analyses. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3.0T MRI, SPM5 preprocessing/statistics) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies of natural reward-related cue-reactivity.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (page shows loading/error message). Cannot verify core methods/results. Inclusion criteria not demonstrably met: I3 (uncertain whether visual cue component is present), I4 (no confirmation of within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5/I6 (no confirmation of whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results available), I7 (participant and MRI details cannot be verified). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) can be confirmed from the incomplete content. Because essential information required to determine eligibility is missing, I exclude the study pending access to the full article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using validated visual food images. It reports within-participant contrasts of fattening food versus objects (cue>control) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: ROI-based analyses with cluster-level FWE correction across predefined ROIs (small-volume-corrected) and exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Behavioral intake was linked to postmeal voxelwise activation. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (including fMRI paradigm, acquisition, processing, and statistical correction), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of smoking that includes visual smoking images and reports task-evoked, group-level voxelwise results for an interoception task and resting-state seed connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (smoking cue images used in a Smoking Pleasantness task), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported for the Interoceptive Attention task), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI, and software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 — there is no within-participant voxelwise contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (no smoking-cue>neutral cue fMRI contrast reported; the SP task produced behavioral pleasantness ratings but no cue-reactivity voxelwise activation map). No exclusion criteria from the review list (E3–E6) are directly triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires a within-subject cue>control task-evoked voxelwise contrast, this study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual stimuli (hedonic food images) with a within-participant contrast (hedonic food > non-food objects). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with corrected cluster thresholds, and a small-volume-corrected ROI analysis is also presented. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, 3.0T field strength, preprocessing with SPM5) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual erotic vs. neutral pictures. It includes within-subject contrasts (placebo/erotic > placebo/neutral; GHB/neutral > placebo/neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (threshold p<.001, k>15) as well as small-volume (FWE) corrected ROI results with coordinates. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of visual food cues (natural reward) using a within-participant high-calorie food > nonfood contrast, with group-level voxelwise analyses within predefined ROIs and family-wise error correction reported for insula clusters (coordinates and figures provided). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing software (SPM5), and methods are reported and the full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets I3 (visual natural reward cue-reactivity), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume/FWE correction), I6 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures), and I7 (participant and MRI details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study uses visual methamphetamine cue pictures (I3), implements a within-participant Methamphetamine Cue > Control Cue contrast at the subject level and reports group-level analyses (I4), and reports whole-brain cluster-corrected voxelwise results with coordinates (Z>2.3, p<.05) satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting (I5). Results are presented in figures/tables and described in text (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes the required within-participant cue>control contrast rather than only between-group contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI work. Full article core content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore, the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity.

The full text reports an fMRI task using visual smoking and matched neutral images (I3). Analyses include within-participant contrasts of smoking>neutral (I4). A group-level voxelwise analysis restricted to the PCC was performed with cluster-level correction using nonparametric permutation testing (z=3.1, p<0.05), which satisfies the requirement for a whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise result (I5). Relevant voxelwise results are presented in figures/supplementary materials (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported in Methods (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only (it includes voxelwise PCC analysis), not limited to connectivity or resting-state analyses, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural (sexual) reward cue processing using visual erotic stimuli and reports group-level voxelwise results (Tables and SVC FWE-corrected findings). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise results reported, SVC FWE corrected), I6 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures), and I7 (participant demographics and methodological details reported). However, the paper does not present a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control stimuli (e.g., erotic>neutral) or an equivalent cue>control task contrast. Analyses focus on parametric modulation by subjective value and delay, and on between-group comparisons/interactions, but no qualifying within-subject cue>control contrast is reported. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (only between-group contrasts/parametric effects without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Consequently the study must be excluded from this cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

While this fMRI study examines visual natural reward cues (food) and reports group-level voxelwise and small-volume-corrected task-evoked results, it does not present a clear within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., food cues > neutral/control stimuli) as required by the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. The primary reported analyses center on parametric (amplitude-modulation) relationships between pleasantness ratings and BOLD activation and group-by-CRP interactions, rather than an explicit within-subject cue>control contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise/small-volume-corrected results), I6 (results reported in main text/tables), and I7 (participant and acquisition details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) explicitly apply. Because I4 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with visual cues signaling potential monetary wins (natural reward-related cues). It reports within-participant contrasts of WinMoney > WinZero (WinMoney-WinZero) and WinMoney-only versus baseline, and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain thresholded maps described at p < .0001, k > 150) alongside ROI analyses. Participant demographics (age range, sex handling), cue type (monetary Win cues), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software (AFNI/FSL/SPM8) are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual food images (natural reward cues) with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie food images > objects) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses outside ROIs, cluster-corrected and reported with peak coordinates and figures/tables). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FreeSurfer, ANTs), participant ages/sex, and cue types are reported. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain/small-volume-corrected results), I6 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), and I7 (key methodological details reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cues (monetary gains/losses) using explicit visual cues (colored circles predicting outcomes), with within-participant contrasts (anticipation/delivery of gains vs losses and cue vs baseline reported). Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted with small-volume correction within prefrontal/limbic masks and ROI analyses; results are reported with coordinates and figures/tables. Key methodological details (age/sex, cue type, 3T field strength, AFNI preprocessing/statistics) are provided. The study therefore meets the meta-analysis scope (natural reward cue-reactivity with visual stimuli) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7. It does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; reports voxelwise SVC results and within-participant contrasts). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-cue pictures and a within-participant drug-related vs. neutral contrast. Group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests of the drug>neutral contrast; main effects thresholded at p < .05 FWE corrected) and whole-brain exploratory results and coordinates/figures are provided. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (pictures and videos) with matched neutral control stimuli. The authors computed within-participant contrasts of smoking>control (e.g., BEGIN S2-T2, END S4-T4) and performed group-level voxelwise second-level analyses, reporting activations/deactivations in tables and figures. ROI analyses were performed with small-volume correction procedures; MRI field strength (1.5 T), preprocessing steps, and software (SPM5) are described, and participant demographics/groups are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

Full text presents an empirical fMRI study using visual-only smoking-related videos (satisfies I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of smoking vs. non-smoking videos (smoke>non-smoke) with corresponding group-level voxelwise statistical results (whole-brain analyses using FSL/FLAME1, cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05), satisfying I4 and I5. Results are reported in the main text, figures, and supplementary tables (I6). Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL 5.0.9) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-participant cue>control contrasts, and are original human fMRI data (so E3–E6 do not apply). The provided full text contains intro, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual food stimuli and within-participant food>nonfood contrasts. The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise food vs. nonfood results (figures/brain maps from Day 1; display threshold p<0.001, cluster size reported) used to identify local maxima and ROIs, satisfying a whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, SAS) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) cues and includes within-participant contrasts (mSEX > neutral; mSEX > aversive). Group-level voxelwise results are reported: small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (FWE pcorr < 0.05) with peak coordinates (Table 1) and an exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected activation (right inferior occipital gyrus). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply.

Study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical fMRI investigation of drug (cigarette) cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (participants held and viewed a cigarette via a live video feed) and uses within-participant contrasts (cigarette cue > control cue). Analyses were conducted at the group level using voxel-wise, two-level random-effects GLM and whole-brain inference with cluster-wise correction (AFNI AlphaSim), and results (cue effects and ambivalence-related voxelwise correlations) are reported in the main text/tables, satisfying requirements for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected task-evoked voxelwise results. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual cues (written labels). It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts comparing labeled reward cues versus control/neutral cues (e.g., high-calorie > neutral, low-calorie > neutral; and low vs high), with group-level whole-brain analyses reported (cluster-level FWE correction). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI acquisition and preprocessing, and analysis software are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only or connectivity-only results; results include qualifying task-evoked voxelwise, within-subject contrasts). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic stimuli (natural reward), reporting voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses and peak coordinates, and providing participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (meets I3, I5, I6, I7). However, the full text does not report any within-participant cue>control (e.g., erotic>rest or erotic>neutral) contrast results; the reported analyses focus on contrasts between two cue types (male>female and female>male). Inclusion criterion I4 (at least one within-participant cue>control contrast) is not satisfied based on the provided text. No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met. Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting I4.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) film excerpts contrasted with emotionally neutral film excerpts (within-participant erotic>neutral contrast). Group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (SPM99 random-effects, two-sample and one-sample t-tests) are reported with thresholding and coordinates in tables/figures (whole-brain analyses and ROI-based uncorrected results are presented). Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue type, 1.5T MRI field strength, preprocessing and SPM software). Therefore it meets I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures), and I7 (participant and MRI/method details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic video stimuli (natural reward) with a within-subject erotic>non-erotic contrast at the group level. The paper reports whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and provides MNI coordinates and cluster sizes (qualifying voxelwise results). Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and provides qualifying group-level voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts, empirical task-evoked fMRI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of favorite-food (natural reward) cue-reactivity with whole-brain voxelwise results, but the paradigm used personalized guided-imagery auditory scripts rather than visual cues. It therefore fails the meta-analysis requirement for a visual cue component. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts: favorite-food vs neutral and stress vs neutral), I5 (whole-brain FWE-corrected voxelwise results), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/tables/figures), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/stat software). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (requires visual cue component — study used auditory guided imagery only). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Consequently the study should be excluded from the visual-stimuli cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of high- and low-calorie foods). The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing high-calorie versus low-calorie food cues (e.g., snack go > vegetable go) and nogo>go contrasts, with group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Z>2.3, cluster p<0.05 corrected). Results are reported in tables/figures with MNI coordinates and ROI follow-ups. Methods report participant age/sex, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) and control (neutral/disgust) stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts of erotic > neutral and erotic > disgust (I4 satisfied) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain analyses and voxel-level correction (I5 satisfied). The paradigm is visual-only and thus meets the visual cue requirement (I3). The paper describes voxelwise results in the main text and (implicitly) in figures/tables (I6 satisfied). Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported (I7 satisfied). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pornographic pictures). It contains within-subject contrasts comparing preferred (MF/FF) vs non-preferred (MM) pornographic cues, and reports group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction in the ventral striatum (FWE-corrected) and whole-brain cluster correction. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (7T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food) and includes within-subject contrasts of hedonic>neutral foods, and reports participant demographics and MRI details. However, all reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based (mean signal extracted per anatomically defined ROIs with Bonferroni correction). The paper does not report any group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result) and fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study with visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue contrast hedonic>neutral), I7 (reports age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete. Consequently, the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity that includes visual cue exposure (participants held a cigarette and a live video feed of their hand was shown), and reports within-participant contrasts comparing cigarette cue > control cue. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (main effect of cue and interaction effects) with coordinates and cluster thresholds (AFNI/AlphaSim), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, FSL, etc.). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes within-participant contrasts (available > non-available food; high-calorie > low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results: whole-brain t-tests and ROI analyses with small-volume FWE-corrected peaks (coordinates reported) for the availability contrast (e.g., ACC, OFC, caudate). Participants’ age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity studies using visual natural rewards.

This is a task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual-only stimuli (appetizing food images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food stimuli > baseline (Close + Far > fixation) and strategy contrasts (Far > Close). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (cluster thresholds determined with AlphaSim; coordinate tables referenced in Supplemental Tables S1–S8), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Relevant methodological details are provided (3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing, participant age/sex, cue type). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to natural (food) visual cues.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (erotic images and monetary pictograms) to assess cue-reactivity for natural (sexual) and monetary rewards. It reports within-participant contrasts (erotic cue > control and monetary cue > control) at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain results (coordinates and cluster-level corrected statistics are provided). MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM2), and participant demographics (age, sex) are reported. Results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food pictures in a within-subject, randomized double-blind crossover design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of Food-Go > Object-Go and tests interactions with prednisolone. Group-level voxelwise results are reported both as whole-brain analyses and as small-volume-corrected (SVC) ROI results (bilateral amygdala and right insula) meeting voxelwise SVC FWE thresholds. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, MRI field strength 3T, preprocessing and SPM12) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) and reports within-participant cue contrast (ADMIT_TASTY > ADMIT_NONTASTY) showing activation in ventral striatum, insula, and ventral PFC. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (REGULATE_TASTY vs ADMIT_TASTY with whole-brain FDR correction; ADMIT_TASTY vs ADMIT_NONTASTY reported with coordinates). Methods and participant details are provided (female participants, ages, 3T MRI, SPM5 preprocessing). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using explicit visual sexual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing sexual > neutral pictures (Sex LO > Neutral LO and Sex PC > Neutral PC). Group-level voxelwise results are reported: ROI-based small-volume-corrected analyses (anatomical masks, p < .05 FWE-corrected) and whole-brain analyses are available in the supplementary material. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cigarette (drug) cue-reactivity using visual smoking images (ISIS). The design includes within-participant contrasts (delay conditions: smoking cues vs control/neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise GLM results with cluster-level multiple-comparisons correction and Talairach coordinates (tables/figures). Preprocessing, field strength (3T), and analysis software (BrainVoyager) are described. Full article text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies with qualifying whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (sexual stimuli) with a clear visual cue component. It includes within-participant contrasts of preferred-sex versus nonpreferred-sex stimuli and analyses of preferred- and nonpreferred-stimuli versus baseline. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results with cluster-level correction (AlphaSim), and presents coordinate/cluster results. Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity/resting-state only, or only between-group contrasts without within-subject cue>control contrasts) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI visual natural-reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports ROI-based analyses (mean ROI z-scores in preselected regions) and group comparisons of these ROI values; no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical results (e.g., corrected voxelwise maps or coordinate tables/clusters) are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images), I4 (within-participant contrast of high-calorie > low-calorie food images), I7 (participant demographics and scanner/preprocessing details are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result provided), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in tables/coordinates/figures that would satisfy I5). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet I5 and instead falls under exclusion E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (subliminal sexual images) with within-subject contrasts (Sex vs Neutral; Sex vs Fixation). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (Sex vs Neu: cluster-corrected results, Z>2.3, p<.05), and small-volume-corrected ROI analyses in the NAcc are also provided. Participant demographics and scanning/preprocessing details are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain and SVC results), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main results/tables), and I7 (participant and MRI details provided). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (sexual) and monetary cue-conditioning using visual stimuli, and contains task-evoked voxelwise group-level results. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing Sexual and Monetary outcomes/stimuli to Neutral controls (e.g., Sexual>Neutral; Monetary>Neutral) and reports whole-brain cluster-corrected FWE results and small-volume-corrected (SVC FWE) ROI results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food > neutral images, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses with small-volume correction (ROI-based conjunction analysis and GLM in SPM5), and multivariate PLS results; coordinates/results are reported in tables/figures. Participant demographics (female, ages 18–40), cue type (food images), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (images of milkshake vs water). It includes within-participant contrasts of unpaired milkshake cue > unpaired tasteless cue, and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction and coordinates. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, MATLAB). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-evoked fMRI study in humans using visual erotic scenes (IAPS) as natural reward-related cues and neutral control pictures; it reports within-participant contrasts (erotic>neutral) in a crossover design. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain results are reported (erotic vs neutral, fearful vs neutral) with FWE-corrected statistics, and ROI small-volume-corrected results are also provided for VTA/NAcc/amygdala. The paper provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8), and stimulus/cue type. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study uses a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with explicit visual incentive cues (e.g., text cues “Win $5.00” vs “No Money at Stake”), providing a visual natural-reward-related cue component. It includes within-participant contrasts of large gain anticipation > neutral anticipation and large loss anticipation > neutral (satisfying a cue>control contrast). The manuscript reports group-level one-sample t-tests for task contrasts and refers to supplemental material (Table S1, Fig. S1) for task main effects, indicating voxelwise group-level results are available (meeting whole-brain/small-volume-corrected reporting and permissibility of supplemental-coordinate reporting). Participant and methodological details (age/sex, cue type, field strength, preprocessing/software) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) stimuli (videos and pictures) with within-participant contrasts of erotic > non-erotic stimuli. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed using SPM5 with whole-brain results reported (including FDR-corrected maps and thresholded statistical maps and cluster coordinates). Essential reporting details (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software) are provided. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity meta-analysis of visual natural rewards and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of desserts vs vegetables). It reports within-participant contrasts of appetitive food cues versus control stimuli (no-go/dessert > go/vegetable and no-go/dessert > baseline) and provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with ROI-based small-volume correction (T-maps thresholded and pFDR correction across ROIs). The manuscript includes necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using visual smoking-related versus neutral pictures (visual cues) in smokers and controls. It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking > neutral) including paired t-tests in smokers and a whole-brain 2×2 ANOVA (cue × group) with voxelwise group-level results (FWE-corrected clusters) reported. Core reporting details are present: participant age/sex, cue type (pictures), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, FSL). Voxelwise task-evoked results are presented as whole-brain corrected clusters and ROI analyses are secondary/exploratory. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). The authors performed within-participant contrasts comparing palatable foods to neutral foods and non-food items, and conducted group-level voxelwise analyses (multiple regressions) across the whole brain with family-wise error correction. They report a significant FWE-corrected cluster (right superior frontal gyrus) with coordinates and p-value, satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing and SPM8, participant characteristics (adolescents/young adults), and cue types. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) cues (static erotic pictures) with a within-subject design (erotic vs non-erotic contrasts). Group-level voxelwise analyses (ANOVA, post-hoc F-tests) were performed and reported with cluster-level FWE correction; coordinates and cluster statistics are provided. Methods report participant age/sex (19 healthy males, mean age 24), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high- and low-calorie food images vs. nonfood objects). It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie>object, low-calorie>object) in premeal and postmeal states. Group-level voxelwise GLM results are reported with Talairach coordinates, cluster thresholds, and whole-brain/FDR-corrected thresholds; results are extractable from text/figures. MRI field strength (4.0T), cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX, SPSS) are reported. Full article text with methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual methamphetamine-cue pictures (I3). The analysis includes within-participant contrasts comparing methamphetamine-cue blocks to rest baseline (methamphetamine task vs rest), meeting the required cue>control within-subject contrast (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results were performed and reported using SPM5 with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extent (group one-sample and two-sample t-tests; voxelwise T=3.11, P<.001, cluster>10 voxels), satisfying the whole-brain/small-volume-corrected evidence requirement (I5). Results are described in the main text and figures/tables are implied, consistent with allowance for reporting formats (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion, conclusion).

The study uses a Monetary Incentive Delay task with clear visual cues signaling gain vs neutral (natural reward-related visual cues). It reports a within-participant gain anticipation > neutral anticipation contrast, and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (one-sample and between-group permutation t-tests using TFCE) with activation maps and results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL FEAT, randomise, MATLAB) are reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrast, empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text provided is incomplete (only a website privacy/cookie notice). Cannot verify critical methodological details required by inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/unknown: I3 (unable to confirm this is an fMRI study with a clear visual cue component from the provided text), I4 (no confirmation of a within-participant cue>control contrast), I5/I6 (no evidence of group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results reported), I7 (participant demographics and MRI parameters not available). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 can be assessed from the incomplete content. Decision rationale: because the full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is missing, I cannot determine whether the study contains qualifying task-evoked voxelwise fMRI contrasts; therefore it cannot be included at this stage. Recommend obtaining the complete full text to reassess.

Although this fMRI study uses visual palatable-food cues (sweet/savory images) and reports task-evoked voxelwise results with small-volume correction, it does not include a within-participant cue>control (food>neutral or food>non-food) contrast. The primary within-subject contrasts reported are Enhance versus Regulate (both conditions use food images with different instructions), which does not meet the review’s required natural reward-related cue>control contrast (I4). Thus the study fails inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise small-volume-corrected results), I6 (results reported in main text/tables), I7 (participant/cue/MRI/preprocessing details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high- and low-calorie food images). It reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie vs. fixation; low-calorie vs. fixation; neutral vs. fixation), and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are presented with stereotaxic coordinates (e.g., right hippocampus coordinates and Brodmann area) from SPM5 analyses. ROI masks were defined with the WFU Pickatlas, and statistical thresholds/clusters are reported, meeting the requirement for small-volume/voxelwise reporting. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are provided. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only without voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural (food) reward cues using visual food images and includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie > low-calorie food images (HGo vs. LGo). However, the paper reports ROI-based analyses (parameter estimates extracted and averaged across predefined ROIs) for the reported correlations and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results in the main text. Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one qualifying voxelwise group-level result. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E3. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise group-level result reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic cues (videos and still images) as natural reward stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts of erotic vs. control (sport) stimuli in both block (video) and event-related (picture) designs. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses (fixed-effect voxel-wise group maps, thresholded and localized in Talairach space), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results. Participant demographics (age, male sex), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager 4.9, GLM) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) cues vs neutral control videos, with within-subject contrasts (erotic>neutral for both corresponding and opposite orientations). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM02) with tables/figures of coordinates and ROI small-volume analyses; preprocessing, scanner field strength (1.5T), participant ages/sex, cue types, and analysis software are all reported. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual package images as cues. The study reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., viewing regular package > healthier package; multiple package/taste contrasts) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain exploratory analyses and ROI-constrained voxelwise results with cluster-corrected thresholds and reported coordinates/cluster statistics). Visual cue component, participant details (age/sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual erotic film stimuli (visual-only cues). It includes within-subject contrasts of erotic films > neutral films across menstrual phases. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (mixed-effects FLAME stages 1+2) with cluster-based thresholding (Z>2.3, p<0.05 corrected), reporting activation maps/clusters, and results are described in the main text/figures. Key methodological details (participant sex/age, MRI field strength 3.0T, preprocessing/statistical software FSL) are provided. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI experiment with visual reward cues (MID task) and reports within-subject contrasts of reward anticipation (gain cues > ¥0). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain analyses and an a priori NAc ROI with FWE small-volume correction), and voxelwise results are presented in text/tables/figures. Participant/method details (age range, task cue types, MRI field strength, preprocessing software) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic video stimuli (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts of activation versus rest (EARLY/MID/LATE vs REST). Group-level voxelwise fixed-effects one-sample t-tests (p<0.05) are reported using SPM2, with whole-brain analyses and ROI labeling; core methods, results, and discussion are present. The study reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics software. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (natural rewards) presented during scanning (block design), satisfying the review’s focus on visual reward cue‐reactivity. It reports within-participant contrasts of sexual vs control stimuli (sex>neutral, sex>positive, sex>negative), meeting I4. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with voxel-level tests corrected for multiple comparisons (FWE) and small-volume corrections in ROIs (SMC/SVC), satisfying I5. The study clearly describes the visual cue type, participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), meeting I7. Reporting of peak voxels/conjunctions and figures/supplementary material is described, fulfilling I6. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with a within-participant contrast (food > non-food) analyzed at the group level using SPM8. Second-level paired t-tests (random effects) were performed and voxelwise results in a priori ROIs (insula) were reported with small-volume correction (p<.05). The methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant characteristics (men aged 18–60), and cue type (high- and low-calorie food pictures). Results are presented in text, figures, and tables. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food photographs) and measures cue-reactivity.
