It reports within-participant contrasts (fattening>object; non-fattening>object; fattening>non-fattening) and group-level voxelwise analyses using an ROI-based approach with cluster-thresholding (small-volume correction) across predefined anatomical masks. Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing and FSL statistical software). Results describe voxelwise clusters in amygdala, OFC, occipital cortex, etc., fulfilling the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met: it is not ROI-only without voxelwise results, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. Methods report within-participant contrasts (sexual vs neutral; sexual vs other rewards) and group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain and region-of-interest small-volume analyses) with coordinates and figures (supplementary tables referenced). MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, MarsBar) are reported; participant characteristics are provided. All required inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study using visual stimuli (graphic cigarette warning labels) related to a drug (tobacco) and assessing neural and behavioral responses. It includes within-participant contrasts of LABEL>CONTROL and HIGH>LOW, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and provides tables/figures of coordinate results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. Although the stimuli are aversive warning images rather than appetitive drug paraphernalia, they are clearly drug-related visual cues and modulate craving, fitting the review’s scope. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pornographic vs neutral pictures). It includes within-participant contrasts of explicit>neutral (explicit/neutral regressors at subject level) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses reported with cluster-level FWE correction and peak coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (3T Siemens), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), participant demographics (age, all male), and cue type. Results provide whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked findings and coordinate tables/figures and also acceptable PPI connectivity analyses. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; contains task-evoked voxelwise results; includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to visual natural rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI study (N=21) using visual erotic (natural reward) pictures and matched non-erotic control pictures with within-subject contrasts (e.g., bodily>non-bodily; positive bodily>positive non-bodily). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM2; FDR-corrected thresholds, cluster sizes, coordinates referenced), and parametric modulation analyses relate subjective ratings to BOLD. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue types, 1.5T MRI field, preprocessing and statistical software) are reported in Methods. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette cue-reactivity using visual smoking images in treatment-seeking smokers. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing smoking cues to neutral control images (LookSmoking > LookNeutral). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with whole-brain cluster correction (AlphaSim) and coordinate data shown in tables/figures; PPI connectivity analyses are also reported. The methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant demographics; the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria for task-evoked, visual cue fMRI analyses.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) with visual cues and within-participant contrasts (high-/low-energy food > object), meeting I3 and I4, and participant/method details reported (I7). However, the paper reports ROI/fROI-based analyses (average BOLD within a priori functional ROIs defined from a separate cohort) rather than reporting any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps/results for the current sample. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result). Inclusion criterion I5 (group-level voxelwise or SVC result) is not met. Full text appears complete.

The study uses visual erotic films (sexual stimuli) as natural reward-related cues and reports within-subject contrasts (Disgust vs Rest) at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain analysis with coordinates and cluster thresholds. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2/Matlab) are reported. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of high- and low-energy foods). The study reports within-participant cue contrasts (nogo_dessert vs rest and nogo_vegetable vs rest) and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses reported at p=0.001, k=8) with reported peak regions/tables, satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, DARTEL) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study includes a within-participant Food > Activities contrast (cue>control), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (p<0.001 uncorrected with cluster-level FWE p<0.05) with tables/figures of significant clusters, and provides participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Full text content provided is only a website privacy/cookie notice; core article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is missing. I cannot verify whether the study used fMRI with visual reward cues (I3), included a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), or reported voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results (I5/I6). Therefore none of the required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) can be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on the available content. Recommend obtaining the complete article PDF to re-screen.

This is an fMRI study of milkshake (gustatory) consumption and stress imagery. While it includes a within-participant contrast of natural reward (milkshake) > control (tasteless) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results using SPM5 at 3T (satisfying I4, I5, I6, I7), it does not include a visual cue component. Stimuli were taste deliveries via gustometer and auditory imagery scripts; no visual reward-related cues (visual-only or multimodal including visual cues) are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (clear visual cue component) required by the meta-analysis, and must be excluded. Exclusion IDs met: none (study excluded for not meeting I3).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cigarette-related stimuli (FDA graphic vs non-graphic warning labels) and measures cue-evoked craving. It includes within-participant contrasts (graphic > non-graphic and graphic > baseline), reports group-level voxelwise results with coordinates and cluster-level correction, and conducts a priori ROI (small-volume) analyses with corrected statistics. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/software (FSL), and participant age/sex. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual food cues (personal food images) as natural reward stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts comparing Picture versus Word and Picture+Word versus Word, i.e., cue>control contrasts, and presents whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with cluster-level correction (AlphaSim). Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis objective and all inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical).

The study is an fMRI intertemporal decision (delay-discounting) task using chocolate rewards, not a cue-reactivity paradigm presenting clear visual reward cues; it does not contain a within-participant cue>control contrast of drug or natural reward-related visual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported, including whole-brain exploratory analyses), I6 (voxelwise results reported clearly), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no assessment of cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component), I4 (no within-participant contrast of natural reward-related cues>control stimuli). No exclusion criteria from the review’s list are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I3 and I4.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts comparing food versus blurry baseline and food versus non-food (animal) images. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are presented (random-effects GLM, whole-brain corrected alpha < .05) with activation clusters and Talairach coordinates reported (e.g., BA45, BA42 coordinates). MRI field strength (3T), participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This full-text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (natural reward) with block-design within-subject contrasts (sexual condition > neutral and emotional control). Data were analyzed with SPM12 and a second-level random-effects voxelwise analysis with FDR correction; results are reported as clusters/MNI coordinates and P-values in the main text and supplementary tables/figures. MRI field strength (3-T), participant sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are described. Therefore the study satisfies the review’s requirements for (i) natural reward-related visual cue-reactivity, (ii) within-participant cue>control contrasts, (iii) group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain voxelwise reporting), and (iv) availability of results in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only without within-subject contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (explicit penile-vaginal images). It includes within-participant contrasts (PEN>NEU and PEN>BOD) and group-level voxelwise second-level analyses reported with whole-brain FWE-corrected results (maps/figures). Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore the full text is complete.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food > non-food images. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) and results are presented in figures and tables; preprocessing and analysis software (FSL/FEAT) and MRI field strength (3T) are described, and participant age/sex and cue type are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant contrast, empirical human fMRI data).

This is an fMRI study of a natural reward (palatable food) with a clear visual cue component (milkshake picture vs water picture). The paper includes within-participant contrasts of natural reward-related cues > control (milkshake image > water image) and taste receipt contrasts (milkshake taste > tasteless). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (cluster-corrected whole-brain analyses with cluster sizes and Z maxima; figures/clusters described). Preprocessing and analysis details (3T scanner, FSL/FEAT, motion correction, smoothing) and participant demographics are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes qualifying within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images and within-participant contrasts of food vs nonfood control objects. The paper reports group-level voxelwise activation maps (random-effects t-maps with cluster-level correction via Monte Carlo) and ROI analyses, with results presented in figures and supplemental tables. Key methodological details (participants’ age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software BrainVoyager/SPSS) are reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of responses to erotic visual stimuli (sexual reward — a form of natural reward). It includes within-participant cue>control contrasts (erotic pictures contrasted with fixation cross; erotic videos contrasted with nature scenes) and male>female and female>male contrasts. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with FWE correction and cluster reports) and ROI analyses; whole-brain voxelwise results are available and described. Methods report participant ages/sex, stimulus type, MRI field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12), satisfying reporting expectations. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, contains within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food images). It includes within-participant contrasts (food > non-food and high-calorie > low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise second-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster correction (Monte Carlo simulations; voxelwise p<0.001), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. MRI field strength (3T), stimuli type, and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager) are reported. Although ROIs were also used, whole-brain voxelwise results are presented, so the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual monetary cues (images of $5/$25; immediate vs delayed) to evoke reward-related cue responses. It includes within-subject contrasts of reward cues > implicit baseline/no-prize and specific contrasts of immediacy/magnitude. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (permutation-based nonparametric paired t tests with threshold-free cluster enhancement) and significant activation maps are reported (caudate, putamen, ACC, etc.). Key reporting elements (participant age/sex, cue type, 3-T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software [FSL]) are provided. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results.

The full text describes a human pCASL perfusion fMRI study using visual smoking-cue (video) and non-smoking control video, with within-subject SCs > non-SCs contrasts. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were conducted using an anatomically defined ROI mask with voxelwise thresholding and cluster-based correction (i.e., small-volume-corrected results) and coordinates are reported in Table 2. Participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the monetary incentive delay task with clear visual cues (geometric symbols) to probe reward anticipation (a natural reward). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of gain anticipation versus neutral (¥20+¥100+¥500 > ¥0), and group-level voxelwise results using whole-brain thresholds and an a priori NAc ROI with FWE small-volume correction. Coordinates, tables, and figures of activation are reported. Participant demographics (n=19, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/MATLAB) are reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (custom gambling images and food images). It includes a within-subject contrast gambling cues > gambling-matched neutral cues and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with cluster-based family-wise error correction (Z=2.3, p<0.05) and MNI peak coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT/FLAME), participant demographics (age/sex reported; all male), and cue types. Results include whole-brain corrected activity contrasts and small-volume/ROI supplementary tests (nucleus accumbens ROI). Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion; core content appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria E3–E6.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic video stimuli (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (erotic vs sport control). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported, including small-volume correction (hypothalamus) and voxelwise correlations between BOLD (erotic>sport) and individual measures. Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager 4.9) are reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for natural reward visual cue-reactivity (I3), a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), and provides qualifying group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (I5–I6); reporting details satisfy I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues (24 heroin-related and 24 neutral images), satisfying I3. The analysis includes within-participant contrasts of heroin-related > neutral cues (heroin-related vs neutral), satisfying I4. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical results are reported (ANOVA and post-hoc contrasts; threshold P<0.05 corrected via Monte Carlo simulation/AFNI; voxelwise clusters/tables and figures provided), satisfying I5 and I6. The manuscript reports MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (DPARSF, SPM8, AFNI correction), and participant sex/clinical details, so I7 is met or at least not violated. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of natural rewards (food) using visual food images and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of reward-related cues > control stimuli (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food images). The main within-subject contrasts compare food images with vs. without calorie information (two types of food cues) rather than food cue > control stimuli; therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. The study does satisfy I3, I5, I6, and I7, and it is a complete full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply to this manuscript.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity in human participants using visual cues paired with tastes. It includes within-participant cue contrasts (anticipatory palatable cue > sub-palatable cue; matched palatable > matched sub-palatable; prediction error contrasts), satisfying I4. The study used whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (FSL Randomise with TFCE, reported coordinates and cluster-level FWE p-values), satisfying I5 and I6. The design includes a clear visual cue component (taste-paired cues), satisfying I3. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete=true). It is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, nor non-empirical, and contains qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results, so no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity studies using visual stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast (food > nonfood). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (ANCOVA voxelwise correlations, corrected for multiple comparisons using cluster-level Monte Carlo simulation), and results are reported at the whole-brain level. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual (natural reward) cues vs neutral images. Methods specify voxelwise, group-level SPM12 analyses and report within-participant contrasts (sexual vs neutral backgrounds) and main effects of background (sexual>neutral) with FDR-corrected, whole-brain results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, 3.0T MRI, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Results are reported as voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and percent-signal-change follow-ups. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials referenced but not required. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3–I7) and should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in children. It used a within-subject crossover design with modeled regressors for high- and low-calorie food blocks and blurred control images as an implicit baseline, and reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (ANOVA with cluster correction) including stimulus main effects and activity×stimulus interactions. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI, ANTs) are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity, within-participant cue contrasts, and qualifying group-level voxelwise results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes within-participant contrasts of food cues versus control (HC–C, LC–C, HC–LC) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM8) with cluster/voxel thresholding and reported activation clusters. Stimuli, MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing, and software are described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for inclusion as a whole-brain task-evoked visual cue-reactivity study.

This fMRI study is a task-based investigation of monetary reward anticipation (monetary incentive delay task), not a cue-reactivity study using drug-related or natural reward visual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports voxelwise, group-level task-evoked results with whole-brain and small-volume corrections), I6 (voxelwise results presented in text/figures/tables), I7 (reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with clear visual cue component; uses monetary reward cues rather than drug/natural reward images), I4 (no within-participant contrast comparing drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control stimuli). No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective of visual drug/natural reward cue-reactivity and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using clear visual stimuli (erotic pictures and videos). Within-subject contrasts were computed for male and female pictures/videos contrasted with fixation (pictures) and neutral nature scenes (videos), satisfying a cue>control contrast. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) as well as ROI analyses, fulfilling the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Stimuli are visual (pictures/videos), and reporting includes participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM, MarsBar), meeting reporting preferences. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie, low-calorie, neutral images). It reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie and high-calorie > neutral) and presents group-level voxelwise SPM results (whole-brain voxelwise maps and tables of cluster coordinates; voxel-level thresholds reported). Methods include MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Although the sample is small (three genetically leptin-deficient adults) and the group analysis is fixed-effects, the paper nevertheless provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise whole-brain results for visual natural-reward cues, satisfying the review inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using clear visual cues that predict monetary (natural) rewards and losses. The study models within-subject anticipation and outcome conditions (gain, loss, neutral/fixation) and reports within-participant contrasts (anticipation/outcome effects) and whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (tables of clusters/coordinates are provided). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete. Therefore it meets criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (images). It includes within-participant contrasts (food [high+low] vs nonfood; high-calorie vs low-calorie; high-calorie vs nonfood). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported using whole-brain random-effects analyses with familywise error correction and ROI small-volume corrections (nucleus accumbens, insula, hypothalamus), with coordinates provided. Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue type, 3.0-T MRI field strength, SPM12 preprocessing/statistics). The full text supplied contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant contrasts). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual tobacco-related advertisements as cues (e-cigarette, cigarette, and matched control images). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing flavored/tobacco/control conditions (e.g., sweet/fruit vs tobacco, and comparisons with control images). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (cluster FWE-corrected p<0.05) for sweet/fruit versus tobacco advertisements, and notes exploratory whole-brain comparisons with control conditions in the supplement. Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity that includes a visual cue paradigm (appetizing > unappetizing food images) and within-participant contrasts. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and significant activations are reported with MNI coordinates and cluster correction. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI acquisition parameters, preprocessing, and software are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (participants viewed food and non-food images). Within-subject contrasts were used (highly desirable > less desirable food; all food > non-food) and these first-level contrasts were entered into group-level voxelwise analyses. The authors report small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (SVC, p<.05 FWE-corrected) with peak coordinates (e.g., −34,12,0), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. The manuscript provides necessary methodological details (3T scanner, cue types, sample, contrasts); while not all preferred reporting items (e.g., explicit preprocessing/statistical software) are fully detailed, I7 is stated as preferred only and does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual images of stimulant drugs and food (visual cues). The paper reports within-participant contrasts including drug vs neutral, food vs neutral, and drug vs food. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with cluster correction) are reported and visualized; VOI/small-volume results are also provided. Participant demographics and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported; MRI acquisition site is given (field strength not explicit but missing details do not preclude inclusion per criteria). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity and behavioral craving ratings but does not include any task-evoked cue-reactivity fMRI contrasts (no within-participant cue>control visual stimulus contrast). Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for task-based cue-reactivity results. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (only seed-based/resting-state analyses without task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (no within-participant cue>control contrasts; only between-group/ connectivity comparisons). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity with visual cues during scanning), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). Full text appears complete. Consequently, EXCLUDED.

This study examines visual food cue reactivity (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (pre- and post-stress food cues vs neutral) and reports detailed methods and participant demographics. However, the neuroimaging results are reported as ROI-averaged statistics (paired t-tests on ROI mean parameter estimates) rather than as group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps/coordinates. No qualifying voxelwise, whole-brain, or SVC-corrected group-level results (tables of coordinates or SVC-corrected clusters) are presented in the full text. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion applied: E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food pictures as natural reward cues (visual-only). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing food versus neutral object conditions and related contrasts (food>neutral, attention manipulations) at the group level using random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (F- and t-maps), with thresholding and cluster criteria and reported fROIs/coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual sexual (natural reward) cues versus neutral control photographs with within-subject contrasts (S > N) reported. The paper reports group-level voxelwise statistical results (SPM99; fixed-effects group analysis with whole-brain thresholds and coordinates) and individual voxelwise results for lower-brain analyses. Participant demographics (age, male sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics details are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual sexual stimuli (a natural reward). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing sexual>neutral (and sexual>positive/negative). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with both small-volume (ROI) corrections and whole-brain family-wise-error corrected analyses. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Thus the study meets the review’s scope (natural reward visual cue-reactivity) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images versus non-food/blurred controls, with within-participant contrasts (food > non-food) at the single-subject level and group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses reported. The paper presents voxelwise results using small-volume correction within a priori ROIs and reports FWE-corrected clusters, meeting the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanners, preprocessing with SPM8) are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the review (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates neural cue-reactivity to social (natural) rewards (smiling faces) with explicit visual cues. It includes within-subject contrasts of reward cues versus control (smile intensity levels including a 0/control condition) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain FWE-corrected analyses) as well as small-volume ROI results (VTA, NAcc, vmPFC) with corrected p-values. Essential details (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI, preprocessing and SPM5 software) are reported. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It contains a within-participant contrast (food > non-food) analyzed at the group level with voxelwise whole-brain statistics (one-sample t-test; voxelwise p=0.001, cluster-level FDR Q<0.05) and reports activated clusters with MNI coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual images (highly processed, minimally processed foods, and household objects). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., Highly Processed Foods > Household Items; Highly Processed > Minimally Processed) and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses corrected for multiple comparisons (AFNI 3DClustSim cluster correction) with reported significant brain regions. Methods report participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12; AFNI used for cluster correction). Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts of motivational (male) versus control (female) stimuli (Male > Female), and other NoGo>Go contrasts. Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses were performed and reported with whole-brain cluster correction (z>2.3, p<.05), and voxelwise regional findings (right dAIC) are presented in figures and described in the text. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Full text incomplete: provided content contains only metadata/PMCID/disclaimer and lacks core article sections (methods, results). Based on title and known topic, this study concerns conscious self-regulation of emotion (emotion regulation), not drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not assess drug or natural reward cue-reactivity with visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cue>control or reward-cue>control contrast apparent), I5 (no available qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results in the provided content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confirmed from the incomplete text. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot fully verify eligibility; excluding on that basis.

This article is a study protocol/trial methods paper that describes an fMRI paradigm using visual food cues (natural reward) and planned within-participant contrasts (food vs. non-food), but it does not report any task-evoked voxelwise group-level fMRI results. Exclusion criterion E6 applies (non-empirical/protocol paper without original human fMRI results). Inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI study of natural reward with visual cues) is met based on methods, but inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met because no within-participant cue>control contrast results are reported, and no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistical results are presented. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to visual monetary reward cues (ring of dollar signs vs neutral cue) during a rewarded antisaccade task in abstinent smokers and non-smokers. It includes within-subject comparisons of reward vs. neutral trials (incentive effects and incentive × time interactions), and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain cluster-corrected using voxel p<0.001 and AlphaSim cluster threshold; Talairach coordinates and F-statistics are provided). Participant demographics, cue type, 3.0T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, AFNI) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (images) (I3). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of smoking-related versus neutral cues (within-group t-tests in current smokers showing greater NAcc and amygdala activation) and condition effects (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported: whole-brain corrected activation maps (cluster correction) and small-volume-corrected analyses for regions including DLPFC and amygdala; NAcc was treated as an anatomically defined ROI with reported ANOVA/interaction (I5). Voxelwise results are presented in the main text/tables/ROI analyses (I6). Participant demographics and methodological details are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not rely solely on ROI analyses (whole-brain and SVC present), is not only connectivity/resting-state, and includes within-participant cue>control contrasts. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in children comparing obese and normal-weight responses to visual food cues. It includes within-subject contrasts (food > neutral), reports group-level voxelwise random-effects results with whole-brain and ROI-corrected statistics (coordinates/tables/figures), and provides necessary methodological details (participant demographics, cue type, 1.5T MRI, SPM5 preprocessing). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This study is an fMRI investigation of visual food cues (natural rewards) and thus meets inclusion criteria I3 (visual natural reward cue-reactivity) and I4 (within-participant contrast: fattening vs non-fattening food cues). It also reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software details (I7). However, the fMRI results are reported using an ROI-based approach (mean parameter estimates in predefined ROIs and region-by-region analyses) and do not present group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical maps or coordinate tables that would qualify under I5. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC results) and cannot be included in the voxelwise meta-analysis.

This is a human task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (high- and low-energy food pictures) and non-food object controls, with within-subject contrasts (HE>object, LE>object). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (FEAT/FSL), even though no clusters survived correction; the main text clearly describes these voxelwise results and ROI analyses. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity (I3, I4) and provides qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (I5) with acceptable reporting (I6) and demographic/method details (I7). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of a natural reward (juice) task with an explicit visual cue and within-subject task regressors, and it reports participant demographics and MRI parameters. Therefore it meets I3 (natural reward with visual cue), I4 (within-participant task contrasts for reward/disappointment), and I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). However, all task results reported are ROI-based (caudate/putamen activity measures and ROI RSFCs) and I find no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables in the full text. Thus it does not meet I5 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result) and I6 (no voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement). Because it reports only ROI analyses without qualifying voxelwise results, exclusion criterion E3 applies. Accordingly the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of cigarette cue-reactivity using visual cues and reports group-level voxelwise statistical maps for task contrasts (Attend vs Regulate). However, the paper does not present a qualifying within-participant voxelwise contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., CS+ > CS−) at the group level. The primary reported imaging contrast is Attend CS+ vs Regulate CS+ (instruction effect), and ROI/extraction analyses are reported for dACC. Because the meta-analysis requires at least one within-subject drug-cue>control voxelwise result, this study does not meet inclusion criterion I4 even though it meets other requirements (visual cues, group voxelwise maps, figures/ROI reporting, and participant details). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates neural responses to natural reward (food) cues with a clear visual component (food pictures) and gustatory stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (food>nonfood, high-calorie>nonfood, chocolate>tasteless). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are presented with small-volume FWE-corrected statistics (cluster sizes, t values, P-FWE) in predefined ROIs; results are reported in tables/figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, contains within-subject cue>control contrasts, empirical human fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3–I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This is a single-case fMRI study of visual sexual (natural reward) cues with within-participant cue>baseline contrasts and coordinates reported, but it does NOT provide a group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) as required by I5 — the analyses are at the single-subject level. Therefore it fails the essential inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing food choices versus non-food choices (food>non-food) and high- vs low-calorie food choices. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (one-sample t-tests, whole-brain thresholds; peak coordinates and tables/figures provided), and preprocessing/MRI field strength/participant age and sex are described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (hardcore sexual penetration images) and reports within-participant contrasts (PEN > NEU). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters and small-volume-corrected analyses; coordinate tables and figures are provided. Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T Philips), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this fMRI study includes within-participant cue>control contrasts (favorite-food cue vs neutral-relaxing), reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (FWE-corrected), and provides coordinate/figure results, it does NOT include a clear visual cue component. The paradigm used personalized guided-imagery audio scripts (auditory/imagery), not visual or multimodal designs that include visual stimuli. This fails inclusion criterion I3, so the study must be excluded despite meeting I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. This study used gustatory (taste) cues (alcohol vs. juice) during fMRI rather than visual cues, so it does not satisfy the required visual-cue component (I3 not met). It does meet other inclusion requirements: within-participant alcohol>control contrast (I4), whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported (I5) with results available in figures/tables (I6), and reports participant age/sex and MRI details (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails I3 (no visual stimuli).

This fMRI study used a revised monetary incentive delay (MID) task that presents visual cues for gains/losses (natural reward-related visual stimuli). It includes within-participant contrasts of gain>neutral and loss>neutral (cue>control) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses with small-volume-corrected (SVC) ROI results (striatum, ACC) and corrected cluster thresholds. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (AFNI) and participant demographics. Results are presented as task-evoked voxelwise effects and figures/tables, satisfying availability of qualifying voxelwise results. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking pictures). The authors report within-subject contrasts of smoking versus matched control pictures (BEGIN- and END- smoking stimuli minus control stimuli) and conduct group-level voxelwise analyses using FLAME with voxelwise FWE-corrected thresholds (p<0.05). Results are presented as thresholded statistical images, tables of coordinates, and figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not provide task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity contrasts. Although participants viewed visual erotic (natural reward) and neutral films behaviorally, the neuroimaging component consisted of resting-state/seed-based functional connectivity (VTA-seeded fcMRI), not task-based cue-reactivity. Therefore it lacks the required within-participant cue>control task contrast and any task-evoked voxelwise (whole-brain or SVC) results. Exclusion IDs met: E4. Inclusion IDs met: I7 (reported participant sex/age grouping, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (fMRI assessing cue-reactivity with visual cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (task-evoked voxelwise group-level result), I6 (not applicable because no task-evoked voxelwise results to report). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cue reactivity (palatable foods) that includes clear visual cue components (food images; visual cues predicting milkshake). It reports within-subject cue>control contrasts (appetizing food > unappetizing food; appetizing food > water; milkshake cue > tasteless cue; milkshake receipt > tasteless receipt). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with cluster correction and stereotactic coordinates (MNI), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) and scanner field strength (3T) are provided. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food pictures. It includes within-participant contrasts (food pictures vs baseline; high-calorie vs low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results using whole-brain mixed-effects analyses (and small-volume corrections for seeds) with coordinates and statistical thresholds. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used visual food cues (natural rewards) and includes within-participant contrasts (no-go vs. go; high- vs low-calorie comparisons), so it meets I3 and I4. However, all reported fMRI results are ROI-based (mean beta extraction from a priori ROIs) rather than group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps. The manuscript does not report qualifying voxelwise results in the main text, tables, or supplements. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete. Accordingly, the study is excluded because it lacks a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked group result required for inclusion in the cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity (palatable food) that uses clear visual cues (pictures of high-fat/high-sugar foods) and milkshake cues. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (high-fat/high-sugar food > vegetables; high-fat/high-sugar food > water; milkshake cue > tasteless cue) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholding and cluster criteria described) with reported BOLD results. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food and nonfood images). It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie food; food > nonfood) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume correction (FWE-corrected ROI mask) showing significant activation differences (right putamen/pallidum). Results are reported in the main text and figures; participant demographics and preprocessing software (SPM5) are provided. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. MRI field strength is not explicitly stated in the provided text, but this omission alone does not preclude inclusion per protocol. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for voxelwise cue-reactivity analyses with visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images and reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts; however, it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward cues > control (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food images) as required by inclusion criterion I4. The reported contrasts compare different cognitive strategies/mindsets (LATER, DISTRACT, ALLOW) against a NOW control mindset while presenting the same food images; these are strategy-related contrasts rather than stimulus-related (food>control) contrasts. The study therefore fails to meet I4, and per the review rules is excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results), I6 (results available in figures/tables), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) specifically apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy volunteers examining natural reward (chocolate) and aversive cues with explicit visual cues (chocolate picture, mouldy drink) and a control grey image. The paper reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts of pleasant/unpleasant cue > grey image (anticipatory phase) and taste > rinse, with group-level voxelwise results reported and corrected (whole-brain cluster FWE and small-volume corrections for ROIs). Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3T Siemens) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity visual-stimulus fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not report an explicit within-participant cue>control contrast of natural reward cues versus control stimuli (Inclusion criterion I4 not met). This study used visual food cues and multivariate/univariate analyses (parametric modulators and RSA) but presented only food images without a clear non-food or control-cue contrast; analyses focus on valence/WTE parametric modulation and pattern similarity rather than a cue>control voxelwise contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward-related visual food cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported with whole-brain and SVC FWE correction), I6 (voxelwise results available in main text/tables/figures), I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore excluded for failing I4. Confidence=0.80.

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts of food cues > control (HC–C and LC–C) at the group level, with voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM8. Results include ROI analyses with p ≤ 0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons (FWE or small-volume correction) and report coordinates/clusters, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines natural reward (milkshake) cue-reactivity with clear visual cues (geometric shapes) and reports within-participant contrasts (cue predicting milkshake > cue predicting tasteless solution) and detailed demographic/MRI/preprocessing information. However, the full text reports ROI-based analyses (parameter estimates extracted from caudate, putamen, ventral pallidum using WFUPickAtlas masks) and mixed-effects growth models on those ROI values. The manuscript does not present any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain maps or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results) or coordinate tables indicating such results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I7 (reporting of age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise or SVC statistical result), I6 (not applicable since no qualifying voxelwise results reported). Hence EXCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (food images) with non-food control stimuli included. The design and analyses used within-subject contrasts (e.g., High-ED vs Low-ED; large vs small portions) based on a GLM that included regressors for food and control blocks, and whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses were conducted with cluster correction and peak coordinates reported (Table 3). These elements satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-participant voxelwise task-evoked contrasts, and reporting of whole-brain results. Participant/sample and MRI details (age/sex, scanner, preprocessing/statistics software) are provided or described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply.

This study used erotic (visual) movie clips as natural reward cues (I3 satisfied) and reports participant demographics and scanning/preprocessing details (I7 satisfied). However, it does not report any within-participant voxelwise task-evoked contrast of cue>control (no standard erotic>neutral GLM contrast reported), nor does it present group-level whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise activation results. Analyses are ROI-based intersubject correlation/IS-RSA and meta-analytic decoding rather than qualifying voxelwise task-evoked statistics. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5, and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/region-based results with no qualifying voxelwise results). Excluded on this basis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual sexual stimuli (natural reward). The study uses within-subject contrasts (sexually preferred vs non-preferred; explicit vs less-explicit) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses, p<0.001 uncorrected, cluster extent threshold) with anatomical localization. Key methodological details required by the review (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8) are reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food vs object images with within-subject food>object contrasts. The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses and small-volume (ROI) corrected results (cluster-based permutation correction), and provides participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, Freesurfer). Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > non-food) in pre- and post-meal conditions. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and corrected for multiple comparisons (cluster-based whole-brain correction) with peak coordinates reported. MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager), and participant age/sex information are provided. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and is includable in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (e.g., healthy food choice vs healthy food reject; HD vs ND; TD vs ND). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (one-sample t-tests, whole-brain thresholding with cluster-level correction and coordinates/figures reported). Participant demographics, cue type, field strength, and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (high- and low-calorie pictures) in humans, satisfying the meta-analysis scope. The study includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie foods > cars; high- vs low-calorie foods) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results using SPM2 with small-volume correction (SVC) for ROIs (p<.01, extent threshold), and provides coordinate-based activation results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes qualifying within-subject contrasts).

This is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that used visual stimuli (visual + auditory multimodal paradigm) and within-subject contrasts (high- vs low-calorie and food vs non-food). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were reported (SPM8, cluster-extent thresholding with corrected P<0.05) and results are presented as statistical maps/clusters. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a human fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with a within-subject contrast of food>scenery. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (thresholded t-maps, cluster correction, peak coordinates), and interaction analyses were performed; results are presented as voxelwise statistical maps and peak coordinates (qualifying whole-brain/small-volume-corrected results). Participant demographics (age, male-only), MRI field strength (1.5T), imaging parameters, preprocessing, and analysis software (fmristat) are reported. The paradigm uses visual-only stimuli (food pictures) and includes the required task-evoked contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material presence is noted but not required. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7.

The study reports an fMRI investigation using the Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task, which uses clear visual cues signaling monetary (natural) rewards versus neutral cues. It includes a within-participant contrast of monetary reward anticipation > neutral anticipation. Analyses are whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise group-level results (with peak coordinates reported), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. Key methodological details (participant age range, sex considerations, 3-T MRI, and FSL preprocessing/software) and cue type are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not solely connectivity, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (infant and sexual images). The design includes within-participant contrasts of stimulus types (infant/sexual vs neutral/fixation) in a GLM. The authors report group-level voxelwise GLM analysis with FDR correction (p=0.05) used to generate activation maps and provide ROI center coordinates (e.g., [−13 10 −8], [11 10 −8], [0 −20 −8]), indicating availability of voxelwise results. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX 2.2), participant age/sex, and cue type are reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This study investigates neural responses to food images (natural rewards) using fMRI (meets I3) and includes a within-participant contrast of high-calorie vs low-calorie food (HC>LC) (meets I4). Participant details (age, sex) and MRI details are reported (meets I7). However, the reported results are seed-to-voxel functional connectivity (task-modulated connectivity) group comparisons; no task-evoked voxelwise activation (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) contrasts are reported. Therefore the study reports only seed-based connectivity results without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result, which falls under exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criterion I5 (required qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result) is not met; I6 (allowing voxelwise results reported in tables/figures) is also not met because there are no qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results. Full text appears complete.

Full text incomplete: only abstract and references provided, so core methods and results (introduction, methods, detailed results, figures/tables) are unavailable. Inclusion criteria met based on the abstract: I3 (fMRI study with clear visual sexual cues) and I4 (within-participant contrast: sexual stimuli > neutral stimuli is explicitly described). Inclusion criteria that cannot be confirmed from the abstract: I5 (presence of at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result) and I6 (whether voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures/supplement). I7 (reporting of MRI details and preprocessing) is incomplete in the abstract. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because the full text is not available to verify the critical voxelwise analytic results required by I5/I6, I must exclude this study pending the complete full text.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (food and scenery images). It reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie and food > scenery) and group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction (TFCE, p<0.05 FWER after SVC) including MNI coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength, preprocessing and software. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical fMRI study examines food (a natural reward) cue-related anticipation and receipt using visual cues (abstract snack/ basket and wallet images) and directly contrasts high vs no reward within participants (10 SP vs 0 SP; EUR1 vs 0). Group-level voxelwise results are reported both as small-volume-corrected ROI findings (FWE-corrected) and whole-brain cluster-corrected results. Relevant methodological details (participant age ranges, sex matching, cue types, 3T scanner, preprocessing and SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Exclusion: E4 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported). This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cues with a clear visual component (I3 satisfied) and includes within-participant contrasts of high-ED > low-ED food cues (I4 satisfied). The paper reports group-level seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity maps (voxelwise connectivity results), but does not present a qualifying task-evoked whole-brain or small-volume-corrected activation contrast (high>control) in this manuscript; the authors state main BOLD activation results are reported elsewhere. Participant/sample and acquisition/preprocessing details are reported (I7 satisfied). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4, and must be excluded.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in adolescents that includes visual cue exposure (Coke product and logo advertisements) and within-participant contrasts of Coke ads > non-food ads. Results are reported as voxelwise, whole-brain cluster-corrected analyses with stereotactic coordinates in tables, and methods report MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8/AFNI tools). Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses event-related fMRI with visual sexual stimuli (natural rewards) and matched nonsexual control images, meeting the review’s cue modality requirement. It reports within-participant contrasts of sexual stimuli > nonsexual control stimuli and preferred > non-preferred stimuli. Group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with whole-brain results (and cluster-level correction) and small-volume correction for predefined ROIs; stereotactic coordinates and corrected statistics are provided. Participant characteristics (age, sex/orientation), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM2) are described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical task-evoked voxelwise results present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual picture stimuli. It includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol>neutral), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results using SPM with voxel p<.001 and cluster-level FWE correction, and provides coordinates and cluster descriptions. The full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Note: some acquisition details (e.g., MRI field strength) appear referenced in supplementary material, but lack of that single detail does not preclude inclusion per the review’s guidance (I7 is preferred, not required).

This fMRI study of visually evoked sexual (natural reward) arousal uses erotic vs nonerotic films (visual cues) and reports within-participant contrasts, so it meets I3 and I4 and reports participant details (I7). However, it does not report a group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Results are presented as per-subject activation maps/pixel counts and counts of subjects showing activation; no group-level voxelwise SPM-like results, coordinates, or small-volume-corrected analyses are provided. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met, so the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to infant faces (natural reward-related visual cues). It includes within-participant contrasts of familiarity (own > unknown infant faces) and emotion (sad/happy) which serve as cue>control contrasts for natural reward cues. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (voxel-level p<.001, pFWE<.05). Visual stimuli are primary (infant faces), and scanner parameters, preprocessing, and analysis software (SPM12) are reported. Therefore it meets I3 (visual natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue contrasts), I5 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I6 (results presentation acceptable), and I7 (reporting details). Full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (sexual stimuli) using visual cues (nude vs dressed images). It includes within-subject contrasts of sexual > neutral (nude>dressed) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (thresholds reported, FDR-corrected contrasts and voxelwise maps/tables described). Methods report MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and SPM02, participant demographics and cue type. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, lack of within-subject cue>control contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexually explicit film clips (natural reward cues) with a within-subject contrast of erotic video > active (nonsexual) control video. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM2; voxelwise thresholds and activation foci/coordinates are described), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward-related cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using visual monetary incentive cues (MID task).
