It reports within-participant contrasts (anticipation of gain vs. neutral and anticipation of loss vs. neutral) and group-level voxelwise results. Ventral striatal findings were corrected using small-volume correction (FWE-corrected) with reported peak coordinates and t-values. Methods report participant characteristics (sex distribution/age table), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) visual cue reactivity. It includes within-participant food>nonfood contrasts, reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level statistical maps with cluster-level correction, and provides necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing software BrainVoyager). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco cue reactivity using visual cigarette-related images. It reports within-subject contrasts comparing smoking (craving) versus neutral pictures (craving>neutral) and other task contrasts. Results are presented as voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster-level correction (AlphaSim/FWE-equivalent) and reported peak coordinates and tables. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing and SPM8 statistical software. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and supplementary details). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is a human task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward). It includes a within-participant contrast (high-calorie > low-calorie foods). Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume correction in the hypothalamus (one voxel survives SVC, coordinate and p=0.0125), and results are described in text and figures. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images. It reports within-subject contrasts of food cues versus control objects (HD+LD > OBJ and HD > LD) and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain cluster-level FWE-corrected contrasts and a small-volume-corrected ROI analysis). Participant demographics, cue types, scanner (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual pornographic images (natural reward cues) and neutral images, with a within-participant contrast of pornographic > neutral (pornographic vs. neutral) reported. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed with whole-brain inference (p < 0.05 FWE cluster-corrected), and ROI analyses supplement these results. The paper reports participant demographics (age, all heterosexual males), cue type (pornographic vs. neutral images), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). Thus it provides a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise within-subject cue>control contrast using visual stimuli appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of visual drug/natural reward cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual food images (natural rewards). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food versus control stimuli (food > people/nature) entered into second-level random-effects analyses and reports peak coordinates (NAcc MNI 12,9,-3) and associated statistics (t(30)=2.87, p=.007), from which ROI beta values were extracted for group-level prediction models. Imaging acquisition, preprocessing, and analysis software/details (3T scanner, SPM8, smoothing, normalization) are described. The go/no-go whole-brain analyses and the cue-reactivity contrast provide task-evoked voxelwise results appropriate for inclusion. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis’ fMRI visual cue-reactivity inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI responses to visual food cues (pictures) comparing functional vs standard foods using a within-subject contrast (functional > standard). First-level contrasts and second-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported with voxelwise results and corrected cluster thresholds (Monte Carlo/AlphaSim), including coordinates and cluster extents. The methods report MRI field strength (3.0 T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM), participant age range, and task details. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for natural reward-related (food) cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking cues and includes within-participant contrasts (smoke vs neutral) used to define patient-specific ROIs (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper reports ROI-based percent signal change analyses (t-tests) and does not provide any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected coordinates/maps) required by I5. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of natural-reward (chocolate) cue-reactivity that presents visual chocolate pictures during task runs and contrasts chocolate versus neutral (office) pictures. The paper reports within-participant/task-evoked contrasts (chocolate > neutral) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps (F-maps) with cluster-level correction; voxelwise results are presented in tables and figures. MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX), participant sex/characteristics, and cue type are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

The study examines fMRI responses to visual food cues (natural reward) but does not include a within-participant cue>control (food cues > non-food/control stimuli) contrast required by the review. The task presented food pictures only and used comparisons across metabolic state (fasting vs. non-fasting) and high vs. low subjective rating (median split), but no explicit reward-cue > control-stimulus contrast is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. It does meet I3 (visual natural reward cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (voxelwise results available in text/figures), and I7 (participant demographics and imaging/preprocessing details reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) explicitly apply. Because I4 is not met, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity that uses a multimodal Alcohol Taste task with an explicit visual cue component (visual labels 'Alcohol Taste' vs 'Control Taste' preceding each trial), satisfying the visual-cue requirement. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (Alcohol Taste > Water Taste) and presents whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise results (Z>2.3, p<0.05) with tables/figures of coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL), and demographics are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visually presented food words. It includes within-subject cue>control contrasts (food > neutral) at the group level, and reports voxelwise task-evoked results from whole-brain analyses (and small-volume corrections for a priori regions) with corrected inference. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food words), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (only ROI/connectivity results, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity with a visual cue component.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based analyses and does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results required for inclusion (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images) and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing software are reported; field strength not stated but missing details alone do not exclude). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise results reported), I4 (no clear within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrast is reported in the full text), I6 (not applicable because no voxelwise results are available to be reported in tables/figures). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore it fails the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of neural responses to sexual (natural reward) visual cues. It includes within-subject contrasts (supraliminal sexual > neutral; subliminal sexual > neutral), reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with coordinates and statistical thresholds (P<0.001 uncorrected; tables/figures), and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of visual natural reward (high-calorie food) cue reactivity. It includes within-participant contrasts (food > neutral in the localizer and regulation vs. mirror contrasts), and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (second-level random effects ANOVA) with cluster-thresholded results and tables/figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (drug) cue reactivity using multimodal audio/visual smoking cues. It uses within-participant contrasts comparing smoking cues versus matched non-smoking control stimuli and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results within an ROI (small-volume) mask (SPM random-effects analyses; t-statistic reported for left putamen). Although some reporting details (e.g., MRI field strength and participant ages) are not explicitly provided in the re-analysis text, the manuscript satisfies the core inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked results with visual cue components and within-subject contrasts. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. I7 (complete reporting of age/field strength/etc.) is only partially met but is not required for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (natural rewards). It reports within-subject food>nonfood contrasts and both ROI and whole-brain voxelwise analyses, including cluster-wise corrected whole-brain results (P<0.05 corrected) with reported coordinates. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are provided. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for visual cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical task fMRI study of adolescent alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol-picture stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > non-alcohol beverage cues, and group-level voxelwise analyses (AFNI 3dttest++ whole-brain exploratory analysis and ROI cluster-corrected results using AlphaSim) with reported significant clusters (locations, cluster sizes, corrected p-values). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, lack of within-subject cue>control contrast, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for voxelwise task-evoked cue-reactivity with visual stimuli.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation that used visual-auditory cues (visual images with matched sounds) paired with methamphetamine versus placebo in a within-subject design. It reports within-participant contrasts directly comparing methamphetamine-paired > placebo-paired cues and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (AFNI 3dmvm whole-brain analysis with cluster correction) reported in tables and figures. Core methods (participants, MRI field strength 3.0T, preprocessing with AFNI, statistical thresholds) and results (clusters in visual/auditory cortex and insula) are described in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not a between-group-only contrast, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports a smoking vs. nonsmoking within-participant cue-reactivity fMRI task using visual smoking images (I3 met) and uses within-subject smoking>nonsmoking contrasts (I4 met). However, all reported task results are ROI-based parameter estimates (a priori ROIs/AI, dACC, PCC, vmPFC, rACC), and the analyses and mediation rely on these ROI values. The full text does not present any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical maps/tables for the smoking>control contrast (I5 not met). Reporting of participant demographics, cue type, scanner and preprocessing is present (I7 met). Therefore the study must be excluded per E3 (only ROI analyses reported). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (photographs of appetizing, disgusting, bland foods and nonfood objects). It includes within-participant contrasts of appetizing>bland and appetizing>nonfood (cue>control) and reports group-level voxelwise statistical results with coordinate peaks and small-volume-corrected (SVC) results for a priori ROIs. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), participant age/sex, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99). All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that uses visual cues (abstract images) paired with food odors (a multimodal design that includes visual cues). The paper reports within-participant contrasts and learning-related analyses comparing food cue trials to non-food/air trials (e.g., faster RTs and greater CS value/RPE-related activity for food vs non-food/air), satisfying a within-subject cue>control comparison. Voxelwise task-evoked results are reported at the group level with whole-brain FDR-corrected maps (and SVC in the hippocampus); statistical maps are available on NeuroVault, meeting the whole-brain/SVC requirement. The manuscript provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. Full text is complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using explicit visual predictive cues (fractal images) that were associated with different juice flavors. The design includes within-participant contrasts (cue types versus baseline and model-based TD cue-related regressors across trials), and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with coordinates and p-values (ventral midbrain, ventral striatum) at the specified threshold (p<0.001) within a priori ROIs. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, and participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI experimental study of appetitive (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual erotic pictures as cues. It includes a within-participant contrast CS+ > CS− (natural reward-related cue > control) used in group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper reports whole-brain results (uncorrected threshold) and ROI analyses using small-volume correction (FWE-corrected) with peak coordinates reported in tables and figures. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (180 food photographs vs 45 non-food photographs). Subject-level regression produced beta coefficients for food and nonfood stimuli, and the authors performed whole-brain voxel-wise group-level analyses (corrected for multiple comparisons) identifying eight regions showing group activity differences to food cues. These elements satisfy the requirement for a within-participant cue>control contrast (food vs nonfood implicit in the subject-level betas) and provide group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results. Participant demographics and imaging/analysis details are reported (with imaging parameters in supplement). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (milkshake vs water) and includes within-participant contrasts (picture milkshake > picture water; receipt milkshake > tasteless). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported using cluster-thresholded Z-statistic images with corrected cluster significance (Z>2.0, cluster p<.05) and ROI masking (constituting acceptable small-volume/voxelwise results). Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are reported. Connectivity analyses are present but are not the sole reported results. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so completeness is sufficient.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) visual cues with within-subject contrasts (Sex vs Fix, Sex vs Neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (Sex vs Fix and Sex vs Neu; Z>2.3, cluster-corrected p=0.05), and a small-volume-corrected ROI analysis (linear contrast levodopa>placebo>haloperidol) yielded voxel-corrected significant effects in bilateral NAcc and dACC. Participant sex, MRI field strength (3T), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FEAT, FLAME) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes qualifying within-participant contrasts, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) versus non‑erotic control stimuli with within‑participant contrasts (erotic > non‑erotic). Group‑level random‑effects voxelwise analyses were performed in SPM5 and report whole‑brain results with cluster and voxel thresholds and some FWE‑corrected coordinates; coordinates/tables are provided. Visual cue component is explicit. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward conditioning using visual fractal cues predicting juice (natural reward) versus neutral outcomes. The study includes within-subject, task-evoked analyses of cue-related responses using temporal-difference model-based parametric regressors (value and RPE at cue onsets), and reports group-level voxelwise results with peak MNI coordinates and t-values (ventral striatum, substantia nigra, amygdala), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain/SVC reporting. Key methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8/FSL) are reported. Although the fMRI analyses are model-based parametric regressors rather than a simple categorical CS+>CS− contrast, these are within-participant cue-related voxelwise analyses indexing natural reward cue-reactivity and therefore meet the review’s requirements. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural (palatable food) and conditioned (monetary) rewards that used clear visual cues (milkshake vs tasteless images; coin displays). It reports within-participant contrasts (milkshake receipt > tasteless; unpaired milkshake cue > unpaired tasteless; monetary win > reward-neutral) and conducted group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with multiple-comparison correction (AFNI 3DClustSim), reporting peak effects and effect sizes. Participant demographics and cue types are reported; preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) is mentioned. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material availability noted but not required. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual infant-face stimuli as natural reward cues (own vs. unknown infants). It includes within-participant contrasts (own-happy vs. unknown-happy; own-sad vs. unknown-sad). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (FDR-corrected maps, tables of coordinates) and a striatal ROI/SVC analysis is also described. Key methodological details are reported (participant ages, 3T MRI, BrainVoyager preprocessing/statistics, stimulus description). These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used visual natural-reward (palatable food) cues and within-participant cue presentations (food vs neutral/baseline) and EMA-fMRI integration. However, the reported neuroimaging analyses are based on ROI-average estimates (paired t-tests on ROI averages), and the full text presents no clear group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results that are whole-brain or explicitly small-volume-corrected (no voxelwise SPM/FSL cluster tables or SVC-corrected coordinate results are provided in the supplied full text). Although coordinates of activated voxels are mentioned, the manuscript emphasizes ROI-average analyses rather than voxelwise, whole-brain, or explicitly SVC-corrected voxelwise results required by I5. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise result) and does not satisfy I5.

This study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It measured resting cerebral blood flow (ASL) 4 h after ingestion of high- vs low-GI meals, without presentation of visual cues or a within-participant cue>control task contrast. Thus it fails key inclusion criteria I3 (no cue-reactivity with visual cues) and I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast). Although the paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinate results and provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (satisfying I7), it does not report any task-evoked cue-reactivity voxelwise result, so exclusion criterion E4 (only resting/unspecified non–task-evoked analyses) applies. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of visual food cues (natural rewards) that reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (high-ED > low-ED; large PS > small PS) and provides sufficient methodological detail (age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). However, the article explicitly states that data for the nonfood control conditions (scrambled images and furniture) were not presented, and no within-participant contrast of cue > control (food > nonfood) is reported. Inclusion criterion I4 requires at least one within-participant cue>control contrast; that criterion is not satisfied here. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject cue>control, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I4 (no reported cue>control within-participant analysis).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of visual natural reward (food) cue reactivity in children. The fMRI task used visual food images (high-ED and low-ED; plus furniture/scrambled images), and group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected results with peak coordinates and cluster size). A within-participant contrast was reported (high-ED > low-ED food images), which constitutes a cue-related contrast of differing reward stimuli. Whole-brain voxelwise results are provided and corrected for multiple comparisons. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with qualifying voxelwise results.

This fMRI study uses visual cues (pictures of food/money) and includes within-participant contrasts of food>money (anticipation and win), and reports participant demographics and scan details (meets I3, I4, I7). However, the analyses are ROI-based: voxelwise parameter estimates were extracted from preselected 6 mm spherical ROIs and entered into regression models. The paper does not report any group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked statistical results (coordinates/tables/SM showing corrected voxelwise effects). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result) and must be excluded.

Excluded because the study reports only pre-defined ROI-based analyses (beta weights extracted from amygdala, NAc, VTA ROIs) and does not present group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Exclusion IDs met: E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with clear visual natural-reward cues — sexual and infant images), I4 (within-participant contrasts comparing sexual/infant vs. neutral stimuli), I7 (reports participant/sample characteristics, cue type, MRI field strength [3T], and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level statistical results reported). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore excluded per E3.

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli (photographs). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food > nonfood (animal) stimuli and group-level voxelwise/random-effects analyses with cluster-level correction (P=0.01, cluster-level α=0.05), reporting significant activations in amygdala, hippocampus, parahippocampus, and midfrontal gyrus. Methods include MRI field strength (3-T Siemens Trio) and preprocessing/statistical software (Brain Voyager QX), and participant demographics (age 15–20, female). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an fMRI task study using visual natural reward cues (erotic pictures) and monetary cues in a within-subject design. It includes within-participant contrasts of high>low erotic cues (reward-related cues) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with small-volume-corrected statistics in predefined ROIs (ventral striatum, amygdala, OFC, hypothalamus) with t-values/p-values and coordinates described. Results and methods (participants’ age/sex, 3T MRI field, preprocessing with SPM12/DARTEL/CAT12) are reported. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue contrasts, and qualifying voxelwise (small-volume-corrected) group results. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

Exclusion E3: the study reports only ROI-based analyses (mean β coefficients averaged within a priori spherical ROIs and ROI-level t-tests) and does not present qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual food cues used), I4 (within-participant food>nonfood contrast), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise or SVC result reported), I6 (no qualifying voxelwise results reported in tables/figures/supplement to satisfy voxelwise reporting requirement). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of monetary reward anticipation using clear visual cues (coins), testing within-subject contrasts (e.g., €1.00 > €0.05). The paper reports group-level voxelwise results: whole-brain cluster-level FWE-corrected activations and ROI small-volume FWE-corrected striatal results, with MNI coordinates and statistics. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue contrasts). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

The study examines visual food cues (natural reward) using an fMRI anticipatory task (square cue preceding food images vs object images). It includes within-participant contrasts (Food Anticipation > Object Anticipation and Food Image > Object Image) and conducts whole-brain voxelwise group- and within-subject analyses with voxel thresholds and cluster correction (AlphaSim). Key voxelwise results are reported with coordinates (e.g., right ventral anterior insula, xyz=38,11,-8) and cluster volumes in the main text. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is original empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of high- and low-caloric foods and non-foods). It reports within-participant contrasts (high-caloric > low-caloric; also HC, LC, and NF against implicit baseline) and provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results with small-volume correction in a predefined VTA ROI (FWE-corrected results, peak coordinates and t/z values reported). Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies with visual cues and qualifying voxelwise results.

This fMRI study examines neural responses to natural reward-related cues (palatable food) and includes a visual cue paradigm (food pictures) and visual cue shapes signaling milkshake delivery, meeting the review’s focus on visual cue-reactivity. It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts (appetizing food > unappetizing food; appetizing food > water; milkshake cue > tasteless cue; milkshake receipt > tasteless receipt). Group-level voxelwise results were analyzed with small-volume correction (SVC) and peak coordinates are reported; statistical methods (SPM5) and MRI field strength (3T) and participant demographics are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual alcohol images and a within-subject alcohol>pleasant contrast. It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (left caudate cluster with MNI coordinates, Z-value, and cluster extent) and whole-brain analyses, satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant age/sex and cue type are provided; MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are indicated as available in supplemental materials. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual sexual stimuli and visual expectancy cues. It includes within-subject contrasts of sexual cues > control (e.g., expectancy of adult sexual stimuli > fixation; picture adult > fixation; child > fixation), and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported as whole-brain analyses with FWE cluster-level correction and peak MNI coordinates and tables/figures. The manuscript provides requisite methodological detail (participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strengths 1.5T and 7T, preprocessing/statistical software SPM8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The study is relevant to a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to natural rewards (sexual stimuli) presented visually.

This is an fMRI study using visual cues (images signaling alcohol, food, neutral) and reports within-participant cue contrasts (alcohol > neutral and alcohol vs food) during the anticipatory phase. The paper presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results across the whole brain and ROI small-volume-corrected analyses (cluster thresholds, coordinates, volumes, and supplementary tables/figures are reported). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI), participant demographics, and cue details. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity fMRI studies using visual stimuli and provides qualifying voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met (not limited to ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is original human empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study presenting visual erotic and other emotional cues (IAPS images) and examines neural reactivity to erotic versus neutral pictures. It includes within-subject contrasts (erotic and other emotional categories > neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results from whole-brain analyses (mixed-effects GLM, voxelwise thresholds, cluster tables/figures). Relevant methodological details (participant age/sex, MRI field strength 3.0T, preprocessing and analysis software BrainVoyager) are reported. Results (tables and figures of activations and coordinates) are provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI empirical study using the Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task, which contains clear visual cues (colored squares signaling win vs. neutral) indexing natural (monetary) reward-related cues. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (anticipate-win > anticipate-neutral; feedback-win-hit > feedback-neutral-hit). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were conducted using FSL/FLAME with clusterwise correction and results (clusters/coordinates and figures) are reported. Participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, empirical human fMRI data present).

This study is excluded because it does not include a within-participant contrast of natural reward cues > control stimuli (no food vs neutral/non-food cue contrast is reported), so it fails inclusion criterion I4. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI study with clear visual food cues), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster-level FWE correction), I6 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), and I7 (reports participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (pictures) and within-participant contrasts of high-ED (high-calorie) vs. low-ED foods (visual high-ED > visual low-ED and auditory high-ED > auditory low-ED). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed with ROI-based small-volume-correction procedures (ACC, caudate, putamen, OFC) and report statistically thresholded activation (dorsal ACC) and coordinates; PPI whole-brain analyses were also conducted (exploratory). Participant demographics (female, ages 20–27), cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, AFNI 3dClustSim) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (images). It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie (reward-related) > low-calorie (control) food images. Group-level voxelwise results are reported: whole-brain FDR-corrected maps for high>low food cues and small-volume-corrected voxelwise regression analyses within a striatum mask (FDR SVC), with stereotaxic coordinates and figures/tables. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, MATLAB) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity for natural rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (food pictures) and within-participant contrasts (food vs. non-food; high-calorie vs. non-food). Group-level voxelwise results are reported and corrected using small-volume correction (FWE-corrected voxel-level results within a priori ROIs) and whole-brain thresholds for non-ROI regions. Methods report MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant demographics and cue types. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues/feedback (symbolic cues and visual feedback images of wallets and faces) and includes within-participant contrasts comparing reward-related stimuli to a neutral “no outcome” baseline (e.g., anticipation: anticipation hit outcome > anticipation no outcome; consumption: consumption hit outcome > consumption no outcome). Analyses were performed at the group level using voxelwise SPM5 whole-brain procedures with reported peak coordinates (and supplementary data). Participant demographics, cue types, field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics software are reported. These features satisfy all inclusion criteria for task-evoked, visual cue-related reward reactivity. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (participant-selected food images). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (viewing food > viewing non-food; distraction food > distraction non-food) and carries out group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with family-wise error (FWE) cluster correction (p<0.05, cluster extent reported). MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), and participant demographics are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes a clear visual cue component (tailored appetizing food images). It reports within-participant contrasts (appetizing food pictures > glasses of water; appetizing > unappetizing) and whole-brain voxelwise group-level results (cluster-corrected) as well as small-volume-corrected ROI searches. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM, DARTEL, AFNI, etc.) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of marzipan objects). It includes a within-participant contrast of CS+ > CS- (task-evoked cue>control) at the group level and reports voxelwise results: whole-brain exploratory clusters (p<.001 uncorrected) and small-volume-corrected (SVC) FWE-corrected group-level effects in the left caudate and right amygdala. Methods and sample details (age/sex, MRI field strength 3T, preprocessing with SPM12) are reported. Thus the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (visual cues, within-subject cue>control contrast, and at least one SVC/voxelwise group-level result) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject contrast, empirical task-evoked data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using clear visual cues (coloured squares predicting monetary reward) that examines reward-related cue-reactivity. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing rewarded cues to non-rewarded control cues (main effect of reward: (A+C)-(B+D)). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain thresholding and results surviving P<0.05 corrected; small-volume corrections applied to a priori regions), satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise task-evoked analyses. Key methodological and participant details are reported (age/sex, cue type, 1.5T MRI, preprocessing/statistics with SPM99). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This study is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity fMRI study relating visceral adiposity to insula networks and food craving. Although it reports visual food images and craving ratings, the imaging data were acquired during a 6-min resting-state scan and no task-evoked visual cue paradigm was presented during fMRI. Therefore there is no within-participant cue>control task contrast nor any task-evoked group-level voxelwise (whole-brain or SVC) results. Exclusion criterion E4 applies (resting-state/seed-based connectivity only without qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results). The study does report participant age/sex, cue type (food images used for behavioral ratings), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software, so inclusion criterion I7 is met. Inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are not met (no fMRI cue-reactivity task with visual cues during scanning; no within-participant cue>control contrast; no task-evoked voxelwise results; no task results reported in tables/figures). Full text appears complete. Hence EXCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward (high-calorie food) cues with a within-participant food>non-food contrast and adequate reporting of participant demographics and MRI details. However, the study reports ROI-based analyses only (percent signal change averaged within a priori spherical ROIs) and presents statistical results at the ROI level (FDR correction across ROIs). The full text does not present group-level voxelwise whole-brain maps, voxelwise coordinates/clusters, or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results necessary for inclusion. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study examines neural responses to sexual cues and sexual stimuli (natural rewards) using visual cues (text announcements) and visual stimuli (pictures/videos). It reports within-participant contrasts CUE SEM > CUE NEUTRAL and SEM > NEUTRAL. Results include small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (FWE SVC) and explorative whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected), satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual food cues (pictures of candy/dessert), with a within-subject, counterbalanced design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of cue conditions relative to a low-level baseline (i.e., food cue > fixation baseline) and regulation contrasts (LATER vs NOW), and presents whole-brain voxelwise results with family-wise error (FWE) correction as well as an ROI small-volume analysis. Voxelwise results are reported in the main text and figures, satisfying availability of qualifying statistical maps/tables. Participant/sample, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8/MATLAB) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (visual cue component, within-participant cue>control contrast, whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results, acceptable reporting of results, and adequate methodological details). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses BOLD-fMRI with clear visual natural-reward cues (erotic video) and reports within-subject contrasts (sexual stimulation vs neutral) and group-level voxelwise analyses. Methods state preprocessing with SPM99, smoothing, voxelwise activation maps with cluster and t-threshold (p<0.01), and independent two-sample t-tests comparing groups, with figures showing whole-brain activation patterns. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and software are reported. The design therefore meets I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported), I6 (results presented in figures/tables), and I7 (participant and MRI details reported). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-subject contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study examines visual food cue reactivity (natural reward) with within-subject food>control contrasts and reports voxelwise group results and coordinates, but it does NOT report any group-level voxelwise results that are whole-brain corrected or small-volume-corrected. The food>cars contrasts used to localize ROIs are reported at p<.05 uncorrected; therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural-reward cues), I4 (within-participant food>control contrasts), I6 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported), I7 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (effectively only ROI/connectivity-focused results without a qualifying corrected voxelwise task map). Full text appears complete for screening. Given the lack of qualifying corrected voxelwise results, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task fMRI study of natural reward (monetary and verbal) cue-reactivity using explicit visual cues (distinct arrow cues), and includes within-participant contrasts of reward cue > control (mS+ minus S−; vS+ minus S−). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (both whole-brain and ROI analyses) with small-volume correction (FWE SVC) for pre-defined ROIs, satisfying the requirement for qualifying voxelwise, task-evoked statistical results. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (only ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images and a within-subject contrast of food>non-food (F>NF). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (food>non-food whole-brain contrast) and ROI small-volume-corrected analyses were reported; results are presented in tables/appendix and described in the text. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Although MRI field strength is not explicitly stated, this missing detail does not preclude inclusion under the review criteria.

The study reports an fMRI cocaine-cue reactivity paradigm using visual images (pictures of cocaine and paraphernalia) and includes a within-participant contrast of cocaine cues > neutral control stimuli. Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted (second-level random-effects, cluster-level correction using Gaussian random field theory in SPM8), providing whole-brain task-evoked results. Necessary methodological details (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength = 3T, preprocessing/statistical software = SPM8) are reported, and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual drug cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (natural rewards) and neutral control videos. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of sexual > neutral stimuli, conducts whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction (P<0.05) and reports coordinates/figures of activation. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM12) are provided. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective of visual natural reward cue-reactivity and satisfies all specified inclusion criteria (I3–I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) comparing heavy and light drinkers. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol versus neutral pictures (and other categories) and planned comparisons showing alcohol>neutral effects in heavy drinkers. Analyses are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects ANOVAs with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction; Talairach coordinates and cluster sizes are reported (Table 2, figures). MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistics software (BrainVoyager QX) are described. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This study uses an MID task with visual monetary cues and reports group-level voxelwise (ROI mask / small-volume-corrected) results for operant response outcomes, but it does not report any within-participant cue>control (e.g., gain>neutral) cue-reactivity contrasts in the present paper. The paper models anticipation periods, but the reported main results focus on outcome (hit/miss) contrasts collapsed across conditions; no qualifying within-subject cue-reactivity voxelwise results are presented here. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying qualifying within-participant cue>control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task includes clear visual natural reward cues - monetary MID), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported within an ROI/small-volume-corrected approach), I6 (voxelwise results reported as cluster coordinates/figures), and I7 (demographics, MRI acquisition, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported).

This study does not meet the review’s core scope (drug or natural reward cue-reactivity). Although it is an fMRI task with visual cues and voxelwise, FWE-corrected cluster results within an ROI, the task used monetary (secondary) rewards rather than drug or natural rewards (e.g., food) and therefore fails to satisfy the primary inclusion criterion I3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported with FWE correction / small-volume ROI), I6 (results availability indicated in text/tables/figures), I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with clear visual cue component). I4 is not applicable because the within-participant contrast is monetary reward>baseline, not drug or natural reward cues>control. No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., not ROI-only). Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical fMRI task that uses visual reward cues (Monetary Incentive Delay task: gain vs neutral cues) constituting natural reward-related cue-reactivity. It reports within-participant contrasts of gain>neutral (reward cues > control) for anticipation and feedback phases. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with small-volume familywise-error correction and peak coordinates (satisfying whole-brain/SVC reporting and coordinate tables/figures). Participant characteristics, cue type (monetary visual cues), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although cues are monetary (not drug), they qualify as natural reward-related visual cues per the meta-analysis objective, and the paper provides task-evoked voxelwise SVC results, so all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (high-calorie food pictures). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food > control (cars) and performs group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with cluster- and voxel-level correction and reported coordinates), satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing details are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs. neutral pictures) in adult non-dependent drinkers. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of alcohol>neutral cue blocks and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests and regressions) with cluster-level FWE correction; peak coordinates and clusters are reported. Results are presented in the main text and figures, and ROI/mediation analyses supplement the voxelwise findings. Participant sex is reported and cue type and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM, MarsBaR) are described; imaging protocol is referenced in the supplement. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural (primary) reward cue-reactivity using clearly presented visual cues (the words “sweet” and “neutral”), satisfying the visual-cue requirement. The main analysis includes a within-participant contrast of sweet cues > neutral cues (reward anticipation: sweet minus neutral) and reports voxelwise task-evoked results. Statistical correction was applied within a priori ROIs (small-volume-corrected using AFNI’s 3dClustSim), and significant clusters (ACC and bilateral amygdala) are reported with coordinates (supplementary tables/figures referenced). Resting-state analyses are supplementary and do not replace the primary voxelwise task results. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (core content present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The full text describes a cue-reactivity task contrasting high-calorie food pictures versus neutral control pictures and reports voxel-wise, group-level statistical results (voxel clusters, peak coordinates, t-values, FWE-correction) from whole-brain analyses. Participant characteristics, MRI field strength(s), preprocessing and analysis software are reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used visual alcohol cues (beer bottle images) in a Go/NoGo paradigm (I3). The design included modeled 'Go' (coke/water) and 'NoGo' (beer) conditions, and individual contrast images were created and entered into group-level, voxelwise SPM8 analyses comparing conditions/groups, providing whole-brain task-evoked results (I4, I5). Results (activation maps/coordinates) were reported and thresholding described; participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported (I6, I7). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or lack of within-participant cue>control contrast) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (food image viewing). It contains within-participant contrasts (food vs non-food; high-calorie vs low-calorie) and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with whole-brain cluster-level correction (voxelwise p<.001 with cluster extent thresholds derived from Monte Carlo simulations). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and participant and scanner details are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses an fMRI Monetary Incentive Delay task with explicit visual anticipatory cues indicating reward, loss, or neutral outcomes, and reports within-participant contrasts (reward > no-incentive; loss > no-incentive). Whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (cluster-corrected, z>=3.1, p<0.05) are reported, and striatal ROI analyses are supplementary to voxelwise results. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL/AFNI/FreeSurfer) are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (wine) cue effects where visual price cues were presented and manipulated. It includes a within-subject contrast of price cue conditions (high vs low) that tests cue-related effects on brain activation and experienced pleasantness. Voxelwise whole-brain multilevel mediation analyses are reported, and results were corrected using small-volume correction (SVC) for a priori ROIs; coordinates and voxelwise results are provided in tables/figures. Participant demographics (age/sex), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, Mediation Toolbox) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study of anticipation to visual natural-reward stimuli (erotica/romance) versus neutral (everyday) and aversive (violence) scenes. Colored visual cues signaled upcoming picture content, and the authors report voxelwise whole-brain analyses (ANOVA and pairwise contrasts) with cluster results and coordinates indicating increased BOLD for anticipating romance > everyday. Imaging parameters (3T scanner), preprocessing (AFNI), and participant demographics are reported. Thus the study meets the review’s requirements for (I3) visual natural reward cue-reactivity, (I4) within-participant natural reward>control contrast, (I5) group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain), (I6) voxelwise results reported, and (I7) basic methodological details reported. Full text is complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (abstract shapes predicting beer vs water) to probe alcohol-related cue reactivity. It reports within-subject contrasts (beer>water) for anticipation, outcome, and delivery phases and provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain results (thresholded maps and coordinate tables; NeuroVault link). Participant demographics (age, sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, ICA-AROMA) are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper is primarily a review but includes a small interleaved TMS/fMRI pilot in 11 cocaine users. The fMRI results reported are TMS-evoked BOLD changes before vs after cTBS (group-level, voxelwise, FWE-corrected clusters) and behavioral craving ratings after cue exposure. However, there is no clear description or reported voxelwise contrast of drug-related visual cues > control stimuli (no task-based visual cue-reactivity BOLD contrast is presented). Therefore the study does not meet I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast). It does meet I5 and I6 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported, and these are presented as corrected clusters/figures). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are met. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it lacks the required cue-reactivity visual task contrasts (I3, I4 not met).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) cues (erotic videos) with within-participant erotic>sports contrasts. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed and reported (SPM random-effects, whole-brain contrasts thresholded at P<0.001), and results are presented in tables/figures. Participant demographics (female, ages 18–30), cue type, MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99/SPM2) are reported. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Although this is an fMRI study of visual natural reward (visual sexual stimuli) and reports voxelwise small-volume-corrected ROI results, it does not present a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., VSS > control) as a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result. The reported primary voxelwise findings are parametric modulators of Delivery VSS correlated with individual ratings and regression with s-IATsex; no explicit VSS>Control contrast results are reported in the full text. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with clear visual cues of a natural reward), I5 (group-level small-volume-corrected voxelwise ROI results reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/tables/figures), I7 (participant/sample and MRI methods reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports fMRI studies using visual food cues (high-ED vs low-ED) and auditory cues; the key contrasts include within-participant high-ED > low-ED cue comparisons and task-evoked, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses reporting whole-brain significant clusters (midbrain, posterior cingulate, hippocampus, etc.). Thus it provides visual cue-based natural reward-related cue-reactivity, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and reports voxelwise group results. Some preferred details (e.g., participant age/sex, MRI field strength) are incompletely reported in the provided text, but missing these does not preclude inclusion per I7. Full text appears complete for methods/results/discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that uses clear visual cues (food pictures and visual symbols predicting chocolate milk). It includes within-participant contrasts of food>non-food (watching food vs non-food; high-calorie vs non-food) and anticipation/receipt contrasts (including chocolate milk vs tasteless solution). Group-level voxelwise statistical results are reported with MNI coordinates and small-volume FWE correction (ROI and some whole-brain results described), fulfilling the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Relevant methodological details (age/sex, cue type, 3.0T MRI, SPM8 preprocessing) are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies of natural rewards.

This is an fMRI study using visual erotic stimuli (natural rewards) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain results; however the paper does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast (e.g., erotic>neutral) required by I4. The reported analyses are main effects (sex, age) and interactions (sex×age×group) and ROI follow-ups, but no explicit within-subject erotic>neutral contrast is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying within-participant cue>control contrast).

This fMRI study examines neuronal responses to a natural reward (sweet taste) using a conditioned visual cue (geometric CS predicting sucrose) and includes within-subject contrasts (SU expectation > AS expectation and SU receipt > AS receipt). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 with whole-brain GLM and small-volume correction (FWE SVC) reported; results are presented in the text/tables with coordinates. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-related natural reward reactivity.

This paper is a commentary/systematic review of stimuli content in alcohol cue-reactivity neuroimaging studies and does not present original human fMRI task-evoked voxelwise results. It does not report a within-participant drug-cue>control contrast or present group-level whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise statistical maps/coordinates from an original experiment. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. It meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data). No inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This fMRI study uses visual food cues (natural reward) and directly contrasts food > non-food within participants. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (random-effects ‘food > non-food’ contrasts) and several clusters were confirmed with small-volume/ROI correction (p < .005). The paper provides necessary methodological details (participant age/sex, cue type, 1.5T MRI, preprocessing with SPM99) and presents whole-brain and ROI-corrected voxelwise results in the main text. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as a natural reward (food) cue-reactivity fMRI study with visual stimuli.

Full text is incomplete: the provided content only shows an error message that the site couldn’t load and does not contain introduction, methods, results, or discussion. Therefore I cannot verify whether this is a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity study with visual stimuli (I3), whether it includes a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4), or whether it reports qualifying whole-brain or small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (I5/I6). No inclusion criteria can be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be positively identified from the available metadata alone. Because core article content is missing, the study is excluded from the review at this stage pending retrieval of the full text.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study that uses visual food stimuli (natural reward cues) and reports within-participant contrasts (food > low-level baseline and food > non-food). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics, meeting the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected voxelwise results. The manuscript provides participant demographics (adult women), cue types (food, non-food, body images), MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing/statistics software (XBAM). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

The study used visual appetitive food cues (appetizing food images) and computed a within-participant contrast (appetizing food pictures > glasses of water), and reports participant demographics and MRI details. However, the paper does not report a group-level voxelwise task-evoked result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) for the visual cue contrast that would provide coordinates or statistical maps usable for coordinate-based meta-analysis. The Results state no significant between-group differences for the picture contrast but do not provide voxelwise coordinates or SVC/whole-brain statistical results for the appetizing>water contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise result reported for the visual cue contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) from the list are explicitly met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It uses a within-participant contrast of food > nonfood, reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected) and also reports ROI analyses (nucleus accumbens). Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager, SPSS), participant sex/age ranges, and cue types. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant contrast, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a visual monetary reward anticipation task (visual cues indicating monetary incentive) and reports a within-participant contrast of monetary incentive > control (reward anticipation vs control). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (whole-brain activations described) and small-volume-corrected ROI voxelwise results in bilateral ventral striatum are presented (FWE-corrected). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains within-participant cue>control contrast, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for fMRI studies of natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (photo pairs of high- and low-calorie foods and objects). The study reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > object, low-calorie > object, food > object) and performs group-level voxelwise random-effects GLM analyses with cluster-based multiple-comparison correction (family-wise p < .05) and reports coordinates/cluster results. Results are presented for pre- and postmeal states, and voxelwise group comparisons are reported. Therefore the paper satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and qualifying group-level voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without cue>control, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of a natural reward (erotic images) with explicit visual cues (X, O, ?). It reports within-participant contrasts for cues (X>O, ?>O) and for outcomes (erotic>neutral), and conducts group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses with FWE cluster correction and reported peak coordinates. Scanner field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software (SPM8), participant demographics (N, age, sex), and cue details are reported. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pleasant images) and visual task cues (potential-win vs non-potential-win cues). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (potential win > non-potential win; wins > non-wins) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise mixed-effects analyses (FSL, cluster-based thresholding), with results reported across anticipation and outcome phases. MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing/software (FSL), participant ages, and task/cue details are provided. Although sex distribution is not clearly enumerated in the excerpt, missing a single demographic detail does not preclude inclusion per I7. Therefore the study meets I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual food images (high- and low-calorie) as natural reward cues and non-food control images, with within-participant contrasts (e.g., high-calorie > non-food; high > low). Results are reported as whole-brain cluster-corrected voxelwise statistical maps with Talairach coordinates and cluster thresholds (group-level task-evoked voxelwise results). Methods describe MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager). The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts.
