Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-based natural reward fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food>non-food (participants imagined eating the food). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (cluster-based XBAM analysis with FDR correction) and coordinates/figures are reported. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in humans. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing food conditions to neutral control stimuli (e.g., palatable foods – neutral focus > neutral stimuli – neutral focus) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with cluster-level FWE correction (and whole-brain searchlight MVPA). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CoSMo MVPA) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only results, connectivity/resting-state only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI visual natural reward cue-reactivity and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual images of food vs nonfood (visual cue component). First-level within-participant contrasts were computed (food vs nonfood; HEPF vs LEUF) and submitted to group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported with MNI coordinates, cluster thresholds, and Monte Carlo multiple-comparison correction (i.e., qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results). Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, 1.5T MRI field strength, preprocessing with SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without cue>control, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol and neutral images (ACR task). It includes a within-participant contrast (alcohol > neutral) with reported group-level voxelwise activations (mOFC, bilateral occipital cortex, PCC) and whole-brain statistical thresholds (voxel p<0.001, cluster p<0.05 FWE). The methods report imaging field strength (3T), participant age/sex, cue type, and preprocessing/statistical approaches. Voxelwise results are described in text and figures/tables. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity and provides qualifying whole-brain task-evoked results.

This is an fMRI study using visual-only video cues (segments of the Internet video game) and neutral control stimuli, with within-subject contrasts of game cues > neutral. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported as whole-brain clusters with Talairach coordinates and FDR correction (cluster-wise thresholding), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain/small-volume-corrected statistical results. Key methodological details are reported (participant age/sex, MRI field strength 3.0T, preprocessing/statistical software Brain Voyager). The paradigm assesses natural reward–related cue-reactivity (video game cues) and thus matches the meta-analysis objective. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (sugared drinks) that employs clear visual cues (colored lights and images of Coke/Pepsi cans) to manipulate expectations. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing branded visual cues versus control visual cues (e.g., Coke-can image cue > light cue) and presents group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (SPM2 random-effects whole-brain analyses with coordinates, cluster thresholds, and p-values). Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Cannot confirm critical inclusion criteria: I3 (no clear description in provided text that the task used a visual cue component), I4 (no explicit within-participant cue>control contrast reported in the abstract), and I5 (abstract mentions group analyses and activation foci but does not confirm a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected statistical result with coordinates). Although the study examines monetary reward/punishment (a type of reward) in an fMRI task, the available content is insufficient to verify the required task design and voxelwise reporting needed for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on the available information. Requesting the full methods/results (including task cue modality, contrasts, and voxelwise/statistical reporting) could allow reassessment.

This is an fMRI study using visual monetary cues (pink cross/green circle predicting 75¢ vs 0¢) and reports within-participant contrasts of Cue Money > No-money (Cue Money – No-money) and Receive Money – No-money. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (with multiple-comparison correction) and ROI small-volume-corrected voxelwise results, i.e., group-level task-evoked voxelwise statistical findings. Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), cue type, preprocessing, and statistical approach. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes clear visual stimuli (visual HED vs LED food cues) and multimodal (visual + auditory) design. The study reports within-participant contrasts HED > LED (visual and auditory) and conducts whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with cluster-extent correction, reporting peak coordinates and statistical findings. Methods (participants, imaging parameters, preprocessing, statistical models) and results are fully described in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains qualifying within-subject cue>control contrasts). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol advertisements as cues in a cue-reactivity paradigm in college students. It reports within-participant contrasts (ALCOHOL > CONTROL) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with cluster correction and peak MNI coordinates (Table 1 and whole-brain maps). Methods detail participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8), and statistical correction procedures. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I3–I7). No exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not solely between-group contrasts, and the paper is empirical). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes (fulltext_incomplete = false).

This study used fMRI with erotic visual stimuli (natural reward) but did not include a within-participant cue>control contrast (I4 not met) nor report a task-evoked voxelwise activation contrast (I5 not met). Instead, analyses are based on ICA-derived functional connectivity and between-group comparisons of network Z-maps (connectivity), which corresponds to exclusion criteria E4 (connectivity/ICA-only without qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results) and E5 (only between-group contrasts without within-participant cue>control contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cue; erotic video) and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts (food > nonfood; high-calorie > low-calorie) and interaction effects pre/post DMPA. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (Z>2.3, cluster-corrected p<.05), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise results. Relevant details (participant sex/age range, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software FSL) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This study investigates neural responses to food images (natural reward visual cues) and includes a within-participant food>object contrast; however, the Food Picture task results reported here were tested using ROI analyses (an ROI analysis on Food Picture task) rather than a group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result for the visual cue contrast. The gustatory (tastant) task includes whole-brain analyses but does not qualify as a visual cue-reactivity analysis. Therefore the paper fails Inclusion Criterion I5 and meets Exclusion Criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues present), I4 (within-participant food vs object contrast performed), I7 (participant and methods details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC result reported for the visual cue contrast). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards). It reports within-participant contrasts of HCF>NF and LCF>NF, and presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain results with FWE correction (AFNI AlphaSim), satisfying voxelwise reporting requirements. Participant demographics (age/sex), cue types, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BioImageSuite, AFNI) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual food pictures and non-food control images. The design includes within-participant task-evoked contrasts: food-picture responses were modeled at the first level (food blocks relative to implicit baseline) and differential contrasts (post-load minus basal) were entered into group-level analyses, providing within-subject cue-evoked effects. Group-level voxelwise results from whole-brain analyses (four-way repeated-measures ANOVA) and multiple-regression analyses (with multiple-comparison correction reported) are presented with peak coordinates in tables/figures. The paper reports participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM8). Full-text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates visual (and auditory) food cue reactivity (natural reward) and includes within-participant contrasts of food stimuli vs baseline/non-food stimuli, so it meets I3 and I4. It also reports participant sex, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistics details, meeting I7. However, the paper does not report a group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical result (random-effects whole-brain or small-volume-corrected group analysis); the authors explicitly state a random-effects group analysis has not yet been completed and results are based on individual-subject voxelwise analyses conserved across subjects. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I5 is missing, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and directly compares food>control contrasts within participants. It includes within-subject contrasts (e.g., Food > Places & Clocks; Food > All Other Objects) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses corrected for multiple comparisons (TFCE permutation testing in FSL randomize). Results and peaks are reported across figures/tables and participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL) are described. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports task-evoked, group-level voxelwise results. The paper includes within-participant contrasts comparing cue-associated (Go) versus control (NoGo) items during probe/training, and reports vmPFC and striatal activations with correction within a predefined medial PFC mask (small-volume-corrected) and whole-brain cluster correction for other analyses. Methods report MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for natural reward visual cue-reactivity, within-participant cue>control contrasts, and qualifying voxelwise results.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes a within-subject first-level contrast of food stimuli > neutral stimuli that was entered into a group-level (second-level) voxelwise full-factorial analysis. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (thresholded at uncorrected P<0.001, k>5) with stereotactic coordinates provided. Participant demographics (female, age 20–30), cue type (individualized food images), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Magnetom), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual erotic film clips (natural reward-related visual cues). The authors report within-participant E (erotic) > N (neutral/relaxing/sports) contrasts and implemented a random-effects, group-level voxelwise analysis using SPM99. Results are reported as loci of significant activation (tables/figures with coordinates) with both ROI-based thresholds and whole-brain corrected thresholds described. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI task-evoked voxelwise cue-reactivity to visual natural rewards and should be included.

This is an fMRI study using visual smoking cues (BEGIN/END stimuli) with within-subject contrasts (smoking minus matched control pictures). Group-level voxelwise second-level analyses were performed using anatomical ROI masks with FWE-corrected voxel-level inference (small-volume/ROI-corrected results reported). Participant characteristics, MRI parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported; the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visually presented food-word stimuli. It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts (food vs. non-food; high-ED vs. low-ED) at the first level and group-level second-level voxelwise analyses (Bayesian posterior inference) reported with cluster coordinates and regions. The methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8), participant ages/sex distribution, and cue type (visual words). Results include whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked findings and coordinate reporting. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is original human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures). The study includes within-participant contrasts (unhealthy foods > healthy foods and vice versa). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses were performed and reported with whole-brain cluster correction (Monte Carlo/3dClustSim) and results described in the main text (with ROI analyses also reported). The manuscript provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software details. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual monetary cues (images of coins) and within-subjects contrasts comparing high-value vs low-value cues (Euro > Cent). Group-level voxelwise analyses were reported with whole-brain cluster-level inference (FWE-corrected) and results are presented in figures/tables. Participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Exclusion based on connectivity/ROI-only reporting. This study meets inclusion I3 (natural reward—monetary incentive task with visual cues) and I4 (within-subject reward>neutral contrasts). However, it does not report a group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation contrast (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) qualifying for meta-analysis of cue-evoked activations: task activation results are reported as ROI-extracted NAcc values, while the principal voxelwise results are seed-based PPI connectivity maps. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E4 (reports primarily seed-based connectivity/PPI without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and E3 (task activation reported only via ROI extractions with no qualifying voxelwise activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked result). Full text appears complete. Given E3 and E4, the study must be excluded from the activation-based cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

Full text is a human fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (clusters/coordinates) and resting-state/seed analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural reward cues: food images), I5 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I6 (voxelwise results reported in main text/figures), I7 (participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistics reported). However, the study does not include a within-participant contrast of cue>control (e.g., food images > neutral/non-food control) required by I4: instead contrasts compare approach vs. avoidance responses to food (push vs. pull) and pre/post training effects. The authors explicitly note they did not include neutral non-food images. Because I4 is not satisfied, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met.

Exclusion E3 met: the study’s analyses are confined to predefined ROIs and multivariate searchlight/ensemble classifiers within those ROIs rather than reporting a qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked result. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (visual natural-reward cues—food pictures) and I4 (within-participant food>neutral contrasts / GLM contrast maps). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported as whole-brain or small-volume-corrected). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the study is excluded under E3.

This fMRI study uses visual erotic (sexual) cues (I3: visual natural-reward cues — erotic IAPS images) and reports within-participant cue contrasts (erotic > emotional and erotic > neutral) used in first-level models (I4). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates and cluster statistics (p<.005 uncorrected, k≥10), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise task-evoked result (I5); results are reported in tables/coordinates and described in the main text (I6). Participant characteristics, cue type, scanner field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported (I7). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward (food) cue-reactivity in humans using food pictures (high- and low-calorie) vs neutral control stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts (high-calorie > neutral, low-calorie > neutral, utensil > neutral) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses using SPM2. Results include whole-brain thresholding and cluster-level FDR correction and also report small-volume correction for a priori ROIs; coordinates and regional activations/deactivations are described. Participant sex, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Monetary Incentive Delay task (visual cue-based) to probe reward cue-reactivity (anticipation and outcome of monetary gains/losses). It includes within-participant contrasts of reward cue > no-reward control (anticipation of gain vs no gain; outcome hit gain vs failed gain; avoided loss vs loss). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (SPM12, whole-brain FWE cluster correction), with results presented in tables/figures. Participant demographics, task details, MRI acquisition, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Monetary cues constitute natural reward-related cues for the purposes of a reward cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Caveat: monetary (financial) cues are treated as natural reward-related in this inclusion; confidence 0.85 due to possible scope interpretation of ‘natural reward’ across reviewers.

The study assesses visual cue reactivity (alcohol, appetitive, neutral images) and reports within-participant cue>neutral contrasts and participant/method details (meets I3, I4, I7). However, for the cue-reactivity analyses the paper reports ROI-extracted NAcc percent-signal-change and regressions rather than providing a group-level voxelwise task-evoked cue>control result (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) for the cue contrasts. The only explicit voxelwise, corrected group-level result reported in the text is for the rejection>acceptance contrast (rVLPFC), not for drug/natural reward cue>neutral contrasts. Thus the paper effectively provides only ROI-based cue-reactivity results and lacks the required qualifying voxelwise cue>control result, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of a natural reward (food) using visual cues (food images). It employs a within-subject design with explicit contrasts comparing food versus nonfood control stimuli and reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results with stereotactic coordinates and small-volume FWE-corrected (SVC) p-values in ROIs (amygdala, hypothalamus, vmPFC). Results and coordinates are presented in the main text/tables/figures. Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study directly examines fMRI responses to visual natural reward cues (food images) in human participants, matching the review objective. It reports within-participant task-evoked activation maps for food-image blocks (combined low/high-calorie food blocks as the ‘activation to food’), uses those subject-level contrasts in voxelwise multiple regression and group-level comparisons, and reports whole-brain cluster results with FWE correction. Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, 3T scanner, preprocessing in SPM8), and results include voxelwise group-level statistical findings (clusters/coordinates). Therefore I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (palatable food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) with within-participant contrasts (appetizing > unappetizing; appetizing > water). Group-level voxelwise analyses were reported with small-volume correction (peaks significant at p<0.05 FDR within a priori spheres), with coordinates given. Methods report participant age/sex (adolescent females), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images. The study reports within-participant contrasts of food>non-food (food versus non-food images) at the group level, with voxelwise whole-brain analyses and voxel- and cluster-wise FDR correction, and provides peak coordinates and figures. Methods report participant age/sex (female), cue type (food images), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (XBAM). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cues with visual stimuli and within-participant contrasts (High ED vs Low ED; High ED vs Scrambled), so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met. However, the paper reports an ROI-based analysis (5 mm spheres around a priori coordinates) and presents correlations and ANOVAs on extracted ROI values; there is no report of group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain or small-volume-corrected) in the main text or supplementary material. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no qualifying voxelwise/whole-brain or SVC result) and fails to meet I5. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visual cue-reactivity using e-cigarette advertising images (visual stimuli) presented to adolescents. It includes within-participant contrasts of e-cigarette cues > matched neutral control images and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-corrected using AFNI 3dClustSim; results presented in tables and figures). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for visual cue fMRI studies and provides qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food), using within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood and high-calorie food > nonfood). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported with small-volume correction within predefined ROIs (insula, striatum, amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex) using SPM8 on a 3.0T scanner; results are presented in figures and supplementary tables. Participant age, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes within-participant contrasts (high-energy > low-energy food cues) and reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (RFX-GLM) with voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction, and reported cluster statistics/regions. The methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and analysis software (BrainVoyager), participant age/sex, and cue types. Full article text (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of high- and low-calorie foods and neutral non-foods). It includes within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food > non-food, and reports whole-brain voxel-wise group-level analyses (FWE- and FDR-corrected voxel-wise results) with MNI coordinates. Methods report MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8 and processing scripts), and participant age/sex/cue details. Results include voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate tables. Therefore the paper meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli in overweight/obese participants. It includes within-participant contrasts of food images > non-food images and high-calorie > low-calorie images. The study reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain voxelwise analyses and masked voxelwise analyses within ROIs / small-volume approaches), along with ROI analyses. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (high/low calorie food images, non-food), MRI field strength (3 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported. Although many drug-related contrasts yielded null findings, the presence of group-level voxelwise results satisfies the requirement for inclusion. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of appetitive (reward) cue-reactivity using visual CSs (colored rectangles) paired with monetary reward (secondary/natural reward). It reports within-subject contrasts CS+ > CS− during acquisition and extinction, and group-level voxelwise results using whole-brain FWE correction and ROI small-volume corrections (Harvard-Oxford masks; SPM8). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics software (SPM8) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-participant cue>control contrasts; empirical task-evoked voxelwise results are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). First-level within-participant contrasts of high-calorie food > neutral/control were computed. Group-level voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise LME) were reported with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values for significant voxels (DLPFC, MTL, VLPFC), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise results. Necessary methodological details are provided (participant sex counts, age covariate, cue type, MRI field strengths 1.5T and 3T, preprocessing with SPM12), and coordinate results are reported in the text/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (greyscale landscape photographs) to probe anticipation of monetary reward and punishment. It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts of reward-predicting > neutral cues and punishment-predicting > neutral cues at the group level, with SPM5 preprocessing and statistical analysis. Results report small-volume-corrected (SVC) voxelwise activations (FWE-corrected spherical search volumes) in a priori regions and report coordinates/activations in the main text/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity to natural (monetary) rewards with visual stimuli and provides qualifying voxelwise task-evoked results.

Full text is not available (page shows a redirect/‘checking your browser’ message); only title/metadata provided. Cannot verify key inclusion criteria: I3 (whether the study is an fMRI task assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a clear visual cue component), I4 (presence of a within-participant cue>control contrast), or I5 (reporting of at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result). I6 and I7 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be determined from the available information. Therefore exclude due to incomplete/full-text unavailability and inability to confirm required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes clear visual cues (pictures of chocolate and moldy strawberries) within a multimodal design. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., chocolate picture/taste > control gray image/tasteless rinse) and group-level voxelwise statistical analyses with whole-brain family-wise error correction; coordinates and SPM results are reported. Methods (1.5T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing, participant characteristics) and results are fully described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts (high-calorie foods > neutral control and other cue>control contrasts). Group-level voxelwise statistical results are reported (whole-brain analyses with thresholds and cluster-level corrections, and small-volume correction in a priori ROIs), with coordinates and statistics provided. MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2), participant sex, and cue type are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual food images and includes within-subject contrasts (Food > Non-food; Food > baseline) across pre- and post-meal states. Group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with corrected whole-brain thresholds and Talairach coordinates, meeting the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked results. Methods report participant ages/sex, 3T field strength, stimulus details, preprocessing, and statistical software (BrainVoyager). The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-participant contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Study is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual food images (natural rewards) with healthy controls and clinical groups. It reports within-participant contrasts (Food > Non-food) computed per subject and group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample and two-sample t-tests, ANCOVA) with whole-brain reporting of activated clusters. MRI field strength (1.5T), participant demographics (women, age 20–35), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software (AFNI) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review of visual cue-reactivity and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of visual food cue reactivity (natural rewards) using pictorial stimuli (I3). The analysis includes a within-participant contrast Food > Non-Food at first level and subsequent group-level random-effects analyses (I4). Group-level voxelwise results were reported with small-volume familywise error correction within the fusiform gyrus (I5), with coordinates, p-values and figures referenced (I6). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8) are reported (I7). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-participant contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria, and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using clearly visual brand cues (logos/bottle images) preceding taste (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing cue types (strong vs. weak brands; Coca vs. Pepsi), i.e., cue-related contrasts (I4). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported (SPM random-effects analyses, thresholded maps, cluster coordinates in MNI space; whole-brain reporting) satisfying the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain results (I5,I6). Participant demographics, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts, empirical task-evoked fMRI). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (food pictures) as natural reward stimuli. The study reports within-subject contrasts of food>scenery (food minus scenery) and presents group-level voxelwise t-maps with coordinates and multiple-comparisons-corrected peaks (whole-brain results). Scanner field strength, participant age/sex, cue types, preprocessing, and statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-fMRI study using visual erotic pictures (natural reward cues) presented in blocks versus scenic pictures, yielding within-participant erotic>scenic contrasts. Group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8) and thresholded maps/peak coordinates (AlphaSim-corrected) are reported. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/software details are provided. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for visual cue-reactivity, within-subject cue>control contrasts, and group-level voxelwise task-evoked results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, or lack of within-subject contrasts) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food images (natural reward) and includes a within-subject High>Low calorie contrast. Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and a significant cluster (left gyrus rectus, MNI coordinates provided) was reported after small-volume correction (FDR) within the vmPFC; results and coordinates are described in the text. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for visual natural-reward cue-reactivity with at least one qualifying group-level small-volume-corrected voxelwise result and provides required methodological details.

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of anticipation of monetary and verbal rewards using clear visual cues (distinct CS arrows). It includes within-participant voxelwise group-level contrasts comparing reward-predicting cues to control cues (mCS+ > CS−, vCS+ > CS−, mCS+ > vCS+) analyzed with second-level random-effects and reports whole-brain multiple-comparison correction (Gaussian random field theory, P < 0.05 corrected). Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual cues that reliably predict tastes (visual stimuli signaling glucose, salt, neutral). It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts (e.g., ANTglc > ANTslt, ANTglc > ANTneu, ANTglc > TSTglc) at group level, with coordinates and small-volume-corrected results (SVC) and some whole-brain corrected findings. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (2T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99) are reported. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical BOLD-fMRI study using visual erotic (natural reward) stimuli (video sexual stimulation) and a pharmacological manipulation (apomorphine). Methods describe within-participant contrasts of erotic versus neutral films and randomized placebo/drug sessions (i.e., within-participant cue>control contrasts). Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM-99 with reported cluster-level statistics (p<0.001) and described whole-brain activation patterns (including voxel cluster extents and regional activations), meeting the requirement for whole-brain or small-volume-corrected task-evoked results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Participant age, MRI field strength (1.5T), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI visual cue-reactivity and provides qualifying voxelwise results.

This study uses an fMRI monetary guessing/reward task rather than a cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural reward cues. It does not include a within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control. It does, however, report voxelwise group-level task-evoked results within ROIs with coordinate tables and participant details. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue-based drug/natural cue-reactivity) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual and couple-bonding images (natural reward cues) with a within-participant task design (sexual/bonding vs neutral/other images). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were conducted (mixed-effects FLAME-1, Z=2.3 cluster-corrected) and reported whole-brain activation results and ROI analyses; results are described in the main text and refer to figures/tables. Participant details, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (FSL) and statistical methods are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study directly examines neural responses to visual natural reward-related cues (sexually provocative images) using a within-subject contrast [Sexual–Non-sexual]. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholds and supplementary tables with coordinates are provided) and also reports ROI analyses. Core methodological details are present (participant ages/sex, cue types, MRI field strength = 3T, preprocessing/statistical software BrainVoyager QX). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary tables referenced).

This fMRI study used visual erotic (natural reward) and negative images and performed within-participant voxelwise F-tests per subject, meeting I3 (visual natural reward cues) and I4 (within-participant tests of cue responses). The paper reports voxelwise single-subject results (figures/masks) and details participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/software, satisfying I6 and I7. However, it does not present a group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical analysis or any small-volume-corrected group analysis required by I5; the analyses and results are presented at the single-subject level (n=5) and emphasize single-subject inference. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because I5 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity (food images) with clear visual cues and within-participant contrasts (fattening>nonfattening and fattening>object) so it meets I3 and I4. Participant/sample and imaging details are reported (age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner, preprocessing/software), meeting I7. However, the paper’s imaging results are reported primarily as ROI-based analyses; the only group-level voxelwise contrast mentioned was used to functionally define ROIs at an uncorrected threshold (P<0.05), and the manuscript does not report any whole-brain corrected or small-volume-corrected group-level voxelwise task-evoked results or coordinate tables that would qualify under I5/I6. Therefore the study fails to meet I5 and should be excluded under E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain or SVC voxelwise result). Inclusion IDs met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (qualifying group-level voxelwise whole-brain or SVC-corrected result). Exclusion IDs met: E3.

This is an fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (photographs) as natural reward cues, with within-subject contrasts comparing sexually arousing versus neutral control images (e.g., W SN > W D) and a subtractive contrast controlling for clothing factor. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed (fixed-effects group analysis, SPM99) with reported coordinates and corrected thresholds (P<0.05 corrected), satisfying whole-brain/small-volume reporting. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (romantic and sexual images) and meets all inclusion criteria. I3: The task assesses natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (romantic and sexual pictures). I4: Within-participant contrasts are reported (sexual > neutral, romantic > neutral, romantic > sexual). I5: Group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results are reported using whole-brain random-effects analyses (FLAME 1 & 2) with cluster correction (Z=2.3, p<.01; cluster-wise p<.01). I6: Voxelwise results are reported in figures and tables. I7: Key methodological and participant details are reported (participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength = 3.0T, preprocessing/statistical software = FSL, smoothing, motion correction). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to natural rewards with visual stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual food stimuli (natural rewards) and reports task-evoked, group-level voxelwise analyses. The experiment included visual food pictures and emotional pictures, participants rated valence, and the GLM produced category-specific contrasts analyzed at the group level (whole-brain group comparisons with cluster-level correction and ROI-restriction). Results are reported as clusters/activation maps and discussed with coordinates and figures. The manuscript reports participant age/sex, cue type (high- and low-calorie food images), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (BrainVoyager QX). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-participant cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of smokers using pictorial (visual) smoking cues with a within-participant contrast of smoking vs neutral pictures (LCSP minus LCNP). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 and reported small-volume FWE-corrected results in a priori ROIs (ACC, DLPFC, SPL, etc.), with results presented in text/figures/tables. Participant demographics, cue type, 3T field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. All required inclusion criteria (I3–I7) are met, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided and sufficiently complete for screening.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of natural (social) and monetary reward cue-reactivity using clear visual cues (smiling faces, coin images). The within-subject contrasts compare reward cues>neutral control and social vs monetary cues, with group-level voxelwise results reported (peak coordinates, tables) and small-volume FWE-corrected ROI results (striatum, DMN, amygdala, FFA). Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistics (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (SVC reported), not connectivity-only, and include within-participant cue>control contrasts. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using gustatory (taste) alcohol cues (alcohol taste vs. litchi juice) with within-subject alcohol>control contrasts and voxelwise ROI results reported as coordinates/peak z-scores. It therefore meets I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported, within anatomically defined ROIs / small-volume search), I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables), and I7 (reports cue type, MRI field strength = 3T, and preprocessing/statistical software). However, it does NOT meet I3 because the primary cues are gustatory taste stimuli rather than visual cues; the meta-analysis objective requires a clear visual cue component (visual-only or multimodal that include visual cues). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded on the basis that it lacks the required visual cue component (I3 not met).

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual food cues (natural rewards) in adolescents. It reports within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood and sweets>nonsweet (i.e., cue>control contrasts), and performs group-level voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses with whole-brain voxelwise inference using FDR correction. The manuscript provides participant age/sex, cue types, 3.0T MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study of visual food cues (high- vs. low-calorie pictures and nonfood objects) directly addresses natural reward cue-reactivity. It includes within-participant voxelwise contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie; high-calorie > nonfood) and reports group-level small-volume-corrected voxelwise results (NAcc and DLPFC masks) using nonparametric cluster correction (FSL randomise). Full methodological details (participants’ age/sex, cue type, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing and analysis software: FSL/FEAT, ICA-AROMA) are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; task-evoked voxelwise results present; not connectivity-only; within-participant contrasts reported; empirical human fMRI data). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a monetary incentive delay (MID) task with visual anticipation cues for reward and loss, meeting the review focus on natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues. The authors report within-participant contrasts (reward anticipation > neutral; loss anticipation > neutral). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are provided both whole-brain (task effects under placebo) and via small-volume-corrected ROI analyses (striatum, insula, ACC) with pFWE values. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7).

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (images of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages) collected at 3T with preprocessing in FSL and full methodological details reported. The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (respond alcohol > fixation and respond neutral > fixation) that are cluster-corrected (z>2.3, p=0.05 whole-brain), satisfying the requirement for a qualifying voxelwise result. Although a direct alcohol>neutral contrast was not performed, the within-participant respond alcohol > rest contrast constitutes a task-evoked cue versus control contrast acceptable under the review’s criteria. Participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli and provides group-level voxelwise results suitable for meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual (natural reward) video clips and reporting within-subject contrasts and correlational voxelwise analyses. The paper uses SPM99 group-level voxelwise analyses (reported with corrected thresholds), reports participant characteristics (male, age range), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Subtractive contrasts between sexual and neutral/humor conditions are reported and whole-brain voxelwise results (p<0.05 corrected) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity and provides qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked results.

This study is an fMRI task study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with a within-participant contrast (highly desirable > less desirable food images). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise regressions relating hormone levels to task-evoked activations are reported (stringent voxelwise thresholds, FWE-corrected). The manuscript includes participants’ age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). The full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual reward-related cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This fMRI study used visual cues (photographs of the rejecting beloved vs a familiar neutral face) and reports within-participant rejecter>neutral contrasts at the group level. Voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2, with planned ROI small-volume-corrected results (FDR correction) reported as coordinates and cluster tables; figures and coordinate tables present the activations. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Thus it satisfies: I3 (visual cue component), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level voxelwise results with small-volume correction), I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables/figures), and I7 (participant/MRI/method details). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes qualifying voxelwise SVC results). Full text appears complete.

Full text provided is incomplete (HTML shell only) and does not contain methods/results. Title/metadata indicate an fMRI study of personality/emotion (Gray's theory) rather than drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criteria requiring (I3) assessment of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with visual cues, (I4) a within-participant cue>control contrast, or (I5) at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected result. I6 and I7 cannot be confirmed from the available content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on available information. Full text incomplete: true.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (erotic images) and neutral fractal controls. It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts (e.g., erotic-predictive CS vs fractal-predictive CS; omitted erotic vs omitted fractal) and related BOLD prediction-error analyses. Group-level voxelwise results are reported with MNI coordinates and corrected inference: a whole-brain between-subjects analysis (FWE-corrected) identified left ventral striatum; additional analyses used anatomically defined small-volume inference in ventral striatum. The paper provides participant age/sex (male, ages reported), cue type (erotic vs fractal), MRI field strength (3T Philips Achieva), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study used a Monetary Incentive Delay task with visual reward cues (satisfies I3) and included within-participant contrasts of reward cue/no-incentive (satisfies I4). However, task-evoked voxelwise whole-brain or small-volume-corrected activation results for cue>control contrasts are not reported in the main text: activation analyses were performed and reported as ROI-based beta extractions. The only whole-brain voxelwise results reported pertain to PPI (seed-based connectivity) in response to outcomes, not voxelwise cue-reactivity contrasts. Therefore the paper does not provide a qualifying group-level voxelwise task-evoked cue>control result (I5 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only task activations with no qualifying voxelwise result). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-evoked fMRI study using visual cues (colored squares) predicting monetary reward (a reward-related stimulus). The study includes within-participant contrasts comparing reward-predictive cues (CS+) versus control cues (CS−) across task phases, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with per-voxel thresholds, cluster-size correction, and peak coordinates, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), cue type, and preprocessing/statistical software. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes appropriate within-subject cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (high- vs. low-calorie food images). The paper reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts of high-calorie > low-calorie food images and group-level whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected p<0.05 across gray-matter mask; thresholds and coordinates reported). Methods specify MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM12/DARTEL), cue type, and participant demographics. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (grayscale pictures of objects/animals) that manipulated reward anticipation (monetary reward) and compared reward-predicting versus neutral cues within participants. The manuscript reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (reward-predicting cue > neutral cue; subsequent memory DM contrasts) with whole-brain thresholds and stereotaxic coordinates, and describes localization procedures (including small-volume consideration of midbrain). Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (food images) using visual stimuli, with within-participant task contrasts (food>rest and non-food>rest) and group-level voxelwise analyses. The authors conducted one-sample t-tests on contrast images and report significant ROI clusters with MNI coordinates and z-scores (small-volume correction applied to a priori ROIs), and also provide whole-brain results in the supplement. Participant demographics, cue type, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, MarsBar) are reported. Therefore it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria for task-evoked voxelwise results and visual natural reward cues. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply.

This study uses an fMRI reward-based spatial learning task with a virtual radial maze and monetary rewards, not a cue-reactivity paradigm presenting drug or natural reward-related visual cues. It therefore does not meet I3 (assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity with a visual cue component) nor I4 (having a within-participant contrast of drug-cues>control or natural-reward-related-cues>control). The paper does report group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain and small-volume-corrected) and provides coordinates and participant details, satisfying I5, I6, and I7, but failure to meet I3 and I4 prevents inclusion. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward cue-reactivity using visual food images (food vs non-food). It reports within-participant voxelwise contrasts (Food > Non-food), with group-level small-volume-corrected ROI results (FWE-corrected SVC results for pgACC and insula) and exploratory whole-brain cluster analyses. Methods report participant demographics (female, age 19–60), MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7, and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Results are reported at the group voxelwise level suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual reward cue-reactivity.

The study is an fMRI experiment of a simulated reach-to-eat motor task using food images, focused on spatiotemporal sensorimotor dynamics rather than cue-reactivity to rewards. It does not perform or report within-participant contrasts of drug cues > control or natural reward-related cues > control required for this meta-analysis. It therefore fails to meet inclusion criteria I3 (study assessing drug or natural reward cue-reactivity with visual cues) and I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast). I5 (a qualifying group-level voxelwise cue-reactivity result) is also not satisfied for the purposes of this review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met. Full text appears complete. Consequently EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of a natural reward (food) using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of food>mosaic (control) at the group level with voxelwise random-effects analyses (whole-brain cluster-corrected thresholds and small-volume correction for the amygdala). Results (tables/figures and descriptions) present qualifying voxelwise task-evoked statistical findings. Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, 3T MRI field strength, and SPM12 preprocessing/statistics. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (food pictures) and reports within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood. Group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed (random-effects), with whole-brain FDR-corrected results reported for several regions and a priori ROI thresholds described; coordinate results are indicated to be listed. Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task study using visual cues (monetary symbols and humorous images) comparing reward cues vs no-reward controls and reporting within-participant contrasts (e.g., MA>NA, HA>NA, MA>HA, HO>MO). Group-level voxelwise task-evoked results are reported with small-volume corrections and FWE peak-level thresholds; coordinates and tables/figures of activations are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (visual cue component/natural reward-related cues), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (group-level voxelwise results with SVC/FWE), and I6 (coordinates/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only connectivity, includes within-subject contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

Full text is a complete empirical fMRI study of monetary reward processing in adolescents, but it does not meet the review’s cue-reactivity requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported with ROI small-volume correction), I6 (voxelwise results are reported in the main text/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using explicit visual cue paradigms; it uses a monetary guessing task rather than cue-reactivity to reward-related visual stimuli), and I4 (no within-participant contrast of reward-cue > control-stimulus is reported; contrasts are reward anticipation/outcome > baseline). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails to satisfy I3 and I4. fulltext_incomplete=false

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (female body images), which qualify as natural reward cues. Inclusion criteria met: I3 — clear visual natural reward cues (images of female bodies); I4 — within-participant contrasts comparing more-rewarding versus less-rewarding cues (post-surgical > pre-surgical bodies) and parametric regressions of attractiveness (post-minus pre) on brain activation; I5 — group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical results reported (whole-brain cluster-corrected maps and voxelwise Z-scores; ROI small-volume analyses of OFC also reported); I6 — voxelwise results presented in figures/text; I7 — participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and analysis software (FEAT-FSL) reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-subject cue>control contrasts, and this is original human fMRI data. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This fMRI study uses visual natural-reward (food) cues and reports within-participant contrasts comparing high-calorie versus low-calorie food conditions (i.e., natural-reward cues > control stimuli). Group-level voxelwise random-effects fMRI results are reported with cluster-forming threshold and FWE cluster correction (whole-brain voxelwise results). Task design, participant demographics, cue types, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM/DCM versions) are described (with additional acquisition/preprocessing details in supplements). Although the paper also reports DCM effective connectivity, it additionally provides qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content.

This study used erotic images as behavioral distractors but did not perform task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity analyses. Resting-state fMRI (dFNC) was collected on a separate day and analyses focus on intrinsic connectivity states correlated with behavioral gaze measures; no within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrasts or group-level task-evoked whole-brain/SVC results are reported. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring an fMRI cue-reactivity task contrast. Exclusion ID met: E4 (reports only resting-state analyses without qualifying task-evoked voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant age/sex and methodological details are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI task assessing cue-reactivity), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5/I6 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards). It reports within-subject contrasts of food (HC+LC) > neutral (NF) stimuli and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×3 ANOVA, with FWE correction and whole-brain contrast maps). Methods report visual stimuli, participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, BioImageSuite, AFNI). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and non-food control images. It includes within-participant contrasts comparing food vs. non-food (main effect of memory content) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with cluster- and peak-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates (e.g., posterior cingulum [9 -39 39]). Methods report MRI field strength (Philips 3T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12/MATLAB), and participant demographics (age, female sample). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-subject cue>control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (complex indoor/outdoor scene images) that signal monetary reward versus neutral outcomes (natural reward). It includes within-participant contrasts comparing reward-predicting>neutral cues during anticipation and outcome phases. Group-level voxelwise SPM results are reported (whole-brain and small-volume/ROI analyses; cluster coordinates and statistical thresholds provided). Participant demographics, cue types, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics (SPM2) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study does not report a within-participant cue>control voxelwise contrast required for cue-reactivity inclusion (I4 not met). It does meet I3 (uses clear visual conditioned cues — slot machine vs stamp image), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results, e.g., parametric probability maps and Table 2), I6 (results presented in tables/figures), and I7 (reports participant age/sex and imaging/preprocessing details). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). However, because the meta-analysis requires at least one within-subject cue>control voxelwise contrast (I4) and this is not presented in the full text, the study cannot be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual conditioned cues (colored squares) that predict monetary reward (natural reward). It includes a within-participant voxelwise contrast of CS+ versus CS− (attend trials) reflecting reward-related cue-reactivity, with group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported (activation in bilateral striatum; P<0.005; coordinates/results referenced in Fig.2a and Supplementary Table 1). The visual cue component is clear, and results are reported as voxelwise activations (supplementary materials referenced), satisfying I3, I4, I5 and I6. Participant demographics and scanner/preprocessing details are not fully shown in the provided text but their absence does not preclude inclusion (I7 preferred but not mandatory). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This fMRI study assesses natural reward cue-reactivity to visual food images and reports task-evoked voxelwise results. It used visual IAPS food stimuli, implemented within-participant contrasts (food vs. neutral at first level and paired t-tests for within-group pre/post contrasts), and performed group-level voxelwise analyses including ROI-based small-volume-corrected results (reported left putamen activation). Key methodological details are reported (participant ages/sex, 1.5T scanner, SPM5 preprocessing). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results without small-volume correction, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and includes within-subject contrasts of food images versus neutral images. The paper reports voxel-wise multiple regression analyses and exploratory voxel-wise group contrasts with cluster coordinates and regional results (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results reported), and provides key methodological details (participant demographics, 3T MRI field strength, preprocessing software AFNI, statistical approach). Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity studies (food cues>neutral) and provides qualifying group-level voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains within-participant cue>control contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (erotic IAPS images) and reports within-subject contrasts (Erotic > Neutral, Aversive > Neutral). Group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (whole-brain thresholded maps and tables of MNI coordinates; P<0.001, cluster extent), satisfying task-evoked voxelwise result requirements. Participant demographics (45 males, mean age reported), cue type, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity to visual natural rewards.

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (natural reward: food cues presented visually) and I4 (within-participant food>non-food contrasts). However, the full text reports only seed-based task-dependent functional connectivity analyses (PPI) and does not present group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., food>non-food GLM activation maps) as whole-brain or small-volume-corrected results. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only PPI/seed-based connectivity without a qualifying task-evoked voxelwise result) and cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (appetizing vs. bland food pictures) with an explicit within-participant contrast (appetizing > bland foods). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked results (whole-brain analyses and small-volume-corrected PET/SVC results), provides coordinates and statistical thresholds, and details MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.
